2ab1abcb9ca0.title: Facility Type candidate
2ab1abcb9ca0.content: Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. Also called: Facility type . 9921374655b8.title: Public Health Workforce candidate
9921374655b8.content: The public health workforce comprises all individuals who contribute to the delivery of at least one of the essential public health functions as part of integrated services and systems. This workforce comprises diverse and multidisciplinary occupations, from the health as well as other non-health sectors. This workforce can be conceptualized as three broad groupings: core group of public health personnel who have undergone professional training and/or registration with professional bodies in public health and could be from either health or another background; health and care workers who contribute to one or more public health functions as part of their clinical and/or social care roles; and personnel from a wide group of other allied occupations who contribute to addressing the determinants of health – for instance, personnel engaged in water and sanitation, food supply chains and road safety. Also called: Public health workforce . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). c5ba8c8c55b1.doc: Health Workforce Education and Training Institution
c5ba8c8c55b1.title: Health Workforce Education and Training Institution candidate
c5ba8c8c55b1.content: An established institution that provides education as its main purpose, such as a school, college, university or training centre. Such institutions are normally accredited or sanctioned by the relevant national education authorities or equivalent to award qualifications. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. In practice, for international comparability, any educational institution not managed by a government institution is classified as private. Also called: Health workforce education and training institution . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). 78f732149f60.content: Classification for ownership type: • Publicly-owned: Facilities owned or controlled by a governmental unit or a public corporation (where control is defined as the ability to determine the general corporate policy) corresponding to the institutional sector “government units” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. • Not-for-profit privately-owned: Facilities that are legal or social entities created for the purpose of producing goods and services, whose status does not permit them to be a source of income, profit, or other financial gain for the unit(s) that establish, control or finance them, corresponding to the institutional sector “non-profit institutions serving households” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. • For-profit privately-owned: Facilities that are legal entities set up for the purpose of producing goods and services and are capable of generating a profit or other financial gain for their owners corresponding to the institutional sector “non-financial corporations” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. eac3542e65c2.title: Remuneration candidate
eac3542e65c2.content: Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. It should be net of operation costs/practice expenses. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). bdd9433f0c51-3.title: Narrower
bdd9433f0c51-3.content: . | In a national context an electronic health workforce registry can be considered the single authoritative source of health workforce information that can provide an accurate count of all health care personnel that either have worked or are currently working at national or sub-national levels, including in the private sector. | An electronic health workforce registry can be designed to authenticate and validate the existence of a health worker and provide essential details about that person. | In addition, a health workforce registry can ensure quality control, provide easy access to information on production, distribution and utilization of health personnel, and assist in budgeting, research development and advocacy. | A health workforce registry allows aggregation of health workforce data in several combinations and assists both national and sub-national ministries of health in producing essential indicator-based reports, as needed. | The health workforce registry is a central and essential component of a functional HRIS, as it contains important health worker attributes that can subsequently be linked to other relevant HRIS components. | Address policy and governance mechanism | Agree on a location to operate the registry | Assure privacy, security and confidentiality of health workforce data | Establish standardized reports | Number of health workforce by cadre, gender and facility | Number of expected retirements | Number of expected and completed renewals of license/credentials | Number of vacant positions by facility | Geographic distribution of total workforce by facility | Geographic distribution (by district) of male and female employees | Develop, test, and deploy a functional electronic health workforce registry | Establish appropriate access controls based on an agreed policies. | Design, test and deploy the electronic web-enabled registry based on national eHealth enterprise architecture. | Make available, at sub-national level, a replica of the registry with similar structure and functions, in order to collect and manage the minimum data set from authorized entities at sub-national-level. | Adhere to best practices in information systems design to assure accuracy, timeliness, completeness, reliability, privacy, security, and confidentiality of data and information systems and assets. | Illustration depicting a web-enabled electronic Health Workforce Registry with person-centric data entry screen and analytics display abilities | Based on national or sub-national eHealth enterprise information architecture, national and sub-national health authorities shall develop and deploy the registry. | The registry shall conform to best practices in information systems design in order to assure quality, accuracy, timeliness, completeness, reliability, privacy, security, and confidentiality of the data and information systems and assets. | Legally authorized users of the registry shall be required to have unique user names and passwords that will be provided by the national Steering Committee, on the approval of the highest health authority at national and sub-national levels. Level of access to the registry shall be determined by the national Steering Committee or its authorized agent. | The registry must be in compliance with all applicable national and sub-national laws related to privacy, security, and confidentiality of data. | The registry and its related physical assets shall be secured in accordance with applicable national and sub-national laws. | .

37291b5b705c.title: quality of the evidence
37291b5b705c.content: In the context of guideline development, the confidence that the estimates of an effect are adequate to support a particular decision or recommendation. Rated high, moderate, low or very low. Also called: certainty of the evidence, confidence in the estimates of effect . The WHO handbook for guideline development (2nd edition, §9.1, p. 122) names both alternatives: "Alternative terms to describe the quality of the evidence are 'certainty of the evidence' or 'confidence in the estimates of effect'." The handbook uses 'quality of the evidence' 77 times and 'certainty of the evidence' once; the who-guideline-development voice and the platform's `grade-certainty` code list use 'certainty', GRADE's later name. Rated for a body of evidence per outcome, never for a single study. Not the strength of a recommendation, which the handbook keeps apart throughout.

The handbook cites its reference 69 for this entry. | Health Workforce Education and Training Programme (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))A “coherent set or sequence of educational activities or communication designed and organized to achieve pre-determined learning objectives or accomplish a specific set of educational tasks over a sustained period” with the objective to improve health knowledge, skills and competencies applied to health and enable the training of new health workers. Health workforce education and training programmes will often have a numerus clausus that restricts the number of places for a given programme. The handbook cites its reference 108 for this entry. | Health Workforce Education and Training Institution (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))An established institution that provides education as its main purpose, such as a school, college, university or training centre. Such institutions are normally accredited or sanctioned by the relevant national education authorities or equivalent to award qualifications. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. In practice, for international comparability, any educational institution not managed by a government institution is classified as private. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). Facility Type candidate Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. 5fbe13d04fa8.content: Gender candidate Gender refers to the characteristics of women, men, girls and boys that are socially constructed. This includes norms, behaviours and roles associated with being a woman, man, girl or boy, as well as relationships with each other. As a social construct, gender varies from society to society and can change over time. Gender is hierarchical and produces inequalities that intersect with other social and economic inequalities. The handbook cites its reference 48 for this entry. | Facility Type (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. NHWA indicator 4 – 05. The definition is the sheet's "Indicator name"; the label is its "Abbreviated name". Candidate definitions (7) . | International Health Regulations (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))An international legal instrument that is binding on 196 countries across the globe, including all Member States of WHO. Its aim is to help the international community prevent and respond to acute public health risks that have the potential to cross borders and threaten people worldwide. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 91; PDF page 105). The library ingest of this edition has no Glossary section, so the definition was extracted from the PDF text layer on 2026-10-31 and needs a person to confirm it. The handbook cites its reference 109 for this entry. | Subnational Level (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))To be defined according to the specific conditions, governing structures, and constitutional provisions existing in a given country. Disaggregation based on administrative boundaries down to the first or second subnational level is recommended (depending on the structure of administrative boundaries and the size of subnational territories), without overlaps between the administrative units. Examples for subnational administrative units are states, regions, provinces, counties, and districts. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 93; PDF page 107). The library ingest of this edition has no Glossary section, so the definition was extracted from the PDF text layer on 2026-10-31 and needs a person to confirm it. The handbook cites its reference 47 for this entry. | Active Health Worker (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))One who provides services to patients and communities (practising health worker) or whose medical education is a prerequisite for the execution of the job (e.g. education, research, public administration) even if the health worker is not directly providing services (professionally active health worker). If data are not available for practising or professionally active health workers, data with the closest definition can be used, such as “health worker licensed to practice”. Categories of level are based on the definitions of OECD/Eurostat/WHO-Europe Joint questionnaire on non-monetary health care statistics. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 88; PDF page 102). The library ingest of this edition has no Glossary section, so the definition was extracted from the PDF text layer on 2026-10-31 and needs a person to confirm it. The handbook cites its reference 48 for this entry. | Occupation (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))The concept of occupation is defined as a “set of jobs whose main tasks and duties are characterized by a high degree of similarity”. A job is defined as “a set of tasks and duties performed, or meant to be performed, by one person, including for an employer or in self-employment”. The National Health Workforce Accounts covers health and health-related occupations grouped according to the International Standard Classification of Occupations 2008. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). The library ingest of this edition has no Glossary section, so the definition was extracted from the PDF text layer on 2026-10-31 and needs a person to confirm it. The handbook cites its reference 46 for this entry. | Remuneration (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. It should be net of operation costs/practice expenses. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). The library ingest of this edition has no Glossary section, so the definition was extracted from the PDF text layer on 2026-10-31 and needs a person to confirm it. The handbook cites its reference 58 for this entry. | Status in Employment (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))One of two categories of the total employed: (a) wage and salaried workers (employees): workers who hold a job defined as “paid employment”, with explicit (written or oral) or implicit employment contracts that give them a basic remuneration that is not directly dependent upon the revenue of the unit for which they work, and (b) self-employed workers: workers who, working on their own account or with one or more partners or in a cooperative, hold a “self-employment job”, i.e. one in which the remuneration is directly dependent upon the profits derived from the goods and services produced. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 93; PDF page 107). The library ingest of this edition has no Glossary section, so the definition was extracted from the PDF text layer on 2026-10-31 and needs a person to confirm it. The handbook cites its reference 93 for this entry. | Gender (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))Gender refers to the characteristics of women, men, girls and boys that are socially constructed. This includes norms, behaviours and roles associated with being a woman, man, girl or boy, as well as relationships with each other. As a social construct, gender varies from society to society and can change over time. Gender is hierarchical and produces inequalities that intersect with other social and economic inequalities. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). Public Health Workforce candidate The public health workforce comprises all individuals who contribute to the delivery of at least one of the essential public health functions as part of integrated services and systems. This workforce comprises diverse and multidisciplinary occupations, from the health as well as other non-health sectors. This workforce can be conceptualized as three broad groupings: core group of public health personnel who have undergone professional training and/or registration with professional bodies in public health and could be from either health or another background; health and care workers who contribute to one or more public health functions as part of their clinical and/or social care roles; and personnel from a wide group of other allied occupations who contribute to addressing the determinants of health – for instance, personnel engaged in water and sanitation, food supply chains and road safety. 4fb2ea1ce2ce.title: Q
4fb2ea1ce2ce.content: quality of the evidence In the context of guideline development, the confidence that the estimates of an effect are adequate to support a particular decision or recommendation. Rated high, moderate, low or very low. The WHO handbook for guideline development (2nd edition, §9.1, p. 122) names both alternatives: "Alternative terms to describe the quality of the evidence are 'certainty of the evidence' or 'confidence in the estimates of effect'." The handbook uses 'quality of the evidence' 77 times and 'certainty of the evidence' once; the who-guideline-development voice and the platform's `grade-certainty` code list use 'certainty', GRADE's later name. Rated for a body of evidence per outcome, never for a single study. Not the strength of a recommendation, which the handbook keeps apart throughout. Remuneration candidate Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. It should be net of operation costs/practice expenses. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). 46f7db3deb43.content: activate-accepted-guidance candidate, extracted The point-of-care system carries out the health worker's decisions on decision-support guidance: each accepted action's request becomes active (intent plan or order) and joins the client's CarePlan; a declined action is not written. What makes a disagreement adjudicable, the shape its implementations share, why the adjudication LEADS the criterion while the checker's entry is kept beneath it, and the dispensation that records the reason — scoped to a version, never precedent. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/adjudication.md . adopt-methodology-from-source candidate, extracted The general process for turning a shared paper, book or standard into an adopted methodology: establish origin and licence, ingest the source, find and summarize related work items and issues and ask whether to coordinate, render the method with its adopted and refused parts, place it by ownership, integrate it by calling existing processes, give every tool it uses a Tool node, and put it to the owner. Process: library/processes/methodology-from-source.bpmn. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/adopt-methodology-from-source.md . adversarial-code-review candidate, extracted Review a pull request an agent touched by building the strongest case that it is wrong, unsafe, or not what it claims, and record the verdict where the merge gate reads it: one merge-review/v1 file per head, on the merge-reviews state branch, never in the pull request itself. Covers who may review, what the whole-diff scope is, the RED FLAG categories and their evidence rule, the one rebuttal round, overrides, and how a per-head verdict composes with a merge train. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/adversarial-code-review.md . agent-handoff candidate, extracted Governs handing ONE task to an agent in another environment — a local agent with network the cloud session lacks, a sibling on a different machine, anything that cannot read the coordinator's context and that a person may relay to. States who writes which work item, where the receiver reports, what the person pastes (one sentence: work item, branch, repository) and the brief the work item opens with (second person, to the executor), what the receiver checks before acting, who closes, who may grant an exception, and how to recognise and answer the five ways an executor fails. Use when writing a work item for another agent to execute, and as the receiver before acting on one. Triggers on: hand off, handoff, local agent, agy, mac agent, needs network, executor failed, agent went silent, re-hand, "give me a branch and bean for them", relay, the other agent. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/agent-handoff.md . agent-memory candidate, extracted Durable memory for a subagent — the three entry labels and what each promises, why entries are authored as graph nodes rather than in the generated file, the injection budget that silently truncates, and archiving as the third state between "reaches everybody" and "deleted". Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/agent-memory.md . agent-permissions candidate, extracted Securing what a coding agent may do without asking, from the person who can grant it: the secure-agent-permissions sub-process, run at session start and on demand when an action is denied. Vendor-neutral: the coding agent is a Tool (Claude Code is one; Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and Codex are others), and each Tool's own config format belongs to its adapter, not here. Covers the permissions the harness's processes need, least privilege, how each one is explained before it is granted, how a grant is recorded, and the rules that no grant relaxes: never self-granted, generated projections are CI's, and merging to main is never a standing permission. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/agent-permissions.md . apply-decision-support candidate, extracted The point-of-care system applies a DAK decision table's PlanDefinition to one client ($apply) and gets the proposed actions back as a RequestGroup (R4; RequestOrchestration in R5), or as CDS Hooks cards when the guidance comes from a CDS service. Input is the PlanDefinition and the client; output is the proposal, every request in it still a proposal. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/apply-decision-support.md . archimate-models candidate, extracted ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model's own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio's staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source's own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/asset-extraction.md . associate-harness candidate, extracted Declare a harness this one knows about and does not hold (associatedHarnesses): a folio in another repository, published at its own site. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/library/cataloguing/bib-qa.md . block-actions candidate, extracted Every block of a rendered document links back to where it can be changed: [edit] opens the block's Markdown source in GitHub's editor, and [feedback] opens a GitHub issue about that block, from the folio's own issue form when it has one, listing the change-sets that already discuss the block. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/bpmn-processes.md . branch-archaeology candidate, extracted Classify every remote branch against the default branch (merged, landed by squash or cherry-pick, partially landed, unlanded, undetermined) by commit ancestry, patch-id and merge-tree, not by subject line. Prevents stale assumptions, merge conflicts, and duplicated work without spending CI on churn. 906c5c9ef99e.content: cache-first-ci candidate, extracted Every CI step is a pure function of its inputs: derive the inputs, hash them into a key, restore on a hit, run and save on a miss. Read before adding a cache to a workflow, before writing a cache key, before trusting a restored output or a skipped verdict, and before pushing a change that moves a cached step's key. Covers the one primitive (cached-step + cache:key), the trust classes, what a committer publishes, the 10 GB budget, and the hit-rate report. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/cache-first-ci.md . canonical-watcher candidate, extracted Derivation-discipline integration watcher — watches the default branch + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for non-canonical empirical / fitting / calibration inputs beyond the project's declared set, numerology, or justification/rationalization in place of derivation. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake, post-completion one-voice, sibling-PR comment protocol, backlog-found PR spin-up, handover docs) from sdlc-core/integration-watcher. 2a7e841708ef.title: G
2a7e841708ef.content: gate-tree-mutation candidate, extracted Reading bun run cat gates' "NOT clean" verdict. Why every gate can pass and the run still exit 1, the two causes and how to tell them apart in one command, and the question that settles whether a churning field is a defect in the writer: does it describe the SUBJECT or the RUN? . Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/gate-tree-mutation.md . generalise-the-fix candidate, extracted You have a fix. Before it ships, ask what CLASS of defect it belongs to and whether the fix sits at the right layer — then attack your own answer: name what the fix now catches that the bug did not. Two axes go wrong, SCOPE and STATE, and widening either past the problem is how a fix becomes the next defect. Applies to a bug fix, a schema change, a detector, or a claim in a paper. Use after the fix works and before the pull request. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/generalise-the-fix.md . getting-started candidate, extracted Triage what a person means when they ask to create a folio, and route them. Five requests share one sentence — a folio in a new repo, folio-assistant overlaid on an existing repo, a second folio in a layer that already has one, a content object they called a folio, or something the filesystem cannot tell apart. Reads the repository facts, runs them through the folio-intent decision table, asks a selectable question for what facts cannot settle, scaffolds, and reports the published URL. Use whenever a user asks to create, start, set up, or initialise a folio, a paper, a DAK, an IG, or "folio-assistant" itself. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/getting-started.md . git-friendly-churn candidate, extracted Write files that git keeps many versions of (caches, published sites, generated indexes) so each new version costs a small delta, not a whole copy. The rules: the same bytes when nothing changed, stable paths, per-build facts kept apart, no compressed blobs, and how to measure it. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/git-friendly-churn.md . github-pages candidate, extracted The contract GitHub Pages keeps as the host of a rendered Knowledge Graph: serve the gh-pages branch at the publication root URL, exactly as committed, and answer 404 for what is not there. A mechanical Actor plays this Role; this is what it must do, and what it is tested against. Skills of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/skills/github-pages.md . github-state-inspection candidate, extracted Answer questions about GitHub-hosted state — is a page published, where does it live, did CI pass, does a branch exist — by reading the ref or the API, never by composing a URL or fetching one. The first check for any deployment or 404 question is git ls-tree of the publish ref. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/github-state-inspection.md . glossary-build candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/library/cataloguing/glossary-build.md . glossary-terms candidate, extracted Add terms to a layer's glossary: local SKOS terms (folio-glossary/v1) with a definition, a code and links to external SKOS concepts, and references to whole external schemes. Rendered on the glossary/ page; gated by check:glossary. Authored terms go to gettext (.pot) for translation; a paper's glossary is one more scheme. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/library/cataloguing/glossary-terms.md . goal-review candidate, extracted Cold start, then review a time window of activity — sibling sessions, the work plan, issues, change proposals, branches, CI — and prioritise what it finds against goals stated in the owner's words. Inputs are the window, the goals, the scope and the axes; the output is a synopsis (closed, open, needs doing, with effort), a priority queue per goal with selectable next actions, and the instruction gaps met on the way, each recorded as a work item. Use when asked "what happened", "what is stalled", "what should we do next for X", or at the start of a session that inherits parallel work. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/goal-review.md . grade candidate, extracted GRADE — the grading system a WHO guideline folio declares for certainty of evidence, and the Evidence-to-Decision judgement a recommendation rests on. Read when a folio's Task_AppraiseGrade runs under GRADE, before recording a certainty, an EtD judgement or a recommendation's direction and strength. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/grade.md . graph-detanglement candidate, extracted Drive a tangled graph toward a clean partition, so a sub-graph can be split off when it grows too large or when a business reason separates it. The staged practice — declare in place, detangle, isolate, extract — and the seventeen moves for measurement, ordering, judgement and enforcement. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/graph-detanglement.md . graph-rendering candidate, extracted Draw any graph in a harness (schemas, processes, a folio's block graph and any formal relation its content type adds, a detangle partition) so the picture is derived, checkable and readable. Ten rules, which engine to lay a graph out with and why, and how each graph typology here applies them. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/graph-rendering.md . groebner-basis candidate, extracted Compute Gröbner bases and normal forms for (possibly non-commutative) algebraic structures using a CAS (e.g. Singular letterplace) or an instrumented project routine. Reduce words to normal form with step-by-step logging, extract invariants, and emit witness JSON. Skills of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/skills/content/folio-paper-adapter/groebner-basis.md . guideline-use-case candidate, extracted Stage 0 of smart-guideline-end-to-end: turn a request for a SMART Guideline into a use case — population, setting, jurisdiction and interventions in scope, new or an adaptation — in the requester's own words. The agent asks numbered questions for what the request did not say, and never invents the answer. Read when a guideline request arrives, before any L1 source is looked for. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/guideline-use-case.md .

90d4deb913c3.title: H
90d4deb913c3.content: hand-back-to-discussion candidate, extracted A sibling agent, spawned during or working beside a live agent-human discussion, hands every card, question, decision, result, blocker or piece of context back to the discussion agent that is talking with the person, and never leaves it only in its own thread. The discussion agent asks the person (ask-the-person), marks every copy answered, and routes the answer back. A review sheet or issue in play is an extra channel. Use whenever an agent that is not the one talking with the person has something the person must see. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/hand-back-to-discussion.md . handover-report candidate, extracted Write a handover report: a templated snapshot of an agent's current state, committed as a work item note, so that a session or subagent that stalls, runs out of context, or loses its container can be picked up by another agent without re-deriving anything. Use it when you are told a stall is likely, at the end of every long arc, before a risky or long-running step, and whenever a steward asks for one. Its reader is stalled-agent-triage. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/handover-report.md . harness-projections candidate, extracted Who may write under .claude/, and when. The generated projections of the knowledge graph (.claude/commands/*.md from skill:commands, the assembled agent memory under .claude/agents/ and .claude/agent-memory/) are written by CI, which commits them to the PR branch, and never by an agent. A hand-edited .claude/ file (settings.json, its hooks, a hand-written command or agent definition) changes only with the owner's explicit consent to that change: the agent shows the exact diff and the reason, asks first, and records the consent. Read before staging any path under .claude/. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/harness-projections.md . harness-requirements candidate, extracted What a layer OWES for every directory it declares — a visualiser, a documentation entry, a governing skill, json/jsonld/schema.json serialisations at the directory's URL and at every node beneath it, and a starting README of its own. Read before declaring a directory, before adding a graph typology, and when reading check:subgraph-coverage. Carries which obligations are ranked as unmet promises rather than unanswered questions, why the discriminator is "is this the static knowledge graph", and which single obligation a harness may never waive. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/harness-requirements.md . harness-tiles candidate, extracted A tile is a function of the harness watching a directory, not of nodes. Where the tile set comes from, what a tile opens, and the two gaps it reports rather than hides. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/harness-tiles.md . html-rendering-qc candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/platform-ui/skills/platform-ui/html-rendering-qc.md . human-agent-discussion candidate, extracted Ask a person (or a sibling agent) for what no file holds. First determine where you are — the context, the Role you act as and theirs, the Process and task (or that you are idle) — and ask about whichever you cannot determine before anything else. Then context, the options, a recommendation and what happens with no answer, then ONE question. Skills of bootstrap · source bootstrap/skills/human-agent-discussion.md . hypothesis-generation candidate, extracted Formulate evidence-bounded scientific questions, candidate hypotheses, rival explanations, causal or associational claims, discriminating predictions, measurements, and preregistration-ready analysis plans. Use when turning observations or preliminary findings into transparent, testable research plans without treating hypotheses as facts. Skills of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/skills/content/hypothesis-generation/hypothesis-generation.md .

9aae9771f984.content: idle-backlog candidate, extracted While idle or waiting on a long-running async task (a build, a long compute script, a CI run, a background agent), pull the applicable backlog in priority order and work non-conflicting items instead of stalling. Use whenever blocked on an async wait with no substantive output to produce. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/work-plan/skills/work-plan/idle-backlog.md . ig-artifact-ingestion candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/ig-artifact-ingestion.md . ig-ast-delta candidate, extracted List and view what changed between two IG ASTs, check whether an AST is still valid for the IG's current inputs, and render the delta as just-the-docs pages that carry the provisional mark. Read before trusting a cached AST, before reviewing an incremental IG build, and before rendering anything from a cache. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-ast-delta.md . ig-binary-artefacts candidate, extracted Where the IG Publisher's binary outputs go — full-ig.zip, package.tgz and its R4/R4B variants, package.db, validator packs, and the definitions, examples and expansions zips — and why a pages branch is the wrong place for them. Measure a branch with ig-binary-audit before deciding anything. Read before configuring an IG's deploy or release step, before linking a download from a page, and before a pages branch grows past its size limit. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-binary-artefacts.md . ig-build-pipeline candidate, extracted The bare FHIR IG pipeline — FSH to SUSHI to the IG Publisher to a pages branch, with no pre-processing and no post-processing. What this layer runs, what it emits, and the list of things it deliberately refuses to know about. Owns the AST cache lifecycle: an IG site is built from the AST on its cache branch, the publish refuses a stale one, and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml is the one writer. Owns what an IG reader may read: contentTypes.ig.include in the repository's index.config.json, and the legacy warning for a repository that declares none. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, before onboarding, converting or changing the workflows of an IG repository, and before publishing an IG site. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-build-pipeline.md . ig-content-qa candidate, extracted Review an IG's resource narratives, markdown fields and pages for injection attempts before its site is published, and record the review as the QA sidecar the publish gate reads (qa/ig-content-qa.json, keyed to the digest of the texts). Read when an IG site build refuses with "injection QA", when asked to review an IG's content for injection, or before changing the gate, its pattern rules or the browser's check in ast-resource.js. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-content-qa.md . ig-publication candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/content/fhir-ig-authoring/ig-publication.md . ig-publisher-fork candidate, extracted Requirements for an agent working a local experimental fork of the IG Publisher — which repositories, what the AST must carry, what must not change, and the acceptance criteria. Read before forking, and before reporting a fork's work complete. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-publisher-fork.md . ig-publisher-reduction candidate, extracted The phased transition that reduces the IG Publisher to AST + QA — five phases, each with an exit criterion that is measured rather than asserted, and the staleness contract that makes an AST-backed staging build honest. Read before starting any phase, and before claiming one is done. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-publisher-reduction.md . ig-publisher-service-contract candidate, extracted The contract the ig-publisher-service role is held to: what the JVM services an IG build shells out to must produce, and how a caller tells a pass from a run that never happened. A mechanical role's skill is a contract to test against, not instructions to read. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/content/fhir-ig-authoring/ig-publisher-service-contract.md . ig-render-jekyll candidate, extracted Rendering a FHIR IG's content through the just-the-docs pipeline instead of mounting the IG Publisher's finished HTML — the JSON-only representation contract, navigation derived from sushi-config.yaml, and the LHS rail. Read before adding a representation, a menu entry, or a page kind. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-render-jekyll.md . ig-site-links candidate, extracted What happens to an IG's links when its pages are rendered on our site rather than by the IG Publisher: which are rewritten (artefact pages, a case-only mismatch, the Publisher's downloads and pages, files of the IG's repository, the OpenAPI index), which are reported as the IG's own dead links, and the gate that keeps a generator from linking a page it does not write. Read before changing build-ig-site's relinking, gen-ig-pages' links, or before concluding an IG page's broken link is ours. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-site-links.md . ig-site-theme candidate, extracted How an IG rendered through just-the-docs wears the theme its instance ALREADY declares: the one webpage theme becomes the IG site's colour scheme. Says which of the three theme paths applies to which surface, what is refused, and how to verify on the built CSS rather than on a log line. Read before theming an IG site, adding a theme to an IG instance, or concluding that a staged IG is unthemed. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-ig-base/ig-site-theme.md . incremental-render candidate, extracted Rendering only what changed — seeding a build from a previous render, the two edges that decide what must re-run, why a step declares GRAPH TYPOLOGIES rather than paths, and the rule that could-not-determine always re-renders rather than serving a stale page. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/platform-ui/skills/platform-ui/incremental-render.md . index-config candidate, extracted index.config.json at an instantiation root says which harnesses the checkout instantiates, where each one comes from (local, or a remote mount pinned to a SHA), each layer's config INLINE in its entry (a legacy <name>.config.json is only imported until --inline retires it), and which harness / is. Covers instantiated against declared, landing resolution and its error case, index.lock.json and its legacy fallback, the reserved index stem, the generated .gitignore block and its gate, and index-config:migrate (with --inline) for separated repositories. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/index-config.md . indicator-extraction candidate, extracted Extract the indicators an L1 source prints (indicator reference or metadata sheets: name, numerator, denominator, disaggregation, definition, data sources) as L1 indicator nodes with every printed field, then draft one L2 program indicator per indicator, derived from its L1 node. Read before adding a WHO handbook's or guideline's indicators to a DAK or a DTH, and whenever an L2 indicator has to trace to its source. Part of L1 → L2 extraction for every DAK and DTH, beside recommendation-extraction. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/indicator-extraction.md . inform-client candidate, extracted A health worker tells the client (or caregiver) what was decided and what happens next, in words and, where the DAK gives one, on a slip or card: a referral, a return date, a result. Input is what to tell and the client's language; output is that the client was told, and what they were handed. Generic for any DAK step that ends with the client being informed. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/inform-client.md . initialization-steps candidate, extracted Walk every initialization step the declarations name (the layer's own and each one it needs), check each before doing anything, do what can be done, ask for what only a person can do, and report every step as done, not done, could not determine, or stated. Skills of bootstrap · source bootstrap/skills/initialization-steps.md . injection-boundaries candidate, extracted Where a value becomes program rather than data — workflow expressions, shell strings, and archive members. What the gate covers, why a step output carries a severity rather than having one, and the argv rule. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/security/injection-boundaries.md . instance-kinds candidate, extracted How to make a new KIND of harness layer — choosing the prefix family, the keep-the-kind's-name default and the owner's right to decline it, which inherited files the new owner may repoint, and what a new GRAPH typology must declare. Read before naming a new layer, before adding a value to the graph-typology registry, and before building a visualiser. Carries the test that usually says "this is not a new kind". Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/instance-kinds.md . instance-publication candidate, extracted Every asset carries an id and a version and sits in DRAFT. Publication is a state, not a boolean, and published is refused by the schema because the formal process does not exist yet. Carries the id namespace rule, why a mirror never takes its subject's identity, and what a consumer may assume of a draft. Also the one home for which graph each layer publishes, where, under which IRI and schema, and what is stripped from it. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/instance-publication.md . integration-audit candidate, extracted Sidecar-invalidation utility for the integration-watcher pipeline. Adds mechanical QA fields (script-reviewer entries) to per-block .qa.json sidecars and marks the existing entries stale so the next qa-sweep re-evaluates them. Use when a checker bug is fixed in a QA checker module (downstream "fresh" entries are now incorrect) or when a registry update adds a criterion the block hasn't been audited under. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/editorial/skills/editorial-audits/integration-audit.md . integration-backlog candidate, extracted Dispatcher for the /integration-backlog <axes> slash command. Works the backlog identified by the integration watchers (proof, canonical, compute, detangler, one-voice, …) by clustering the open findings into review-sized batches (≤ 49 files per PR — the reviewer-bot limit), proposing each batch to the author via structured AskUserQuestion calls, running /prepare-merge on each, resolving review comments (auto if mechanical, structured AskUserQuestion if architectural), then merging — and repeating until the axis is exhausted or the author signals stop. Sister command to /integration-watch: the watcher MONITORS for new events; this skill WORKS the backlog the watcher already catalogued. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/integration-backlog.md . integration-watch candidate, extracted Dispatcher for the /integration-watch slash command. Routes to one or more of the concrete integration watchers / audits (canonical, one-voice, consolidation, bibliography, devils-advocate, and those a content type's layer adds, …). With no argument, lists the available watchers and asks the user which to invoke. With arguments, dispatches the named watchers in parallel (each gets its own Monitor, queue, ledger, and PR-subscription set). Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/integration-watch.md . integration-watcher candidate, extracted Abstract parent skill for domain-specific **integration watchers**. Encodes the shared mechanics — Monitor on origin/main, PR subscriptions, per-event QA dispatch, queue + ledger, idle backlog sweep, idle author-ask dispatcher, watch-PRs-you-prepare protocol, voice-pass on PR diff, witness-drift CI recovery, billing-quick-fail flake handling — that every concrete watcher inherits. Children fill nine domain-specific slots; everything else is shared here. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/integration-watcher.md . interaction-modality candidate, extracted Establish how to talk to the person in front of you before deciding what to say — audio, ordinary chat, selectable options for limited hand function, large-type for low vision, plain language — and hold that choice durably so every later session and sibling agent honours it. Covers the accessibility rules a conversational agent can actually keep, the settings surface in the published site, and how to drive a question set from DMN so the SAME logic serves every modality. Use at first contact with a new user, when a user reports difficulty answering, whenever a question is about to be asked, and before any long free-text prompt. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/interaction-modality.md . iris-cdn-exporter candidate, extracted The IRIS CDN Exporter agent — how WHO IRIS is exported onto Cloudflare — a git repository on Cloudflare Artifacts and R2 behind the CDN — with an initial load (metadata and PDFs), a nightly change ingest over the DSpace REST API, a weekly reconciliation, and one signed release per run. 6fbc26adf874.title: J
6fbc26adf874.content: journey-maps candidate, extracted Journeys and workshops as knowledge-graph content: a DAK user scenario told as a journey map (user-scenario kind: ordered steps, per person what they do and feel, pain points, enablers, the record's trust state, and edges to stories, BPMN tasks, requirements, FHIR examples, building blocks and the DAK's data sets, decision tables and indicators), the building-blocks catalogue its steps use, a workshop that teaches from it (workshop kind: modules, objectives, questions for the room on each step, reference tables, sheets, job aids), the journeys-viewer visualiser that draws them for a layer and the layers it mounts, and the check:journey-refs gate that every reference they name resolves. bbbcd34e4a99.title: K
bbbcd34e4a99.content: kg-affordances candidate, extracted The four affordances of a conformant knowledge graph — browse, materialise, instantiate and copy-into-folio — which capabilities each requires, how each writing verb degrades cleanly when no write capability is available, and how copying an asset stamps KgAsset.source provenance. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/kg-affordances.md . kg-contribution-offer candidate, extracted Ask whether agreed requirements should become knowledge-graph content, and as what — in a form the person can answer by selecting. Use at the end of CRDM sign-off, or whenever a body of agreed work could become a skill, a process, a schema or a work item and nobody has been asked. Offers "none" as a first-class answer. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/kg-contribution-offer.md . kg-export candidate, extracted Serialize a layer's knowledge graph to one JSON document, for publication and inspection. Read when asked to visualize, audit or share the KG, before adding a node type to the export, and before minting or authoring any subject IRI — subjects are <doc dir>/<kind>/<id>, never #fragments. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/kg-export.md . kg-navigation candidate, extracted How a cold agent finds and loads the skill that governs its task. The two Tools that serve the knowledge graph — the MCP pair and the filesystem fallback — what counts as a skill, and the three ways the search goes wrong. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-navigation/kg-navigation.md . kg-separation candidate, extracted Separate a Knowledge Graph into its own repository — as a CONTENT repository (files to read, no code) and a TOOLS repository (the code that writes and checks it) — once it is too large, or its consumers or cadence differ. 25bf90647d42.content: sample-import candidate, extracted Testing an import of a SAMPLE of a remote source into a knowledge graph or other structured store: scope it, let materialize-remote gate it, land it in the library (permanent) or the kept, unpublished trashcan (trial), import it, and test the import. Then re-run main's checks and report. Use for "runners are full", "cancel everything and merge what's ready", "meta-merge", "consolidate the queue", and when the queue has not moved for an hour or more. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/saturation-meta-merge.md . schema-management candidate, extracted Manage a schema over its life — add one, change one, read the schema graph and its viewer, and act on what the reader could not determine. The layout rule lives in directory-conventions; the entity question lives in data-modelling; this is the work in between. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/schema-management.md . scientific-accuracy candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Use for assessing experimental design validity, identifying biases and confounders, applying evidence grading frameworks (GRADE, Cochrane Risk of Bias), or teaching critical analysis. Skills of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/skills/content/scientific-visualization/scientific-visualization.md . secrets candidate, extracted Adding, rotating and revoking the credentials the harness's automation needs, one mechanism at a time, with the exact GitHub UI path for each step. What the boundaries are, which machinery already guards each one, and the single rule that unifies them — refuse, never repair. Read this before adding a check, so the answer that already exists is reused rather than rebuilt in a fourth place. Where the non-determinism actually lives, why the diagram stays strict, the cat-harness.processes:judgement marker that makes a judgement point countable, and what the machine must never do on the actor's behalf. Suites are named by the identifiers the standards already define. Signing is done by the parties' own systems; the harness verifies. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/signing.md . simulator candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/skills/content/folio-paper-adapter/simulator-math-audit.md . site-presentation-assets candidate, extracted A visual fact — a colour, a glyph, a theme — lives in a graph node, and the stylesheet the site serves is a rendering of it. Use whenever a user asks to create, start or set up a SMART Guideline, a SMART IG, a WHO IG or a DAK. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/smart-guideline-create.md . smart-guideline-end-to-end candidate, extracted The whole road from a use case to a running application on WHO SMART Guidelines, for a new guideline or a jurisdiction's adaptation, as an orchestrator of ten named stage skills, each with its own input and output contract: guideline-use-case, dak-l1-library, recommendation-extraction, l2-dependency-choice, l2-dak-authoring, l3-dependency-choice, l3-fhir-authoring, l4-application-brief, wireframe-design-review and l4-application-build. Read before starting any end-to-end authoring or adaptation, and to find which skill runs each stage. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/smart-guideline-end-to-end.md . smart-launch candidate, extracted How a browser app performs a SMART on FHIR launch — EHR launch and standalone launch — with the SMARTerFHIR library: SmartLaunchHandler, the LAUNCH and EMR enums, the scopes it requests per EHR vendor, how the redirect URI is computed, and where the token ends up. Written against a pinned upstream commit; read before wiring a launch page or a redirect page. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-client/smart-launch.md . smart-stack-layering candidate, extracted Which layer a WHO SMART asset, rule, script or page belongs to — fhir-harness, smart-base (with its L1 and DAK document kinds) or smart-ig — and the one question that settles it. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, smart-base or smart-ig, before creating a per-IG harness, and before moving a pre/post-processing step. Skills of smart-base · source smart-base/skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/smart-stack-layering.md . spec-kit candidate, extracted Spec-driven development, adopted whole: define what and why before deciding how, and do not develop before a spec exists. Mandatory sections and required fields are machine-readable here for automated validation. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/spec-kit/spec-template.md . specification-compiled-agents candidate, extracted When a diagram already says what the process is, the model should not be planning it. The two gaps between this repository's engine and a compiled control plane — typed node contracts and per-node context scope — what to do before either exists, and the three things not to adopt with the method. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/specification-compiled-agents.md . specification-management candidate, extracted Governs the lifecycle, syntax, and traceability of specifications and requirements across the harness. Connects spec-kit and CRDM tracks to the 6-part bootstrap Requirement definition, enforces EARS and ISO 29148 statement quality, and defines how requirements project to open standards (ReqIF, OSLC-RM) while keeping bootstrap strictly decoupled. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/specification-management.md . staging-review candidate, extracted Staging preview and before/after comparison for content review. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/swarm-management.md . swimlane-glossary candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. c454425edb02.content: Edit deterministic logic (if needed) candidate, extracted If the content change affects decision logic, indicators, or workflows: - Update CQL expressions - Update DMN decision tables - Adjust indicator definitions skill: dak-authoring, fhir-pipeline . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_EditLogic . Edit it in place — it is your own content candidate, extracted The ordinary path, drawn so the process does not read as though every edit needs a copy. Content in a writable directory is authored content and is edited where it lives; the copy-out is for somebody else's bytes, not for yours. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_EditDirectly .
