Edit the component candidate, extracted Create or change the component with the authoring skill the call names, one component per pass. On rework, apply the review's findings; a fix written in an AuditNote is applied as given. An adapted component is edited against its pinned upstream, so the before side of the diff is that upstream, not an empty file. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-component-edit-review.bpmn#Task_Edit . Edit the document as decided, on a feature branch candidate, extracted public-comment edit --branch: the author (human, or an agent in the author role) edits the folio's blocks as the decision says, on a feature branch for one change-set. Its PR says Closes #N for the change-set issue, and opening it moves that issue's accepted comments to editing. Before its preview is staged, the author writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per comment (No. 136: Accepted...), starting from each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, after an optional Overall statement. Quality check: every comment number in the change set has a disposition; the sheet flags gaps and words that differ from the people's. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_AuthorEdits . Edit the document in the row's pull request candidate, extracted One row, one branch, one active pull request: the agent edits on the row's branch and opens its pull request, or updates it when the row comes round again. A closed pull request the committee wants back is reopened, or replaced by a new one on the same branch; earlier ones stay listed in Agentic status. Agentic status (Green) says where it is, and Staging review opens the preview's what-changed page. Before the preview is staged, the agent writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per feedback item, starting from the people's Blue Disposition, after an optional Overall statement; the sheet shows it in Disposition (agent) and flags any item without a disposition, or one that differs from the people's. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_EditInPullRequest . Flows to Task_PoInject, so the round-trip QA runs again over the corrected text — "edit the translation and re-run QA", which is what the adjudication step has always offered and what this process could not do. A userTask, not a service task: this is the one step here where a person edits content, and the lane's actor is the reviewer who just adjudicated. A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. 9754287295af.title: G
9754287295af.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). A slice whose rows do not match its source fails; it never passes as whole. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Check . Gate results: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 2c. RESTORE: the result store (build/result-store/) and the CI cone records, by prefix — a WARM start: the cone (ci-cone.ts) then matches each stored entry exactly (fingerprint from cache:key --base, every recorded path state, every replayed git answer) and only an exact match is reported SKIPPED, never passed. A committer's local gate record is class (b): honoured on the critical path, then re-verified off it. SAVE: main only (class c for CI's records). Owner roles: the gate-reuse session (CI speed 8) and the committer-side session (CI speed 3). cache nodes: result-store, ci-cone, local-gate-records. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Gates . Gather and verify the evidence candidate, extracted Before anything is drafted: the author reads the guidance ALREADY in this content, frames the question as PICO, retrieves candidates across the three evidence classes, and has each candidate's authority resolved against its publisher's own API. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source adds none -- and the subprocess's first gateway (Gateway_RecommendationInPlay) ends it there at its own event, recording the answer, rather than satisfying the search vacuously. The fail condition: no started line within 4 h, no push within 24 h, the session gone, or blocked on something it cannot settle. One line to the session; the instructions are in the bean. Then keep working on the recommended option where it can be undone, or stop if blocking. Hand new feedback to the row's agent; take over stalled rows candidate, extracted On every poll, changed or not, new Blue feedback goes verbatim to the agent working the row, and a stalled row is restarted or taken over. For each row: new Blue feedback goes, verbatim and in the same poll, to the thread that owns the row (named in its Agent row or Feedback (agent)), and Feedback (agent) says who has it. A row is stalled when its Blue cells changed, or Ready for agent turned Yes, more than 10 minutes ago and no Agent step was recorded since; or when its agent recorded no step for 2 hours. A stalled row's owning thread is asked once; with no answer within 10 minutes, or a thread that is done or stopped, the watcher takes the row over, or asks the coordinator for a new thread, and writes the new owner, the step and a link into Feedback (agent). Worked from the row's binds list in upstream-pins.json. For the theme: site-chrome/assets/js/docs-ui.js MOVES the theme's own search markup into the action launcher and binds .search, #search-input and .search-label; docs-ui.css overrides .side-bar, .site-header and .main-header; three e2e specs assert the structure the theme emits. Import hygiene (HARD) and advisories (WARN-ONLY) candidate, extracted FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE RUNNER — bean 7fu5. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/**/*.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner's ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/**/*.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job's LAST step, where it masks nothing. Load the landed sample into the chosen store and check what an import can get wrong: every item arrived (count against the request), identifiers survived (the descriptor's authoritative ones), structure validates against the store's schema, and provenance (source, revision, fixity) is attached to each node. 7cdd3b5ea1a2.content: Jekyll cache: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 5, last: it caches the rendering of what the components above produce. Owner role: the preview session (CI speed 2). cache node: jekyll-cache. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Jekyll . Judge the assets in their design candidate, extracted A person looks at the ingested assets laid out in the design they are for, at BOTH a web and a mobile width. THIS IS A HUMAN STEP INSIDE INGESTION, stated rather than hidden: ingestion of a THEME SOURCE is attended at this step, while ingestion of everything else never reaches it. A judgement made at one viewport is incomplete, not passed, and the wireframe of the surface (wireframe-design-review) says what each layout was meant to be. A clean build, a passing suite and every gate can all miss what only rendering the page and looking finds. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Task_Judge . 6d0a54832cb4.title: K
6d0a54832cb4.content: Keep it as a trial: the unpublished trashcan candidate, extracted A trial goes to the kept trashcan: addressable, exported, never published. Its node declares $schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1 and carries the bean or issue it was written under, since it was never moved from anywhere and a movedFrom would be invented provenance. It is NOT refreshed: a trial records what the source looked like when it was tried. Promoting a trial means running this process again with permanent = yes, so the gates are asked afresh. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Trial . Keep the edit, re-pin candidate, extracted The local edit wins, so nothing is re-materialized — and the pin moves to the upstream revision that was compared against. Re-pinning is the half that is easy to forget and is the reason this is a step rather than an absence: without it the same upstream change is detected as new on every cycle, and a contributor is asked the same settled question for ever. The record says the copy is deliberately divergent FROM a named revision, which is a different claim from being stale against an unknown one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_KeepLocal .

893c6781575e.title: L
893c6781575e.content: L1 completeness gate candidate, extracted See ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn. Skill-backed by l1-document-ingestion: its section "What a complete L1 entry holds" names check:l1-complete as the gate and states its three results. The gate contains one adjudication (Task_FlagDrift: real, spurious or source-wrong), and its own Task_Verdict records the answer as a reason against the verdict before returning. So both answers reach this step, and nothing here branches on them; Gateway_Complete branches on the gate's completeness verdict instead. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Gate . Called, not copied, so a change to the generic pipeline reaches every IG built on it. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dak-l3-ig.bpmn#CallActivity_L3Fhir . Land each member candidate, extracted Once per member, in train order, at the SHA the train's gate set tested. merge-to-main.bpmn is where merging is a step with its own gate: it reads the head's evidence live (the train's green run is that evidence, and merge:guard re-evaluates it), establishes that the owner authorised THIS merge (explicitly, or by a standing ruling quoted verbatim with its date, e.g. 2026-10-01 "you may merge green PRs", which covers green heads only and only the queue as it stood), records the authorisation, merges pinned to the head, and then confirms main, re-pins downstream mounts and notes the bean. Until 2026-10-09 this was two steps here, Task_Release in the owner's lane bound to interaction-modality and Task_Land bound to prepare-merge; neither could refuse a merge, and neither said what happens when a repository has no CI. R1 still holds: what lands is exactly what CI tested. If main moved after the train's CI started, re-run rather than land. Each member's trainId is cleared, and its preview is then taken down by feature-staging.bpmn. A member the sub-process does not merge (held, refused, handed back) leaves the train with its reason on its queue entry. Land the bytes in the copier's own folio/ candidate, extracted Into the copier's own declared folio/, never a scratch area — a directory nobody declared is a directory nobody gates, and the copy would be publishable by accident. The copy is NOT read-only: it is the copier's own content, makes no claim about anybody else's bytes, and freezing it too would mean the next person needs a copy of the copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_Land . Land the feature's PRs candidate, extracted Phase 6's "explicit confirmation before merging to main", made a step that can refuse. Once per pull request the feature still has open, after the sign-off is recorded and before the issue is closed: an issue is not closed on a feature that is not on main. merge-to-main.bpmn reads each head's evidence live, establishes that the owner authorised THAT merge (a stakeholder sign-off or the BA's confirmation is acceptance of the feature, not authorisation to merge it, unless the owner's own words say so), records the authorisation, merges, and confirms the base. A PR the owner holds or refuses stays open, and A_Close then waits: the BA's authorisation to close does not cover a feature that did not land. An increment the owner asked to land earlier in Phase 6 went through the same sub-process at that time. Where cat-harness.sdlc is switched on, this step is the opt-in process merge-to-main (Process_MergeToMain, sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn); it is not called from here, because a layer without that sub-graph does not have it (owner card Q-OPTIN-CALLS A, 2026-11-12). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#Call_MergeToMain . Languages: extracted, rendered, and RTL candidate, extracted Every user-facing string reaches the .pot; every declared locale renders without clipping or overflow; right-to-left is laid out rather than mirrored by accident. New UI is where untranslated strings enter, because nothing was stale — there was nothing there before. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Locales . Lay out the options, with what each costs candidate, extracted Every option the agent could narrow the question to, each with what it costs and what it makes hard to undo. Narrow from context first: an option the agent could have ruled out itself wastes the reader's attention. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_LayOutOptions . Layers ref: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 1, which everything else needs. RESTORE: mount-from-lock replays the lock from refs/cat/layers/<key> (key = sha256 of the lock's layers), verifying every layer's tree digest, declaration and asset sha256 against the committed lock — class (a), verified against THIS tree, so a bad entry is only a miss, and a stale refs/cat/layers/main still serves every layer that did not move. SAVE: the committer (layers:publish, run by mount:remote after it changes the lock), with the re-pin train and main as fallbacks. Not wrapped in cached-step: its per-layer verify is finer than one hit. Owner role: the layers-ref session (CI speed 13). cache node: layers. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Layers . Lean .oleans: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 3, after the layers (the Lean packages are mounted content). RESTORE: the compiled .oleans of each declared Lean package, keyed by the package, the toolchain AND the lake manifest (the Mathlib revision) — the manifest is part of the key, so an entry from another revision is a miss. lake build re-checks every restored module's trace, so a stale module is rebuilt, not trusted: class (a). SAVE: main; a contributor's warm build may be offered back (compiled-artefact-cache) and is accepted only through that same trace check. Owner role: the integrator (CI speed 14). cache node: lean-oleans. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Lean . Leave a reachable way back candidate, extracted Leave the way back reachable: the collapsed window becomes a control in its own position and focus moves to it — left alone, focus lands on <body> and the keyboard position is lost. An action whose inverse is not reachable is not a toggle. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-open-close.bpmn#A_OfferWayBack . Claiming is how two sessions avoid picking the same item; closing someone else's is how one of them loses work it had not finished reporting. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-open.bpmn#Open_LeaveAlone . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Todo . Leave it referenced, record why candidate, extracted A refusal is not a failure of the process — it is the process working. The node stays referenced, which means the graph still knows it exists and where, and the refusing gate's basis is recorded so the next caller does not re-litigate it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_StayRef . Leave the content exactly where it is candidate, extracted The reader said no: nothing moves, no position is dropped, and the board is left exactly as it was. Drawn as its own end state because a destructive action whose refusal is not drawn gets performed by accident. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_Cancel . Link glossary to smart-ra SKOS [terminology-management] candidate, extracted Each handbook term is exactMatch, closeMatch or narrower to a smart-ra concept; conflicts are raised as issues on smart-ra. Calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dth-authoring.bpmn#Call_Glossary . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn#Task_Link . Scan before creating, and never create one without the BA's permission — an issue is the stakeholder's record, not the agent's scratchpad. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Issue . Link to existing issue candidate, extracted A match was found: ask the person whether the requirements go on #NNN, then link the work there. The issue is where stakeholders sign off, so no phase proceeds without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_LinkIssue . Link to smart-ra ArchiMate [archimate-models] candidate, extracted Every block that names an architecture element links to its smart-ra element or view; new elements go to smart-ra, not the handbook. Placeholder: no platform subprocess; done by hand, as for dth-hrh. Calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview. Assess the digital health enterprise architecture, identify the common and enabling components and shared services that make up the digital health platform, and link the investment to both. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/methodologies/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_LinkEnterpriseArchitecture . List indicators and metrics (Component 8) candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Inclusive of the cursor second, de-duplicated by uuid, returned oldest first. BPMN activities of who-iris · source who-iris/processes/iris-cdn-nightly.bpmn#Task_ListChanged . The candidate everybody has is bootstrap itself. Context may name others: "please set up <owner>/<repo> here" names one, and so does any Harness built on bootstrap that the Requestor mentions. This step narrows; it does not decide. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListHarnesses . Both are Knowledge Graph Data Stores; the difference is only how they are reached. A location whose root already holds a declaration, <name>.json, is not a blank slate, and says so in the question. Each step names the declaration that names it, so a reader can see why it is there. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_ListSteps . Nothing is cloned and no API token is needed, so the check runs the same way on a laptop and in CI. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Task_QueryUpstream . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_LoadActive . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogMessage . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogEnd . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogStart . 47a22466b3dd.title: M
47a22466b3dd.content: Make sure every step is done candidate, extracted Following a harness's instructions once is not the same as every step being done. complete-initialization walks the steps the declarations name — FIRST the harness's JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, the primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness; then declared directories, assets, the README and its sections, and the site that carries the documents — checks each, does what can be done, asks the person for what only they can do, and reports every step in its state. An agent may be dispatched to run it on its own: it needs nothing but that diagram and the declarations. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_CompleteInitialization . Make sure gh-pages exists and Pages serves it candidate, extracted Provisioning the target, owned by this process rather than by the publication step that calls it. Pages cannot serve a branch that does not exist, so in order: (1) an orphan gh-pages branch exists — git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages; if absent, push a placeholder (index.html + .nojekyll); (2) Pages is on, Source = the gh-pages branch at / — gh api -X POST repos/<o>/<r>/pages -f source[branch]=gh-pages -f source[path]=/ when gh is signed in, otherwise the exact manual step (Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages, / (root)). Each half is done, not done, or could not be determined; never assumed. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Provision . Make the change candidate, extracted The loop's only open-ended step. Everything around it is procedure; this is the work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Implement . Make the change candidate, extracted content-change-review-make.bpmn: scope the change, branch, edit content and logic, assess and absorb the downstream impact, and push. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_MakeChange . Make the change, check it and merge it candidate, extracted The second phase, drawn on its own page (public-comment-change.bpmn): an author edits the document as decided on a feature branch, the change set is reviewed on its staging preview, an independent QA gate checks the dispositions against the pull request, and each comment it answers is marked incorporated when it merges. A withdrawal still interrupts the comment while this runs. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#CallActivity_MakeChange . Make the PR ready candidate, extracted Its own work is done and its full tier is green as judged; it is marked ready by the queue rule (continual-progress, Pace the ready marking). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-request.bpmn#Sib_Ready . Make the value proposition and set next steps candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 9. The case made to whoever pays, and what follows. Scaling up is a different method and a different publication — 9789241509510-eng, The MAPS Toolkit — which begins where this implementation ends. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/methodologies/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_ValueProposition . Map concepts to WHO Commons dictionary candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/SGAuthoring.DAKLifecycle.bpmn#Task_MapToCommons . Map L2 → L3 candidate, extracted Each data element becomes a profile, each value set a ValueSet, each decision a PlanDefinition / Library. The DAK's L2 content is l3-fhir-authoring's sourceModel; l2-dak-authoring, bound beside it, carries the WHO L2 → L3 ordering, which the generic skill does not name. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dak-l3-ig.bpmn#Task_MapL2 . Map the affected layers in order candidate, extracted Run the re-pin planner (mount:repin:cone) with the fleet and the changed repository. It lists every site downstream in waves, so a site moves only after the layers it takes from have moved, and marks which sites are ready now. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_MapCone . Map the current state and confirm bottlenecks candidate, extracted DIIG Chapter 3.1. Determine the health programme processes to target, map their workflows, identify and confirm bottlenecks. Then 3.2, a root cause analysis. This is where DIIG builds on CRDM, and it says so: "This process builds on the Public Health Informatics Institute's Collaborative Requirements Development Methodology (CRDM)". Its three areas of concentration are business process analysis, business process redesign and requirements definition — two of which name diagrams this platform already executes. They are parallel tracks, not a composite: pick one per decision and name it. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/methodologies/processes/diig-investment-path.bpmn#A_MapCurrentState . Map to ICD-11, SNOMED CT, LOINC candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/SGAuthoring.DAKLifecycle.bpmn#Task_MapToStandards . Map values onto palette roles candidate, extracted surface / ink / edge / accent, shared across every kind. A palette per kind would be three spellings of "accent colour", free to disagree about what an accent IS. Where the source is SILENT on a role, say so and mark the value a choice rather than dressing an invention as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/ingest-theme.bpmn#Task_MapRoles . Mark confirmed items withdrawn (keep bytes) candidate, extracted The record gets a withdrawn state; its bitstreams stay addressable, because a citation to them may exist. BPMN activities of who-iris · source who-iris/processes/iris-cdn-reconcile.bpmn#Task_MarkWithdrawn . Mark every copy answered candidate, extracted Chat copies keep their text: the question struck through and "[Edit: <letter> chosen by <who>, <time>]" added. Cards closed with the chosen option. The sheet's "Decision needed" block replaced by the decision and who made it. Withdrawn or superseded hand-backs marked the same way, with the reason. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_MarkAnswered . Mark incorporated when the change set merges candidate, extracted public-comment incorporate, naming the branch, PR and staging URL; done by the folio's workflow when the PR that closes a change-set issue merges. A PR closed unmerged moves nothing. Ready for merge is set only once the QA gate has passed for the PR's head commit; set earlier, the agent does not merge until it passes. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary that closes its issue. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_Incorporate . The bean itself is not touched: closing or noting on someone else's bean is how a sibling loses work it had not finished reporting. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-drain.bpmn#Drain_Skip . Mark the record superseded or retired candidate, extracted Never delete (git rm) a superseded or retired requirement. When superseding req:<old-slug>, set status: superseded and supersededBy: req:<new-slug> on docs/requirements/<old-slug>.md. When retiring, set status: retired and document the retirement reason and authorising issue in prose. Update any RequirementSet (docs/requirements/*.set.json) so approved/accepted sets hold only in-force members. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/requirements-filing.bpmn#A_UpdateLifecycle . Materialise the part candidate, extracted The ONLY way bytes arrive. Purpose first, then the five gates — size, restrictions, copyright, retention, source loss — then fetch with fixity, or stay referenced with the refusing gate's basis recorded. Both ends of that subprocess return here and the walk continues: one part refused is not the subscription refused. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Materialize remote content (the five gates) candidate, extracted The shared subprocess. It resolves the request against the source descriptor, then asks size, restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, and either fetches with fixity or leaves the content referenced. This process does not restate any of that; it waits for the outcome. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Measure the cutover: separation:cutover:check candidate, extracted Run bun run cat separation:cutover:check --site in the SEPARATED repository (Tool separation-cutover-check). Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate and none assumed: every declared layer mounted at its pin; every path a declaration names resolves (check:declaration-resolution — directories, assets, visualisers, needs); no wiring still names the monorepo (livesAt, a submodule, a reusable workflow, a path into the old checkout); no import or reference against the layer order; and the site builds from the mounts alone. A finding inside a mounted layer is upstream's and is listed, not counted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-cutover.bpmn#Task_CutoverCheck . Measure the signals candidate, extracted Files and bytes per layer, clone cost (bun run cat health), gate time, merge contention, the candidate's cohesion and cut (kg:detangle), wrong-direction edges, and the would-be tools package's import cone. Recorded in the work context; none alone is a trigger. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Measure . Mechanical checks, both viewports candidate, extracted Tool wireframe-check renders every candidate at a web and a mobile viewport. It fails on horizontal overflow at mobile width, on placeholder text, and on a missing viewport, and writes screenshots and a script entry per criterion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#D_Check . Merge and publish candidate, extracted content-change-review-publish.bpmn: merge on the owner's explicit confirmation, then remove the staging preview, rebuild main and watch it. An unmerged change keeps its preview. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_Publish . Merge each member onto the base candidate, extracted merge-base.bpmn once per member, in order, --no-regen; then ONE bun run cat regen over the result. Tool: merge:train. Always onto the current base, never a cached one (R5). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Call_MergeMembers . Merge into each locale candidate, extracted Merge each refreshed template into every locale's catalogue: new strings arrive empty, changed ones fuzzy, and obsolete ones are kept as #~ entries, never deleted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_MergeLocales . Merge it through merge:guard candidate, extracted A workflow PR, or a PR in a repository with no train, merges directly. A workflow PR needs no approval beyond the batch card (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card Workflow PRs, A). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-manager-watch.bpmn#Task_Direct . Merge main in, regenerate, fix mechanical gates candidate, extracted Merge commits only; never a force-push. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_AgentFix . Merge manager for its own PRs candidate, extracted No merge manager is needed (a lone session, or a lapsed lane): the session is its own merge manager for its own PRs only, so it runs the merge manager loop for them. It does not announce itself to the others; it posts the six lines in its own chat and asks the owner by card. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-request.bpmn#Sib_Self . Merge manager watch candidate, extracted The elected session holds the merge steward lane and runs its loop until it hands over or the lane lapses. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-request.bpmn#Sib_CallWatch . Merge restored and rebuilt records candidate, extracted Combine the restored per-artefact records with the cone's freshly rendered ones into one complete set, so the meta-index rebuild that follows has every artefact's record and never re-derives one. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the base in, without committing candidate, extracted git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main on a clean tree (untracked files refuse too, so the final stage cannot sweep in a scratch file). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the one source PR to main candidate, extracted All the templates in one PR to main, merged before any locale starts, so every translator branches from the same main. Once it has merged, its branch receives nothing more: a later fix to the source is a new PR. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_SourcePR . Merge the PR candidate, extracted Merge the layer's PR to main, then confirm the template checks pass on main. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Merge . Merge the pull request candidate, extracted The agent merges the row's pull request, and Agentic status says merged. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary: it goes into the merge, and closes the change set's issue. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the re-pin with its decided revisions candidate, extracted The re-pin merges when its checks are green and every decision it needs is recorded. Its pull request cites the decisions, which become the release notes for this site's update. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge train candidate, extracted Add the merge-train label instead of merging; the train lands the batch with one CI run. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-manager-watch.bpmn#Call_Train . Merge, hold or refuse candidate, extracted The owner's answer to the question Task_Ask asked. Their words are quoted verbatim in the record, so the answer is given in the conversation or on the PR, not inferred from tone. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_OwnerDecides . Merge, on explicit confirmation candidate, extracted The owner says "merge it", and only then is the branch merged. Merge to main triggers: 1. the main site rebuilds with the changes; 2. the staging preview's cleanup runs; 3. the review comments committed on the feature branch land on main, as the review record. bd22b61a7110.content: OCR to ocr/page-*.txt candidate, extracted Each page is read in the document's languages (--lang-hint, from dc.language.iso), narrowed to the script the page shows. A page Tesseract is unsure of (mean word confidence under 70) is read again with each other installed script added, and the most confident read is kept: a French article's Arabic abstract, or the Latin URLs in an Arabic document's references. A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently ("Manual" and "Manval"), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. Options analysis accept · revise · discard candidate, extracted On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down. Not between Gateway_EditorDecision and Task_RecordDecision: Flow_21b runs Task_RecordDecision -> Gateway_EditorDecision, so the gateway reads a decision already recorded. In the Agent lane: the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED (its own decision-audit note), and Task_RecordDecision in Lane_Editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN. The analyst is not the decider. (CallActivity_Evidence is in Lane_Editor because the author performs the retrieval.) On the trigger: A_Frame opens the subprocess on opening-brief's trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. A spelling fix that reached Task_ReviewFindings with one mechanical finding exits immediately; a revise-or-discard on a block other content depends on does not. Options analysis adopt · hold · decline candidate, extracted On the single edge into PM_Decide, and deliberately not earlier: the MVP build and its gates are HOW the options' costs are measured, so an analysis before Task_Mvp would weigh alternatives against no evidence. Everything the decider needs exists by the time the reviewer has finished and the fixable findings are fixed. In the Agent lane, because this step produces the analysis and does not make the decision — PM_Decide is a userTask whose lane admits person only, and putting the analysis in the agent's lane is what keeps that separation legible rather than implied. A subprocess that decided would be a second accepting party. Reached through the loop as well as straight through: SF_UA_8 re-enters at A_Impact, so a run where the reviewer found something fixable arrives here a second time with different evidence. That is a genuine re-analysis and its op="note" appends rather than deduping, which is the behaviour wanted — a second note records that the options were weighed again against changed inputs. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to absorb the impact candidate, extracted On the edge OUT of Task_AssessImpact and before Task_CommitPush, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. Not between Task_AssessImpact and Task_ReviewImpact: those are in different processes with no sequence flow between them; the assessment reaches the committee through Task_CompareBeforeAfter. In the Agent lane, matching upstream-version-adoption: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and GW_Approved in the committee review is where a decision is taken. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. Process_OptionsAnalysis opens with A_Frame, whose trigger is opening-brief's — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator (from Task_EditLogic) does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. By Phase 6 the needs, requirements and data model are signed off, which is exactly the evidence an options analysis needs and the reason it belongs here rather than earlier: at Call_Needs there is nothing to weigh, and after A_Implement the choice has been made in code. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. 500a3b326382.content: P1.1 · Agree the terms candidate, extracted The parties agree the purpose, the datasets, the period, the conditions and duties, which trust anchors each side accepts, and the legal basis the sharing rests on (consent, treatment, public-health law or a research waiver). This sets what the text must say; it is a negotiation between people. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_AgreeTerms . P1.2 · Write the legal text candidate, extracted Write the agreement as a document folio: one normative statement per clause the parties must keep, through normative-statements. The text says which governs if it and a machine-readable form disagree (suggested: the text). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_WriteText . P1.2a · Record the legal basis candidate, extracted The text states the legal basis the parties agreed in P1.1 as a normative statement: consent, treatment, public-health law, or a research waiver. Consent rule 1: only an agreement whose legal basis is consent carries the odrl:obtainConsent duty; treatment, public-health law and research waivers do not rest on consent. The gateway that follows, the ODRL and the reviewers all read the basis from this statement. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_RecordLegalBasis . P1.2b · Draft the plain summary candidate, extracted Consent-based only. Write a plain-language summary of the agreement in the same document folio: what it lets the recipient do with the person's data, in words the person can read. Consent rule 3: every agreement that needs consent publishes this summary, hashed with the agreement (P2.2a), and the summary is what the person consents to. It is reviewed, rendered and versioned with the text. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_PlainSummary . P1.3 · Derive the ODRL 2.2 Agreement candidate, extracted Computable only. One assigner and one assignee (ODRL 2.2 §2.1.3), permissions and prohibitions with target assets (§2.2), constraints (§2.5.1) and duties (§2.6.3), written as JSON-LD. Purposes from HL7 PurposeOfUse. Consent rule 1: the Agreement carries the odrl:obtainConsent duty only when the legal basis recorded in P1.2a is consent. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_DeriveOdrl . P1.4 · Check the ODRL against the text candidate, extracted Computable only. A person checks that the ODRL says what the text says, and signs it off. A program can check the ODRL is well formed; it cannot check that it matches the text. The check includes the consent duty: present when the legal basis is consent, absent otherwise (consent rule 1). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_CheckOdrl . Only the hash of a private annex is ever published. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_SplitAnnexes . P1.6 · Sign candidate, extracted The signatories sign: wet ink, or an electronic signature under national law. Technically a detached JWS (RFC 7515) or CMS (RFC 5652); PAdES for a signed PDF needs the owner's approval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/dsa/processes/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Sign . Place it in uploads/ by a declared route candidate, extracted THE FIRST LINK: everything downstream of here takes a file that is already in the queue, so without this step how the file got there is governed by nothing. WHAT THIS STEP IS. The basic flow's ACCEPT step: choosing an arrival route, writing the bytes into the declared queue of the layer that will own them, and discharging what that route does not discharge for you. The routes, what each writer owes, and the two that are mechanisms against the one that is a persona are in the upload-routes skill; upload-url composes the forge URL for the web route from the declaration rather than from a literal, because a hand-written one can 404. WHY A PLAIN bpmn:task AND NOT A userTask. A userTask asserts a human performs it, and this lane is "Contributor (human or agent)" because both do; asserting human-only would be an activity-fulfilment-kind contradiction. A plain task asserts nothing about the performer. WHY THE BEAN OP IS note AND NOT claim. Placing a file claims nothing; it adds to a queue. What it owes the work plan is visibility. A note against the ingestion bean is what makes the queue's growth something another session can see. Prioritize, and map to health system challenges candidate, extracted DIIG Chapters 3.3 and 3.4. Prioritize the bottlenecks, then map the programme-specific ones onto the generic health system challenges. THE ARITHMETIC IS REFUSED HERE. 4823c4028600.title: Q
4823c4028600.content: QA gate: check dispositions against the people and the pull request candidate, extracted Before Ready for merge. Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, the PR's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every comment number has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted comment has its change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate or Out of scope one has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set), first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows both under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_QaGate . QA gate: check dispositions and PR candidate, extracted Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), the people's Blue Disposition and feedback, the pull request's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every feedback item has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted item has the change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope item has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set) on the Agent tab, first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows the gate under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. QA working copy, built once (NOT A GATE) candidate, extracted Bean jtfk, issue #2456. bun run qa:working-copy (bean 72a8) — the bootstrap kg-export, then every declared QA writer — used to run INSIDE each job that reads the QA tree, and qa-publish ran the same writers again: nine builds of one tree from one commit, measured at 2,284 of 4,714 runner-seconds (48 %) on run 37659324493. Now the qa-working-copy job builds it once and uploads everything the build changed as an artifact with a sha256 manifest; each reader downloads it, checks the manifest against the hash this job reported and every restored file against the manifest, and only then judges. An artifact rather than a cache, because a cache key built from less than the real inputs serves stale data; an artifact is per run and exact. It judges nothing, so it is not a gate and does not reach GW_Join; a failed build fails every reader at its first step (they run if: !cancelled()), never a skip. Drawn feeding GW_Readers, the four tasks that wait for it; within them typescript-static and gates-standalone read no QA tree and do not wait, and qa-publish waits for it as well as for Task_RepositoryGates. bd6a03228c1f.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, R–Z
bd6a03228c1f.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 641 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 255 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 14 (SKOS) · smart-base 161 (SKOS) · who-iris 34 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 441 terms and is 354 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 1206 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 1206 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 441 shown . R S T U V W

cf0d8dd6bd69.content: Raise a finding against the wrong side candidate, extracted The prose and the code really disagree: raise a finding that names which side is wrong and why. Usually the prose, because the code is what runs — but a skill can state intended behaviour correctly while the code has regressed, and then the finding is against the code. Re-materialize and record new fixity candidate, extracted The gates are re-asked, not inherited: a licence can change, and a collection can grow past the size a caller agreed to. AND THE NEW FIXITY IS RECORDED IN THE SAME CHANGE. This step rewrites bytes that a materialization record describes, so leaving the old digest behind would make a CORRECT run of this process fail check:materialized-fixity as a mismatch — the gate reading "somebody edited held content without saying so" about the one process whose job is to replace it. This is the publication exception, stated as a rule rather than as a carve-out, because a list of permitted writers goes stale when a writer is added. The exception is NOT "these actors may skip the rule"; it is "say what you did". A writer that updates the digest alongside the bytes passes, and the record then describes what is actually there. A writer that does not fails, correctly, because it has forked upstream silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Apply . Re-pin downstream mounts, as PRs candidate, extracted For each layer whose index.config.json mounts this repository: a PR moving ref to the merge commit, with a trust.consent whose evidence quotes the owner's consent to that pin, and the lock regenerated by mount:remote. (NOT A GATE) candidate, extracted Bean qbco, issue #2456 (owner, 2026-10-07: "1y, 2y, 3y, 4y"). On a PUSH to main only; on any other event it is skipped and nothing waits for it. A merge-button merge of an up-to-date PR carries a tree CI has already tested. verdict-reuse.sh looks up the runs of this workflow on the merged head (the merge commit's second parent) and answers reuse=true only when one concluded success, ran every job a reuse would skip, and tested exactly this tree: for a pull_request run, the tested-tree: its Task_QaWorkingCopy job wrote into its check run's summary; for a dispatch, the head's own tree. Then the four bun test shards (part of Task_TypeScript), the three e2e shards (Task_E2E) and the standalone ratchet (part of Task_RepositoryGates) are skipped on this push, and the summary names the run whose verdict stands. Everything that judges the tree against main or reads qa-reports still runs. A squash, an API error, a missing record or a mismatch is reuse=false and every job runs: could-not-determine is never green. Drawn before the fork because the jobs it can skip wait for it; the others do not. 2a9914750fe5.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, A–D
2a9914750fe5.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 641 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 255 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 14 (SKOS) · smart-base 161 (SKOS) · who-iris 34 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 379 terms and is 304 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 1206 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 1206 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 379 shown . 0–9 A B C D

72c6ad930796.content: 0 · Describe the use case candidate, extracted Population, setting, jurisdiction, interventions in scope. A sub-graph that owns its own layout gains a NESTED declaration whose paths resolve against its own directory, so the whole graph relocates by moving one folder. 0d46e348f476.content: Abort, restore the tree, list what was refused candidate, extracted git merge --abort. Each refused path is listed with its pattern's reason, or "no declared pattern". BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Abort . Accept it, and record where it came from candidate, extracted Both branches land here. An unprompted offer is accepted as it stands — do not make somebody follow a process to hand over what they already have. Provenance is recorded whichever channel it arrived through: a description given in chat has a source and can be wrong, exactly as a PDF does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Accept . Accept or decline the guidance candidate, extracted See the proposed actions on the device and accept or decline each one, one tap each ("accept all" is one tap); modify one only where the device offers it. Nothing else is asked; an "add a reason" link is shown, never required. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/act-on-decision-support.bpmn#Task_Review . Accept the new state candidate, extracted Runs the check again with --accept, so the state file holds what was just handled and the next poll compares against it. A row the pass could not finish stays changed and is picked up on the next poll. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_Accept . Accept, or send back candidate, extracted The editor's lane, kept separate on purpose: the reviewer who judged the change is not the position that accepts it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Accessibility: measure, do not assert candidate, extracted Contrast COMPUTED against the real ground, including the worst case a backdrop can present; a non-colour channel wherever colour carries meaning (SC 1.4.1); an accessible name on every region; keyboard and focus order. An automated pass is necessary and not sufficient — axe accepts a non-empty placeholder as an accessible name, and a CSS selector that matches nothing raises no error at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Accessibility . Account for every normative sentence [l1-coverage] candidate, extracted Each normative sentence is captured or excluded; exclusions are signed by a person, never by the agent that proposed them. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dth-authoring.bpmn#Task_Coverage . Act on the answer candidate, extracted Never ask the person again for what they answered. A rule-level answer goes into the governing skill in the same turn. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Act . Add an actor, and declare its kind candidate, extracted Human, agentic or mechanical. A userTask because the agentic/mechanical line is JUDGEMENT — role-model.md says so — and reading it wrong disqualifies the actor from every judgement task it exists to perform, silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AddActor . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_AddressReview . Adjudicate against the checker candidate, extracted The reviewer and a checker read the same claim differently — a disagreement about ONE kg-qa criterion (prose-claims-resolve). Descend into Process_CriterionAdjudication, which runs the shared adjudication and then one of its three outcomes: the checker's finding stands, the criterion is scoped, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. The checker's entry is kept beneath the verdict rather than overwritten (requirement R4 of issue #1042). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/narrative-code-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudication . Adjudicate L2 dependencies candidate, extracted Programme manager and business analyst: one row per candidate DAK, rejected ones included. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_AdjDepsL2 . Adjudicate L3 dependencies candidate, extracted FHIR modeller and terminologist: one row per candidate IG, rejected ones included. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_AdjDepsL3 . Adjudicate slot codings and glossary candidates candidate, extracted Review each slot's classification and code against the terminology-coding methodology: the authoritative scheme for the slot, the reuse-first rung, skos:exactMatch vs skos:closeMatch precision (ontologist), and any Rung 4 glossary candidates (promote valid ones from candidate to authored per glossary-terms, or replace them with an existing code). BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/classify-and-code-content.bpmn#Task_ReviewCodings . Adjudicate the conflict candidate, extracted A human or agentic decision, never a merge rule. Which side wins depends on why the local edit was made, and a process that picked automatically would be choosing without the one fact that decides it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the criterion disagreement candidate, extracted The shared judgement — entry condition, untainted dispatch, person-or-agent restriction — asked with THIS question's permitted answers. cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes sits here rather than on A_Adjudicate inside it because the answers depend on what was asked, and the gateway below is what acts on them: the engine refuses a mismatch between the two. Process_Adjudication may also leave at End_NotAdjudicable — one entry and no other side is a review or a gate, not a disagreement — in which case nothing below runs and there is nothing to record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted The judgement itself, and the one step nothing here can check: if a mechanism could decide it, the process would not have been entered. It declares NO cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on purpose, and that absence is the whole of bean bvuk. This step used to name three — stands, scope, dispensation — and six diagrams called it: review-narrative and voice-review, whose question those three answer, and four whose question they do not. refresh-materialized asks which side wins a local-vs-remote conflict; there is no criterion to scope there and no dispensation to grant, yet the outcome half ran regardless. Since the caller's question decides the permitted answers, the caller declares them: cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on its OWN call activity, with its own gateway acting on them. criterion-adjudication.bpmn is that for the QA-criterion question. What could NOT be fixed by passing the codes as data, which was this bean's first recommendation: the three branches ran three different TASKS, so a caller handed local-wins would have had it pointing at A_ScopeCriterion. The branches had to move, not the enum. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/adjudication.bpmn#A_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted adjudication.bpmn. When the editor and a reviewer, or two reviewers, disagree about a finding, an adjudicator settles it and records why; the review comment moves to adjudicated with the Decision that closed it. Permitted answers: stands — the finding is right and the author addresses it; withdrawn — the finding is wrong and the comment closes. Recorded on the comment, not branched: either way the flow goes on to the coverage check. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Call_Adjudication . Adjudicate the flagged passage candidate, extracted A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_FlagDrift . Adjudicate the flagged passage (human) candidate, extracted A human SME or editor reviews the flagged passage. They may: - Accept the translation as-is (false positive) - Edit the translation and re-run QA - Reject and request re-translation The round trip establishes that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the L1 KG candidate, extracted l1-extraction-reviewer signs exclusions and coverage; Clinical SME reviews recommendations beside the printed page. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_AdjKg . Adjudicate the L1 source list candidate, extracted Clinical SME: each source with why it was included or left out. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_AdjL1 . Adjudicate the L4 wireframes and application candidate, extracted Business analyst and clinical SME walk it through each L2 user scenario; FHIR modeller checks L3 conformance. A PREVIEW REBUILDS ONLY ITS DEPENDENCY CONE (owner cards Q-CONE-1 C and Q-CONE-2 B, 2026-11-01): main's writer records say what each derive:publish writer and each step of the QA working copy READ. A writer or QA step whose recorded reads all match is not run, and main's outputs for it are put back. Every other one runs. QA is not left out of a preview, only narrowed to what the change can reach. Build the entry candidate, extracted First the working copy is produced (qa:refresh, bean 3hk4): while the checkout still tracks test/results/, the commit's own copy is the record and nothing runs; once it does not, every declared QA writer runs into the empty tree, because the gates are in judge mode and wrote nothing a publish could carry. A refresh that leaves a writer failed, a family empty or a file unclaimed is INCOMPLETE: the job goes red and qa:publish --completeness refuses, so a partial tree is never stored as the commit's record — the "Not stored" outcome, reached before any push. Then it hashes the working copy of every declared qa directory (<instance>/test/results/**, byte-identical to the checkout's layout) into a tree through a private index, and writes manifest.json (qa-reports-manifest/v1): inputs, producers, verdict counts and the gates' result. Identical JSON is the same blob, so an unchanged family costs nothing to store again. Its git objects live in a private bare repository, never in the checkout's own store. Check the selected methodology's evidence base candidate, extracted Before applying a methodology, establish that the thing being applied is what it claims to be. A methodology is adopted because it is somebody else's named, external work; this step checks that the origin it cites resolves to a source in a declared library, and reads the methodology-evidence QA sidecar for it. WHY THE CHECK IS HERE AND NOT AT ADOPTION. Adoption happens once; selection happens every time a decision is made. A source that was reachable when the methodology was adopted can stop being so, and a methodology adopted before this axis existed was never checked at all. Measured 2026-09-22: six methodologies cited an origin and NONE had that source in any library, so every selection made until then rested on an unverifiable citation. WHAT A GAP DOES AND DOES NOT DO. A missing source does NOT block the decision, and this step has no branch that stops the process — that would make a documentation gap into an outage, and the owner decides whether an unbacked methodology may still be used. It does two things: it runs literature-search to try to close the gap, and it puts the evidence state into the record A_Record writes, so a reader can tell a decision made on a verified method from one made on a citation nobody could follow. The third state is the one that matters. "Source ingested", "source located but unreachable from here" and "no source found" are three different facts, and literature-search exists largely to stop the middle one being reported as the last. Free text is always available and never required. A dismissal is NOT an answer and never selects the default as a choice; the question stays open in the chat. fcb0b345a4c9.title: Glossary: BPMN activities
fcb0b345a4c9.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Build an IG repository's own site from its cached AST, with no instance declaration candidate, extracted The three checkout scripts the platform's site build runs for a repository that holds an IG and only mounts layers (index.config.json): ig-site:ast restores the AST from the IG's cache branch (ig-cache.sh restore) and judges it, refusing a stale, cannot-tell or absent one (a stale one is accepted for a preview by default, refused with SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=0, and never accepted for the root); ig-site:compose derives the artefact index from the AST (binding any IG API sidecars a layer above left in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/), writes the thin artefact pages, stages the IG's input/ and sushi-config.yaml (menu read at build time, palette from the webpage theme of the top layer the repository mounts, edit links from its origin) and composes it at the ROOT of the host site source; ig-site:publisher-pages serves each of the AST's resources once, as <Type>-<id>.json at the root (no ast-data/ mirror) — reduced (minified, no narrative, no ELM data, the ELM attachment pointing at the full copy) when the pages read the full resources by raw URL from the AST cache commit, and off with SITE_ROOT_RESOURCES=0 — the artefact index (or fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json, pointing at the cache's copy) and the sidecars (or none, read from the cache), refuses a page wearing the IG Publisher's chrome, repairs repeated element ids and stamps folio-build.json. Check a review log and its repository's issues for changes candidate, extracted The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet's Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository's open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check's. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell's old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet (Title the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue's URL; a closed issue's row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log's Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. 007f1c8c60a2.title: V
007f1c8c60a2.content: Validate draft MeSH headings against NLM's authority candidate, extracted Stage three of skill-pipeline-subject-indexing for MeSH: look up every candidate heading of a draft (a preferred heading, an entry term, or a descriptor id, with an optional qualifier) in NLM's MeSH authority at id.nlm.nih.gov, current year. Each candidate comes back resolved (in the preferred form), qualifier-not-allowed (descriptor kept, qualifier dropped), ambiguous (options listed for a person) or not-found (dropped). It never adds a heading the draft did not propose and never emits one the authority lacks. The IG site's service worker answers the self-hosted Form Builder's LOINC search from it, and its UCUM search from the vendored full UCUM list, so the site makes no cross-site call. build-ig-site runs it for every IG with a Questionnaire. Write one JSON-LD node per IG artefact, and check a built site's nodes candidate, extracted write turns an artefact index into artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld under a docs root, with no .json twin: one folio-ig-artifact-jsonld/v1 node per artefact, in borrowed vocabularies only (the FHIR RDF class, dcterms, schema.org, PROV), naming the artefact's canonical URL, its representations and, for a compiled copy, what built it. With --root-resources (the IG site's default) the first representation is the reduced <Type>-<id>.json the site serves at its root (local), the second the full copy in the AST cache by raw URL (mirror), and each index entry names the root file (schema:contentUrl). check is the kind's QA: over a BUILT site, every artefact has its node and no node is an orphan, each node is its own file's, no .json twin is served beside it, and every local resource it names is on the site. It also writes and checks the index node, artifact/index.jsonld (folio-ig-artifact-index-jsonld/v1): every artefact once, each entry naming its node. These are the assets the thin pages render. Write the IG AST viewer: a page per instance holding ig-ast directories, and a hub candidate, extracted For every visualiser an instance declares renderedBy: ig-ast-pages, write the hub at <locale>/<harness>/<id>/ and, with subgraphs: "instance", one page per instance that declares an ig-ast directory, at …/<instance>/. Each lists the ASTs the directory holds: the IG's package id, resources in total and by type, dependency edges (resolved inside the IG, by origin, by kind), the rebuild plan when one is recorded, and what stays provisional. A declared directory not on disk — a branch-family member not restored, which is the normal case — is reported UNKNOWN with the family it would be restored from, never as zero ASTs. ig-ast-list summarises one AST it is handed; this Tool needs no AST path. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 5001 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 5001 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss.
