30ebc66c8e20.title: Bibliography: folio-assistant-core-library/arxiv-2510.21603v1
30ebc66c8e20.content: The reference for folio-assistant-core/library/corpus/arxiv-2510.21603v1 (folio-assistant-core) and any references extracted from it. folio-assistant-core-library · All references. Dong∗, Kuicai; Huang∗, Shurui; Ye∗, Fangda; et al.. Doc-Researcher: A Unified System for Multimodal Document Parsing and Deep Research. TitleDoc-Researcher: A Unified System for Multimodal Document Parsing and Deep Research AuthorsDong∗, Kuicai; Huang∗, Shurui; Ye∗, Fangda; Han, Wei; Zhang, Zhi; Li, Dexun; Li, Wenjun; Yang, Qu IssuedD:20251027 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2510.21603 AbstractDeep Research systems have revolutionized how LLMs solve com- plex questions through iterative reasoning and evidence gathering. However, current systems remain fundamentally constrained to textual web data, overlooking the vast knowledge embedded in mul- timodal documents: scientific papers, technical reports, and finan- cial documents where critical information exists in figures, tables, charts, and equations. Processing such documents demands sophis- ticated parsing to preserve visual semantics, intelligent chunking to maintain structural coherence, and adaptive retrieval across modal- ities, which are capabilities absent in existing systems. In response, we present Doc-Researcher, a unified system that bridges this gap through three integrated components: (i) deep multimodal parsing that preserves layout structure and visual semantics while creating multi-granular representations from chunk to document level, (ii) systematic retrieval architecture supporting text-only, vision-only, and hybrid paradigms with dynamic granularity selec- tion, and (iii) iterative multi-agent workflows that decompose complex queries, progressively accumulate evidence, and synthesize comprehensive answers across documents and modalities. To enable rigorous evaluation, we introduce M4DocBench, the first bench- mark for Multi-modal, Multi-hop, Multi-document, and Multi-turn deep research. Featuring 158 expert-annotated questions with com- plete evidence chains across 304 documents, M4DocBench tests capabilities that existing benchmarks cannot assess. Experiments demonstrate that Doc-Researcher achieves 50.6% accuracy, 3.4× better than state-of-the-art baselines, validating that effective docu- ment research requires not just better retrieval, but fundamentally deep parsing that preserve multimodal integrity and support itera- tive research. Our work establishes a new paradigm for conducting deep research on multimodal document collections. 8f9d4b3713a5.content: Genetics Genes and chromosomes The International Committee on Standardizing Human Gene No-menclature has developed a system knownas the International System. for Human Gene Nomenclature, but this is not universally accepted. Human genes are generally denoted by italicized symbols composed of capital letters, sometimes with the addition of an arabic numeral (e.g. CF, G6PD). Lower-case letters are commonly still used in blood-group symbols (e.g. Fy, Rh). Phenotype symbols are set in roman type (e.g. ADA 1). 8d41cf0e899a.title: Isotopic labelling The symbol for the isotope introduced is placed in square brackets directly attached to the part o…
8d41cf0e899a.content: Isotopic labelling The symbol for the isotope introduced is placed in square brackets directly attached to the part of the name to which it refers (e.g. sodium ('4C]formate); appropriate arabic numerals and prefixes are added as necessary (e.g. L-[2-C]leucine). For simple molecules, chemical formulae may be used (e.g. 4#CO,). Square brackets should not be used when the isotopic symbol is attached to a word that is not a chemical name (e.g. “!*C-labelled”). Terms such as “'![-labelled albumin” should not be contracted to [3!T]albumin since native albumin does not contain iodine. 38e0a37b3b10.doc: WHO Editorial Style Monval Interferons Interferons are represented by the symbol IFN to which is attached by a hyphen…
38e0a37b3b10.title: WHO Editorial Style Monval Interferons Interferons are represented by the symbol IFN to which is attached by a hyphen…
38e0a37b3b10.content: WHO Editorial Style Monval Interferons Interferons are represented by the symbol IFN to which is attached by a hyphen the Greek letter representing its type, for example IFN-a for alpha interferons. Non-allelic variants can be indicated by an arabic number or capital letter (sometimes subscripted) attached to the Greek letter. The prefixes “Hu” and “Mu” may be used to represent “human” and “murine” respectively. For example: MulFN-y HulFN-B — HulFN-c4. Interferon nomenclature. Journal of immunology, 1980, 125:2353. b97424990ff1.content: CSF = cerebrospinal fluid; NPA= nasopharyngeal aspirate. Methodological quality Studies evaluating Xpert Ultra on sputum specimens (15 studies) In the patient selection domain, for MRS, we judged the risk of bias as low for most studies (13/15, 86.7%) and high for two studies (2/15, 13.3%) because in one study participants with definitive tuberculosis were excluded (Liu 2021) and in the other, the sampling method was retrospective and by convenience (Enimil 2022). Regarding applicability, we judged low concern for most studies (12/15, 80%). We judged high concern for two studies (2/15, 13.3%) because participants were enrolled exclusively as inpatients in tertiary care centers. We judged unclear concern for one study (1/15, 6.7%) because the setting was undefined. Issued2022 Typedocument As printedCSF = cerebrospinal fluid; NPA= nasopharyngeal aspirate. 68709b66f1e6.title: S-12 (Sassani et al., 1991) 3.2 Immune responses to revaccination Studies have examined presence of antibodies prior …
68709b66f1e6.content: S-12 (Sassani et al., 1991) 3.2 Immune responses to revaccination Studies have examined presence of antibodies prior to and following the second dose of mumps vaccine. In a prospective study, <1% of subjects were seronegative before a second dose of mumps vaccine and, following the second dose, IgM was detectable in only 2% of individuals, suggesting that most vaccine recipients had mounted a secondary immune response to revaccination (LeBaron et al., 2009). Although up to 30% of individuals were reported to be seronegative prior to revaccination in other studies, 75% to 97% seroconverted following the second dose of mumps vaccine. Badly written or ambiguous symbols and signs should be identified for the typesetter (e.g. italic letter “x”/Greek chi/multiplication sign; capital letter “O”/Greek theta/zero), and the spatial relationship of terms made clear. 95cc7b3be020.title: WHO Editorial Style Monval Interferons Interferons are represented by the symbol IFN to which is attached by a hyphen…
95cc7b3be020.content: WHO Editorial Style Monval Interferons Interferons are represented by the symbol IFN to which is attached by a hyphen the Greek letter representing its type, for example IFN-a for alpha interferons. Non-allelic variants can be indicated by an arabic number or capital letter (sometimes subscripted) attached to the Greek letter. The prefixes “Hu” and “Mu” may be used to represent “human” and “murine” respectively. For example: MulFN-y HulFN-B — HulFN-c4. Interferon nomenclature. Journal of immunology, 1980, 125:2353. 69a47f7d4a18.title: Genital herpes can also be due to HSV1 infection, and a study in Scotland found that 40% of genital herpes was due to…
69a47f7d4a18.content: Genital herpes can also be due to HSV1 infection, and a study in Scotland found that 40% of genital herpes was due to HSV1 in 1991 [Ross et al., 1993]. Both HSV1 and HSV2 are able to infect and reactivate in the same anatomic area, although the natural history of these infections is markedly different, with HSV2 recurring more frequently than HSV1, so most clinical reactivations are likely to be due to HSV2 [Sucato et al., 1998]. In developing countries, the proportion of genital herpes caused by HSV1 is unknown, although assumed to be low. 834cd9b7ebba.doc: There are currently few data on HSV2 prevalence from many parts of the world, including Asia, South America and many …
834cd9b7ebba.title: There are currently few data on HSV2 prevalence from many parts of the world, including Asia, South America and many …
834cd9b7ebba.content: There are currently few data on HSV2 prevalence from many parts of the world, including Asia, South America and many parts of Africa. HSV2 incidence data are also scarce [Kamali et al., 1999; McFarland et al., 1999; Hayes et al., 2001]. Prevalence and incidence data are necessary: i) to estimate population attributable fractions (PAFs) for HIV; ii) as background data to inform future intervention studies, such as HSV2 4. EPIDEMIOLOGY AND NATURAL HISTORY OF HSV2 treatment and vaccine trials; iii) to evaluate the need for changes in syndromic management of GUD due to presence of genital herpes; and iv) to evaluate the need for regular HSV2 seroprevalence surveys. Issued2001 Typedocument As printedThere are currently few data on HSV2 prevalence from many parts of the world, including Asia, South America and many parts of Africa. HSV2 incidence data are also scarce [Kamali et al., 1999; McFarland et al., 1999; Hayes et al., 2001]. Prevalence and incidence data are necessary: i) to estimate population attributable fractions (PAFs) for HIV; ii) as background data to inform future intervention studies, such as HSV2 4. EPIDEMIOLOGY AND NATURAL HISTORY OF HSV2 treatment and vaccine trials; iii) to evaluate the need for changes in syndromic management of GUD due to presence of genital herpes; and iv) to evaluate the need for regular HSV2 seroprevalence surveys. 17d590659af1.content: Oncogenes Oncogenes are usually designated by three-letter italic terms, often taken from the names of the viruses with which the genes are WHO Editorial Style Manual associated. A roman prefix may be added: “v-” for viral, “N-” for nuclear and “c-” for the gene’s cellular counterpart (proto-oncogene). Other prefixes and various suffixes are common. For example: Ha-ras-1 N-ras v-erb B yes c-abl fes/fps. 2769cae4a1a8.content: Nahmias et al, 1990 1 (f) females; (m) males 2 Age-weighted sample: younger age-groups were over-represented HSV2 AS A MARKER FOR SEXUAL BEHAVIOUR As HSV2 is more readily transmitted sexually than HIV, HSV2 serology may be a useful marker for changes in sexual behaviour in HIV intervention studies. However, the persistent nature of the infection implies that seroprevalence may not be a sensitive marker of behaviour change, although it will be more discriminating at the lower prevalences seen in younger age groups [Obasi et al., 1999]. HSV2 seroincidence would be a preferable marker of behaviour change, especially in countries in sub-Saharan Africa where there is high incidence among young people. c882701a0c42.content: Ahmed, A.A.; Latoundji, S. (2007). [Pilot study of antiretroviral therapy in Djibouti]. Title[Pilot study of antiretroviral therapy in Djibouti] AuthorsAhmed, A.A.; Latoundji, S. Issued2007-12-31 Typedocument Languagefr AbstractA cross-sectional survey was conducted among 112 HIV positive patients who had received antiretroviral therapy for > 3 months to assess the efficacy of treatment [viral load < 400 copies/mL]. The median age at enrolment was 36 years, 90% of patients were at the AIDS stage and median CD4 rate was 118/mm[3]. Patients received a combined treatment of 2 NRTI +1 NNRTI [51%], 3 NRTI [45%] and 2 NRTI+1 PI [4%]. Virological efficacy was seen in 74% of the patients, irrespective of the prescribed protocol and the initial clinical and immunological profile. Mean improvements measured were 20% on the Karnofsky index [KI], 2.1 kg/m[2] in body mass index and 82 cells/mm[3] in CD4. The prevalence of side effects was 84%. The predictors for treatment success were quality of care and KI > 70% Sources . | iris.who.int/handle/10665/117378 (canonical) | repository record (repository) | . 1ea7ff832d4e.content: World Health Organization (2022). Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV. World Health Organization. TitleGuidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-6-23 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240052178 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guideline provides updated, evidence-informed recommendations for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV. Developed in accordance with WHO Guideline Review Committee procedures, it replaces the 2018 guidance and incorporates important new evidence published in 2021 on the preferred antifungal induction regimen for cryptococcal meningitis. The recommendations are based on systematic reviews using the GRADE approach and are supported by considerations of acceptability, values and preferences, feasibility and cost–effectiveness. The document addresses cryptococcal disease as a major opportunistic infection contributing substantially to HIV-related illness, disability and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, and identifies priority knowledge gaps to inform future research. The guideline recommends updated approaches to the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of cryptococcal disease, including revised guidance on induction therapy for cryptococcal meningitis, while maintaining earlier recommendations where evidence remains unchanged. It also outlines principles for implementation within a public health approach and is intended to support HIV programme managers, policy-makers, health-care professionals and people living with HIV in improving the prevention, early diagnosis and clinical management of cryptococcal disease. 8cdf895b5913.doc: WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience
8cdf895b5913.title: WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience
8cdf895b5913.content: World Health Organization (2016). WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience. World Health Organization. TitleWHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2016-11-7 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241549912 Languageen AbstractThis guideline presents the World Health Organization’s evidence-based recommendations on routine antenatal care to support a positive pregnancy experience for pregnant women and adolescent girls. It aims to provide a comprehensive, consolidated framework for antenatal care that complements existing WHO guidance on the management of specific pregnancy-related complications. The recommendations promote a person-centred, rights-based approach that extends beyond the prevention of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality to enhance women’s physical, psychological and sociocultural well-being, support healthy pregnancies, and improve the quality and utilization of antenatal care. Intended for policy-makers, programme managers and health professionals, the guideline informs the development of national policies, clinical protocols and service delivery models. Developed according to the WHO guideline development process, the document draws on systematic reviews and applies the GRADE and GRADE-CERQual approaches together with the DECIDE evidence-to-decision framework. It contains 49 recommendations covering nutritional interventions, maternal and fetal assessment, preventive measures, management of common physiological symptoms, and health system interventions to improve antenatal care utilization and quality. The guideline also introduces the 2016 WHO antenatal care model, recommending a minimum of eight contacts during pregnancy, and emphasizes implementation, dissemination and periodic updating as new evidence becomes available. a1a32368b617.doc: WHO recommendations on home-based records for maternal, newborn and child health
a1a32368b617.title: WHO recommendations on home-based records for maternal, newborn and child health
a1a32368b617.content: World Health Organization (2018). WHO recommendations on home-based records for maternal, newborn and child health. World Health Organization. TitleWHO recommendations on home-based records for maternal, newborn and child health AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2018-8-27 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241550352 Languageen AbstractThis WHO guideline provides evidence-based recommendations on the use of home-based records for maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH). Home-based records, whether paper or electronic, are household-held documents that complement facility-based records by documenting health services received and supporting continuity of care. Developed through the WHO guideline development process using systematic reviews, GRADE and GRADE-CERQual approaches, the guideline evaluates the effects of home-based records on MNCH outcomes, health service delivery, acceptability, feasibility and equity, addressing an important evidence gap despite their widespread use in at least 163 countries. The guideline recommends the use of home-based records alongside facility-based records for pregnant women, mothers, newborns and children to improve care-seeking behaviours, household support and male involvement, maternal and child home care practices, infant and child feeding, and communication between health providers and women or caregivers. It concludes that current evidence is insufficient to identify a superior record type, format or design, and advises policy-makers to engage stakeholders when determining record content and implementation. The publication also discusses implementation considerations, highlights privacy and sustainability issues, identifies research gaps, and outlines priorities for future evidence generation and guideline updates. e8fe355d40e0.title: Digital transformation handbook for health supply chain architecture
e8fe355d40e0.content: World Health Organization (2024). Digital transformation handbook for health supply chain architecture. World Health Organization. TitleDigital transformation handbook for health supply chain architecture AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2024-11-11 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240101197 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis handbook provides practical guidance for countries seeking to digitally transform public health supply chains through the development of coherent strategies, interoperable architectures and sustainable implementation approaches. Developed within the WHO SMART Guidelines framework, it addresses the growing need for integrated digital ecosystems that support forecasting, procurement, warehousing, distribution, dispensing and traceability of health products. The publication outlines the role of digital technologies in improving efficiency, data availability, interoperability and decision-making across supply chain processes, while helping ensure timely access to quality-assured medicines and health products. The publication presents a stepwise approach for defining a digital health supply chain (DHSC) strategy, assessing existing health supply chain information systems, designing a target architecture, planning implementation and supporting product traceability. It emphasizes stakeholder engagement, alignment with national health, digital health and supply chain strategies, use of open standards, and long-term scalability and sustainability. Drawing on country experiences and established digital health frameworks, the handbook offers practical tools, templates and examples to support governance, planning and coordination of digital transformation initiatives, with the aim of strengthening supply chain performance, improving visibility across the supply chain and enhancing patient safety. 6eef6f834d48.content: World Health Organization (2017). WHO recommendations on maternal health: guidelines approved by the WHO Guidelines Review Committee. World Health Organization. TitleWHO recommendations on maternal health: guidelines approved by the WHO Guidelines Review Committee AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2017-10-17 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis publication compiles WHO recommendations on maternal health that have been approved by the WHO Guidelines Review Committee into a single, accessible reference for WHO staff, policy-makers, programme managers and health professionals. It brings together current WHO guidance covering the continuum of maternal care during pregnancy, childbirth and the postnatal period, with the dual purpose of facilitating access to recommendations and helping identify areas where further guideline updates are needed. The document indicates newly issued and updated recommendations since 2013 and provides, for each recommendation, its strength, the quality of supporting evidence and the corresponding source guideline. The compilation addresses interventions to promote, prevent and protect maternal and perinatal health, including antenatal care, prevention and management of pre-eclampsia, preterm birth, peripartum infections, labour and childbirth, postpartum haemorrhage, postnatal care and health promotion, as well as the management of maternal conditions such as HIV infection, malaria and tuberculosis. Developed according to WHO’s guideline development process using the GRADE approach and structured evidence-to-decision frameworks, it presents evidence-informed recommendations intended to support consistent policy development, clinical practice and programme implementation across diverse health-care settings. 34b5b5578f58.content: World Health Organization (2022). WHO implementation tool for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) of HIV infection: module 13: integrating STI services. World Health Organization. TitleWHO implementation tool for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) of HIV infection: module 13: integrating STI services AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-9-5 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240057425 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis module of the WHO Implementation Tool for Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) of HIV Infection provides operational guidance on integrating sexually transmitted infection (STI) services into HIV PrEP programmes. Developed for programme managers, decision-makers, facility managers and health-care workers, it compiles existing WHO recommendations and evidence to support the planning, implementation and scale-up of integrated, people-centred sexual health services. The document outlines the epidemiology and burden of STIs, particularly among populations who may benefit from or use PrEP, and highlights the public health rationale for strengthening STI prevention, testing, treatment and follow-up within PrEP delivery platforms. The module describes practical approaches to integrating STI services across different service delivery models, including considerations related to workforce capacity, task sharing, monitoring, financing and demand generation. It presents guidance on counselling, health promotion, screening, diagnostic testing, partner services, clinical management, referral pathways and prevention measures such as condom provision and vaccination. Emphasizing differentiated service delivery and human rights principles, the publication aims to improve access to comprehensive sexual health care, enhance service quality and support efforts to reduce the burden of HIV and other sexually transmitted infections through coordinated and efficient health-system responses. a99f89b0ba7f.content: World Health Organization (2021). Consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery and monitoring: recommendations for a public health approach. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery and monitoring: recommendations for a public health approach AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-7-16 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240031593 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThese consolidated guidelines provide comprehensive, evidence-based recommendations for HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery and programme monitoring across the continuum of HIV care. Updating the 2016 WHO consolidated guidelines, this edition integrates guidance issued between 2016 and 2021 and reflects major advances in clinical practice, diagnostics and service delivery. Developed using the GRADE approach and informed by expert consultation and country experience, the guidelines aim to support countries in implementing high-quality, person-centred HIV services while advancing universal health coverage and progress towards ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030. The publication addresses HIV testing strategies, prevention interventions, antiretroviral therapy, management of advanced HIV disease, care for common coinfections and comorbidities, differentiated service delivery, procurement, laboratory services and programme monitoring. It incorporates updated recommendations on HIV self-testing, pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis, dolutegravir-based treatment, rapid antiretroviral therapy initiation, viral load monitoring and community-based models of care. Intended primarily for national HIV programme managers, policy-makers and health-care providers, the guidelines also serve as a resource for technical partners, community organizations and people living with HIV to support the implementation of effective, equitable and people-centred HIV programmes. f6865ef2315c.title: Lignes directrices de l’OMS : recommandations sur les interventions numériques pour le renforcement des systèmes de s…
f6865ef2315c.content: Organisation mondiale de la Santé (2022). Lignes directrices de l'OMS : recommandations sur les interventions numériques pour le renforcement des systèmes de santé. Organisation mondiale de la Santé. TitleLignes directrices de l'OMS : recommandations sur les interventions numériques pour le renforcement des systèmes de santé AuthorsOrganisation mondiale de la Santé Issued2022-5-19 Typebook PublisherOrganisation mondiale de la Santé ISBN9789240046641 (version électronique) Languagefr AbstractCes lignes directrices de l’OMS présentent des recommandations fondées sur des données probantes concernant l’utilisation des interventions numériques pour renforcer les systèmes de santé et soutenir les progrès vers la couverture sanitaire universelle (CSU). Élaborées en réponse à l’adoption croissante des technologies numériques et à la résolution sur la santé numérique approuvée par l’Assemblée mondiale de la Santé en 2018, elles répondent à la nécessité d’évaluer rigoureusement les interventions de santé numérique afin que les investissements reposent sur des données probantes relatives à leurs avantages, leurs inconvénients, leur acceptabilité, leur faisabilité, leurs implications en matière de ressources et les considérations d’équité. Les lignes directrices soulignent que les technologies numériques doivent compléter, et non remplacer, les composantes fondamentales de systèmes de santé performants. Les recommandations portent sur un ensemble prioritaire d’interventions de santé numérique, principalement accessibles au moyen d’appareils mobiles, notamment la notification des naissances et des décès, la notification des stocks et la gestion des produits de base, la télémédecine entre client et prestataire ainsi qu’entre prestataires, la communication ciblée avec les clients, le suivi numérique de l’état de santé et des services reçus, les outils d’aide à la décision destinés aux professionnels de santé et l’apprentissage numérique. Les lignes directrices présentent également des considérations relatives à la mise en œuvre, recensent les principales lacunes en matière de recherche et visent à aider les ministères de la santé, les responsables des politiques de santé, les professionnels de santé, les partenaires du développement et les autres parties prenantes à prendre des décisions éclairées concernant l’adoption, le déploiement à grande échelle et l’institutionnalisation des interventions de santé numérique efficaces. ea2a2bc8da98.content: World Health Organization (2024). Digital adaptation kit for immunizations: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems. World Health Organization. TitleDigital adaptation kit for immunizations: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2024-12-31 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240099456 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis publication presents the World Health Organization’s digital adaptation kit (DAK) for immunizations, developed within the SMART Guidelines framework to support the implementation of WHO immunization recommendations in digital systems. The document provides operational and software-neutral specifications intended to facilitate the translation of immunization guidance into interoperable digital health applications, particularly person-centred point-of-service systems and electronic immunization registries. It outlines the role of digital adaptation kits in strengthening digital health systems by improving the consistency, transparency and standardization of health content, workflows, data structures and decision-support logic used in immunization programmes. The publication also situates the DAK within broader digital health strategies and interoperability standards. The document describes eight core components of the immunization DAK, including health interventions and recommendations, generic personas, user scenarios, workflows, core data elements, decision-support logic, indicators and functional requirements. It incorporates WHO guidance related to routine immunization, electronic immunization registries and digital health interventions, while emphasizing adaptability to country-specific policies and implementation contexts. Additional sections address interoperability, data standards, workflow optimization and the use of digital systems to support longitudinal tracking, reporting, decision support and communication within immunization services. The publication is intended for immunization programme managers, digital health teams, software developers and implementers involved in designing and deploying digital immunization systems. f735ecaf0245.content: World Health Organization (2020). WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 1: prevention: tuberculosis preventive treatment. World Health Organization. TitleWHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 1: prevention: tuberculosis preventive treatment AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2020-2-25 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240001503 Languageen AbstractThis guideline provides updated WHO recommendations for the programmatic management of tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) as part of the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis. It focuses on the prevention of active tuberculosis among people at increased risk of disease progression, particularly people living with HIV, household contacts of patients with tuberculosis and other vulnerable population groups. The document incorporates new evidence on shorter rifamycin-containing preventive treatment regimens and updates previous WHO guidance to improve the clarity, consistency and global applicability of recommendations. Developed in accordance with WHO Guideline Review Committee requirements, the publication presents 18 evidence-based recommendations covering the identification of populations eligible for preventive treatment, exclusion of active tuberculosis, testing for latent tuberculosis infection, recommended preventive treatment regimens, monitoring and evaluation, and implementation considerations. Recommendations were formulated using the GRADE approach, taking into account the certainty of evidence, effectiveness, safety, values and preferences, equity, resource implications, acceptability and feasibility. The guideline is intended to support national policy-makers, programme managers and health-care providers in strengthening tuberculosis prevention and advancing implementation of the WHO End TB Strategy. ab26c09f302b.content: World Health Organization (2025). Digital transformation handbook for health product catalogue. World Health Organization. TitleDigital transformation handbook for health product catalogue AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2025-10-30 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis handbook provides guidance for the implementation of standardized product master data management through national product catalogues (NPCs) to support digital transformation in health supply chains. Developed within the framework of the WHO Digital Implementation Investment Guide and aligned with the SMART Guidelines initiative, the publication outlines regulatory, governance, technological and operational approaches for establishing interoperable product registries and harmonized product information systems. It explains the importance of standardized product master data for ensuring accurate identification, tracking and management of health products across manufacturers, regulatory authorities, procurement entities, warehouses, health facilities and other supply chain stakeholders. The handbook describes policies and procedures for data governance, coding structures, interoperability standards, change management and capacity-building to support sustainable implementation. It also presents guidance on integrating standardized product master data with digital health, regulatory and supply chain systems to improve forecasting, procurement, inventory management, pharmacovigilance, product recalls and traceability. In addition, the publication highlights mechanisms for sharing product master data as a global good and leveraging WHO-hosted tools and open standards to strengthen coordination, data quality and supply chain efficiency across countries and organizations. 9c1f833ec122.doc: Consolidated guidelines on HIV, viral hepatitis and STI prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care for key populations
9c1f833ec122.title: Consolidated guidelines on HIV, viral hepatitis and STI prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care for key populations
9c1f833ec122.content: World Health Organization (2022). Consolidated guidelines on HIV, viral hepatitis and STI prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care for key populations. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated guidelines on HIV, viral hepatitis and STI prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care for key populations AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-7-22 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240052390 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guideline provides consolidated, evidence-based recommendations for the prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care of HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) among key populations. It responds to the disproportionate burden of these infections in groups such as men who have sex with men, sex workers, people who inject drugs, people in prisons and other closed settings, and trans and gender diverse individuals, and to the structural barriers that limit their access to health services. The document aims to support countries in strengthening integrated, people-centred responses to these interconnected epidemics. Developed using WHO guideline standards and the GRADE methodology, the publication brings together existing and new recommendations and organizes them into comprehensive packages of interventions. It addresses enabling factors such as legal and policy environments, stigma, discrimination, violence and community empowerment, alongside essential health interventions including prevention, testing, treatment and harm reduction. The guideline also outlines service delivery approaches, such as community-led services, integration and decentralization, and provides guidance for programme planning, implementation and monitoring. Intended for policy-makers, programme managers and health-care providers, it supports the prioritization of effective, context-appropriate strategies to improve access, coverage and health outcomes for key populations. TitleDigital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing: WHO recommendations in digital systems: web annex A: data dictionary AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-12-14 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis web annex provides the standardized data dictionary supporting the WHO Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems. It defines the core data elements required to implement WHO recommendations across HIV prevention, testing, treatment, care, diagnostics, referral, follow-up and reporting workflows in digital health systems. The annex specifies standardized data element names, definitions, data types, permissible values, calculated fields, coding structures and unique identifiers to support consistent data capture, interoperability and alignment with international terminology standards. Organized according to the business processes described in the digital adaptation kit, it also includes guidance on adapting the data dictionary to national programme requirements while preserving standardized information exchange. Intended for digital health architects, software developers, implementers and programme managers, this resource provides a practical foundation for configuring, customizing and maintaining interoperable HIV information systems that accurately reflect WHO recommendations. TitleNational health workforce accounts: health workforce levels and trends 2026 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2026-6-22 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240122925 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis report presents the 2026 edition of the National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) series, providing an overview of the status of NHWA implementation and an analysis of global and regional health workforce levels and trends based on official data reported by countries to the World Health Organization. Developed to support evidence-informed health workforce policy-making and planning, the report examines progress in strengthening national health workforce information systems, data availability and reporting across countries, and the use of standardized indicators to monitor human resources for health in support of universal health coverage, the Sustainable Development Goals and other health objectives. Drawing on the 2025 NHWA data release, the report analyses the distribution, density and composition of the health and care workforce across regions and income groups, highlighting persistent disparities in workforce availability. It also examines trends in workforce growth since 2006 and presents a thematic analysis of population ageing and health workforce ageing, assessing their implications for future workforce needs. The findings demonstrate substantial improvements in the availability and quality of health workforce data through NHWA implementation while underscoring continuing challenges related to workforce shortages, inequities in distribution and the need for sustained investment in health workforce planning and monitoring. e6b63e8dd6b5.title: Guidelines for the prevention and control of infection with LAV/HTLV III
e6b63e8dd6b5.content: World Health Organization. Control Programme on AIDS (1986). Guidelines for the prevention and control of infection with LAV/HTLV III. World Health Organization. TitleGuidelines for the prevention and control of infection with LAV/HTLV III AuthorsWorld Health Organization. Control Programme on AIDS Issued1986-12-31 Typedocument PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThese guidelines provide recommendations for preventing and controlling infection with LAV/HTLV-III, the retrovirus recognized at the time as the etiological agent of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). Developed as part of the WHO AIDS Control Programme, they are intended primarily for public health authorities and health professionals, who are responsible for adapting the guidance to different populations and settings. The document summarizes available knowledge on transmission, clinical manifestations, laboratory detection, surveillance, notification and confidentiality, and case definitions for AIDS. The guidelines emphasize routine precautions to prevent exposure to blood and other potentially infectious body fluids, particularly among health care workers, laboratory personnel and providers of home and emergency care. They address prevention and management of needlestick, parenteral and mucous-membrane exposures, safe handling of specimens and contaminated equipment, and precautions for non-health-care workers. Guidance is also provided on disinfection, sterilization, and the safe processing of reusable needles, syringes and other instruments. c8e84d71075c.doc: Directriz de la OMS: recomendaciones sobre intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud
c8e84d71075c.title: Directriz de la OMS: recomendaciones sobre intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud
c8e84d71075c.content: Organización Mundial de la Salud (2022). Directriz de la OMS: recomendaciones sobre intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud. Organización Mundial de la Salud. TitleDirectriz de la OMS: recomendaciones sobre intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud AuthorsOrganización Mundial de la Salud Issued2022-5-19 Typebook PublisherOrganización Mundial de la Salud ISBN9789240046993 (versión electrónica) Languagees AbstractEste documento presenta las recomendaciones de la OMS, basadas en la evidencia, sobre el uso de intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud y apoyar el avance hacia la cobertura sanitaria universal (CSU). Elaborada en respuesta a la creciente adopción de las tecnologías digitales y a la resolución sobre salud digital aprobada por la Asamblea Mundial de la Salud en 2018, la directriz aborda la necesidad de evaluar rigurosamente las intervenciones de salud digital para garantizar que las inversiones se fundamenten en evidencia sobre sus beneficios, riesgos, aceptabilidad, factibilidad, implicaciones en materia de recursos y consideraciones de equidad. Asimismo, subraya que las tecnologías digitales deben complementar, y no sustituir, los componentes fundamentales de unos sistemas de salud sólidos y eficaces. Las recomendaciones se centran en un conjunto priorizado de intervenciones de salud digital accesibles, como mínimo, mediante dispositivos móviles, entre ellas la notificación de nacimientos y defunciones, la notificación de existencias y la gestión de suministros, la telemedicina entre pacientes y profesionales y entre profesionales, la comunicación dirigida a los pacientes, el seguimiento digital del estado de salud y de los servicios recibidos, las herramientas de apoyo a la toma de decisiones para el personal sanitario y el aprendizaje digital para los trabajadores de la salud. La directriz también presenta consideraciones para la implementación, identifica las principales lagunas de investigación y proporciona orientación a los ministerios de salud, los responsables de salud pública, los asociados para el desarrollo y otras partes interesadas para adoptar, ampliar e institucionalizar intervenciones de salud digital eficaces sobre la base de la mejor evidencia disponible. 25e796b50846.doc: Consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services, 2019
25e796b50846.title: Consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services, 2019
25e796b50846.content: World Health Organization (2020). Consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services, 2019. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated guidelines on HIV testing services, 2019 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2020-11-3 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241550581 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guideline provides comprehensive, evidence-based recommendations to support countries in delivering high-quality, person-centred HIV testing services (HTS) across diverse populations and settings. Updating and consolidating previous WHO guidance issued in 2015 and 2016, it incorporates new evidence on HIV self-testing, social network-based HIV testing approaches, western blotting, and strategic service delivery to strengthen progress towards global HIV targets. Developed using the GRADE methodology and informed by systematic reviews, modelling studies and expert consultation, the guideline aims to improve the effectiveness, efficiency and quality of HIV testing while promoting timely linkage to prevention, treatment and care. The publication addresses the full continuum of HIV testing services, including demand creation, pre- and post-test services, facility- and community-based testing, implementation considerations for priority populations, strategic planning, diagnostic testing strategies, quality assurance and programme monitoring. It provides updated recommendations on HIV self-testing, provider-assisted referral, social network-based approaches and the use of dual HIV/syphilis rapid diagnostic tests, while emphasizing the WHO 5Cs of HIV testing services: consent, confidentiality, counselling, correct results and connection. Intended for policy-makers, national programme managers, health-care providers and implementing partners, the guideline supports the expansion of equitable, evidence-informed HIV testing services to improve diagnosis and strengthen national HIV responses. aea84d2fc2d8.title: Guidelines: updated recommendations on HIV prevention, infant diagnosis, antiretroviral initiation and monitoring
aea84d2fc2d8.content: World Health Organization (2021). Guidelines: updated recommendations on HIV prevention, infant diagnosis, antiretroviral initiation and monitoring. World Health Organization. TitleGuidelines: updated recommendations on HIV prevention, infant diagnosis, antiretroviral initiation and monitoring AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-3-17 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240022232 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guideline presents updated WHO recommendations on selected priority areas across the HIV prevention, diagnosis and treatment continuum, developed in response to emerging evidence, implementation experience and evolving clinical practice. Prepared according to WHO Guideline Review Committee procedures and informed by systematic reviews using the GRADE approach, it updates and complements the 2016 consolidated HIV guidelines. The publication addresses key public health challenges affecting the global HIV response, particularly in resource-limited settings, and supports progress towards ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030 through a public health approach to service delivery. The guideline introduces or updates recommendations on the use of the dapivirine vaginal ring as an additional HIV prevention option for women at substantial risk of infection, point-of-care technologies for infant HIV diagnosis and viral load monitoring, revised treatment monitoring algorithms, and earlier initiation of antiretroviral therapy for people living with HIV and tuberculosis. It also provides updated clinical considerations for rapid antiretroviral therapy initiation and outlines implementation principles to support national adaptation. Intended for policy-makers, programme managers, clinicians and implementing partners, the guideline aims to strengthen evidence-based HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment monitoring and care across diverse settings. 54106017452e.content: World Health Organization (2021). Global guidance on criteria and processes for validation: elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B virus. World Health Organization. TitleGlobal guidance on criteria and processes for validation: elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B virus AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-11-25 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240039360 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guidance document provides updated World Health Organization criteria and processes for validating the elimination of mother-to-child transmission (EMTCT) of HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B virus (HBV) as public health priorities. Building on previous editions focused on HIV and syphilis, this third version incorporates validation guidance for HBV within the framework of the Triple Elimination Initiative. The document outlines standardized indicators, targets and assessment procedures for evaluating progress towards EMTCT across diverse epidemiological and programmatic settings. It addresses impact and process indicators, surveillance and laboratory quality standards, programme assessment, and requirements related to human rights, gender equality and community engagement. The document emphasizes integrated maternal and child health approaches, universal access to quality antenatal and prevention services, and the importance of strong health systems and surveillance mechanisms. It also provides guidance for countries with high disease burdens through the Path to Elimination framework, as well as for countries with small numbers of affected pregnant women and special populations. Intended for national, regional and global validation bodies, the document supports harmonized validation processes while allowing countries to pursue single, dual or triple EMTCT validation according to national readiness and regional priorities. 6cc7f938d486.doc: WHO guideline for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions for cervical cancer prevention
6cc7f938d486.title: WHO guideline for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions for cervical cancer prevention
6cc7f938d486.content: World Health Organization (2021). WHO guideline for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions for cervical cancer prevention. World Health Organization. TitleWHO guideline for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions for cervical cancer prevention AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-7-6 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240030824 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis second edition of the WHO guideline provides updated evidence-based recommendations for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions to prevent cervical cancer in both the general population of women and women living with HIV. Developed in support of the WHO global strategy to eliminate cervical cancer as a public health problem, the guideline responds to advances in screening technologies and implementation approaches by updating previous recommendations and introducing new guidance to simplify clinical algorithms while improving feasibility, acceptability and programme performance across diverse health system settings. The recommendations were developed in accordance with WHO guideline development procedures using systematic reviews, mathematical modelling where necessary, GRADE assessments of the certainty of evidence, evidence-to-decision frameworks, and consideration of feasibility, costs, acceptability and users’ values and preferences. The guideline presents recommendations and good practice statements on primary screening tests, screening intervals, age at initiation and cessation of screening, triage strategies, follow-up after positive screening results, treatment approaches, and programme implementation for both population groups. It addresses service delivery, integration with HIV care, implementation considerations, research gaps and dissemination, while emphasizing the transition to HPV DNA testing, the use of evidence-based screening and treatment algorithms, and country adaptation according to available resources and local context to improve coverage, quality of care and cervical cancer prevention. b8007fdd6041.content: World Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe (2008). 8th National Tuberculosis Programme Managers Meeting and 13th Wolfheze Workshop: Wolfheze 2008: tuberculosis management, surveillance and evaluation in Europe with high rates or threat of multidrug resistant tuberculosis: The Hague, the Netherlands, 1–2 June 2008. World Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe. Title8th National Tuberculosis Programme Managers Meeting and 13th Wolfheze Workshop: Wolfheze 2008: tuberculosis management, surveillance and evaluation in Europe with high rates or threat of multidrug resistant tuberculosis: The Hague, the Netherlands, 1–2 June 2008 AuthorsWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe Issued2008-12-31 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe Languageen AbstractThe WHO European Region has the highest rates in the world of drug-resistant tuberculosis and increasing rates of HIV/tuberculosis coinfection. Eighteen high-priority countries have been identified to urgently scale up tuberculosis control interventions: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bulgaria, Estonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Lithuania, the Republic of Moldova, Romania, the Russian Federation, Tajikistan, Turkey, Turkmenistan, Ukraine and Uzbekistan. Five of these countries are members of the European Union. Migration and pockets of poverty increase vulnerability to tuberculosis in many western European countries. Related areas, such as the rapid detection of drug-resistant tuberculosis, contact tracing, infection control, health system strengthening and the review of national tuberculosis programmes, are of equal concern among eastern, central and western countries of the WHO European Region. While general awareness and political commitment were raised during the Ministerial Forum held in Berlin in October 2007, how to ensure the follow-up of the Berlin Declaration on TB and monitor its implementation is currently under discussion. The 8th National Tuberculosis Programme Managers Meeting and the 13th Wolfheze Workshop, jointly organized in June 2008 in The Hague, provided a forum for discussion on each of the aforementioned topics and facilitated the sharing of experiences between countries in the Region – which are very different from an epidemiological, organizational, cultural and wealth perspective. 50b0f37c192a.content: World Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe (2014). The case for investing in public health: the strengthening public health services and capacity. A key pillar of the European regional health policy framework Health 2020. World Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe. TitleThe case for investing in public health: the strengthening public health services and capacity. A key pillar of the European regional health policy framework Health 2020 AuthorsWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe Issued2014-12-31 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe Languageen AbstractThe economic crisis has led to increased demand and reduced resources for health sectors. The trend for increasing healthcare costs to individuals, the health sector and wider society is significant. Public health can be part of the solution to this challenge. The evidence shows that prevention can be cost-effective, provide value for money andgive returns on investment in both the short and longer terms. This public health summary outlines quick returns on investment for health and other sectors for interventions that promote physical activity and healthy employment; address housing and mental health; and reduce road traffic injuries and violence. Vaccinations and screening programmes are largely cost-effective. Population-level approaches are estimated to cost on average five times less than individual interventions. This report gives examples of interventions with early returns on investment and approaches with longer-term gains. Investing in cost-effective interventions to reduce costs to the health sector and other sectors can help create sustainable health systems and economies for the future. 21887899ceb6.title: WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents
21887899ceb6.content: World Health Organization (2022). WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents. World Health Organization. TitleWHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-3-18 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240046832 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis operational handbook provides practical guidance for implementing World Health Organization recommendations on the prevention, screening, diagnosis and management of tuberculosis (TB) in children and adolescents under programmatic conditions and across different levels of the health system. Developed alongside the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, the publication addresses the specific epidemiological, clinical and psychosocial vulnerabilities of children and adolescents affected by TB, including challenges related to diagnosis, treatment adherence, prevention and continuity of care. The handbook aims to support the development and revision of national policies, operational guidance and service delivery approaches tailored to the needs of these populations. The handbook covers the full continuum of TB care, including contact investigation, systematic screening, preventive treatment, diagnostic approaches for pulmonary and extrapulmonary TB, and treatment of drug-susceptible and drug-resistant disease. It also addresses decentralized and family-centred models of care, management of TB in children and adolescents living with HIV, TB during pregnancy, malnutrition, pneumonia, adolescent health needs and palliative care. Practical tools, implementation guidance and standard operating procedures are included to support programme managers and health-care providers in strengthening child and adolescent TB services. e37eef3efa18.doc: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 2: screening: systematic screening for tuberculosis disease
e37eef3efa18.title: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 2: screening: systematic screening for tuberculosis disease
e37eef3efa18.content: World Health Organization (2021). WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 2: screening: systematic screening for tuberculosis disease. World Health Organization. TitleWHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 2: screening: systematic screening for tuberculosis disease AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-3-22 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240022676 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractTuberculosis remains one of the leading causes of death from a single infectious agent despite being largely preventable and curable. This updated WHO guideline provides evidence-based recommendations on systematic screening for tuberculosis disease to support earlier diagnosis, timely initiation of treatment and reduced transmission. It revises the 2013 guidance in light of new evidence on the effectiveness of screening interventions and the performance of screening tools, using the GRADE approach to assess the certainty of evidence and the strength of recommendations. The document is intended to assist countries in planning and implementing screening strategies adapted to their epidemiological and health system contexts. The guideline presents recommendations for systematic screening in the general population and in groups at increased risk of tuberculosis, including people living with HIV, household contacts, prisoners, miners, migrants and other vulnerable populations. It also reviews the use of symptom screening, chest radiography, computer-aided detection software, C-reactive protein and molecular WHO-recommended rapid diagnostic tests as screening tools, together with guidance on monitoring, evaluation and implementation considerations. The publication identifies research gaps and is accompanied by an operational handbook providing practical guidance for applying the recommendations in national tuberculosis programmes. 87d0ee7a2921.doc: Consolidated guidelines on person-centred HIV strategic information: strengthening routine data for impact
87d0ee7a2921.title: Consolidated guidelines on person-centred HIV strategic information: strengthening routine data for impact
87d0ee7a2921.content: World Health Organization (2022). Consolidated guidelines on person-centred HIV strategic information: strengthening routine data for impact. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated guidelines on person-centred HIV strategic information: strengthening routine data for impact AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-7-28 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240055315 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThese consolidated guidelines provide normative guidance for strengthening HIV strategic information through person-centred routine data systems that support both clinical care and programme management. Developed in response to persistent gaps in HIV prevention, testing, treatment and retention despite substantial progress in the global HIV response, the guidelines promote the collection and use of individual-level longitudinal data to improve continuity of care, strengthen linkage across services and enhance monitoring of programme performance. They consolidate and update previous WHO guidance while introducing recommendations on person-centred monitoring, digital health information systems, interoperability, data quality, surveillance and the integration of HIV services with tuberculosis, viral hepatitis, sexually transmitted infections and other related conditions. The publication outlines recommendations and operational guidance on HIV prevention monitoring, patient monitoring, surveillance, digital health data, routine data use, priority indicators and implementation considerations. It emphasizes the transition from aggregate reporting to person-centred, digital information systems that support clinical decision-making, programme improvement and public health action while ensuring data privacy, confidentiality and security. The guidelines also describe minimum datasets, standardized monitoring tools and approaches to improving data quality and using routine information to strengthen service delivery and measure progress towards global HIV targets. 0929587156a9.content: World Health Organization (2012). WHO recommendations: optimizing health worker roles to improve access to key maternal and newborn health interventions through task shifting. World Health Organization. TitleWHO recommendations: optimizing health worker roles to improve access to key maternal and newborn health interventions through task shifting AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2012-12-19 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241504843 Languageen AbstractThis WHO guidance provides evidence-based recommendations on optimizing health worker roles through task shifting to improve universal access to key maternal and newborn health interventions. Developed in response to health workforce shortages and inequities in access to care, it assesses whether specific interventions can be delivered safely and effectively by different health worker cadres, including lay health workers, auxiliary nurses and nurse midwives, nurses, midwives, associate clinicians, advanced level associate clinicians and non-specialist doctors. The guidance presents 119 recommendations, ranging from practices recommended for implementation to those requiring targeted monitoring and evaluation, rigorous research, or not recommended. It emphasizes that task shifting should complement efforts to increase skilled care and should aim to expand access while maintaining safety. Implementation should consider health-system capacity and local sociocultural, political and financial conditions, with recommendations adapted through national dialogue and considered as packages of interventions rather than in isolation. 1d77673f03b4.doc: The use of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (TB-LAMP) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis: policy guidance
1d77673f03b4.title: The use of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (TB-LAMP) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis: policy guidance
1d77673f03b4.content: World Health Organization (2016). The use of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (TB-LAMP) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis: policy guidance. World Health Organization. TitleThe use of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (TB-LAMP) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis: policy guidance AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2016-8-8 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241511186 Languageen AbstractTuberculosis remains a major global public health challenge, and the WHO End TB Strategy emphasizes the need for early diagnosis and universal drug-susceptibility testing. This policy guidance presents evidence-based recommendations on the use of the commercial loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay (TB-LAMP) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis. Developed following a systematic review of studies conducted since 2012 and assessment using the GRADE approach, the document evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of TB-LAMP as a replacement for sputum-smear microscopy, as an add-on test after negative smear microscopy, and in comparison with the Xpert MTB/RIF assay, while also assessing the frequency of indeterminate or invalid results. Based on the available evidence, WHO recommends that TB-LAMP may be used as a replacement for sputum-smear microscopy in adults with signs and symptoms of pulmonary tuberculosis and as a follow-on test when further investigation of smear-negative specimens is required. The guidance emphasizes that these conditional recommendations are based on very low-quality evidence, apply to sputum specimens from patients with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis, and should not replace rapid molecular tests capable of detecting rifampicin resistance. It also highlights the limited evidence for use in people living with HIV, notes the extrapolation of recommendations to children, and provides implementation considerations and priorities for future research. 9d7b8d752a0a.content: منظمة الصحة العالمية (2024). تصنيف التدخلات والخدمات والتطبيقات الرقمية في مجال الصحة: لغة مشتركة لوصف استخدامات التكنولوجيا الرقمية من أجل الصحة. منظمة الصحة العالمية. Titleتصنيف التدخلات والخدمات والتطبيقات الرقمية في مجال الصحة: لغة مشتركة لوصف استخدامات التكنولوجيا الرقمية من أجل الصحة Authorsمنظمة الصحة العالمية Issued2024-10-8 Typebook Publisherمنظمة الصحة العالمية ISBN9789240093768 (نسخة إلكترونية) Languagear Abstractتقدم هذه الطبعة الثانية من «تصنيف التدخلات والخدمات والتطبيقات الرقمية في مجال الصحة» تصنيفاً معيارياً يصف كيفية استخدام التقنيات الرقمية لتلبية احتياجات الأفراد والنظم الصحية. وقد أعدت منظمة الصحة العالمية هذا التصنيف ليكون لغة مشتركة تدعم التواصل بين صانعي السياسات، ومديري البرامج الصحية، والباحثين، والمنفذين، ومطوري التكنولوجيا، وغيرهم من أصحاب المصلحة في مجال الصحة الرقمية. وينظم التصنيف التدخلات الصحية الرقمية حول قدرات تكنولوجية محددة صُممت لمعالجة التحديات التي تواجه النظم الصحية، ويربط هذه التدخلات بالخدمات وأنواع التطبيقات الرقمية التي تُستخدم لتنفيذها. ويُحدِّث هذا المنشور ويوسِّع الطبعة الأولى الصادرة عام 2018 ليعكس التقدم في تقنيات الصحة الرقمية، وتطور ممارسات التنفيذ، والدروس المستفادة من استخدامها على المستوى العالمي. ويستند الإطار إلى ثلاثة محاور مترابطة: تحديات النظم الصحية، والتدخلات الصحية الرقمية، والخدمات وأنواع التطبيقات الرقمية. ويشمل تدخلات موجهة للأفراد، ولمقدمي الرعاية الصحية، ولمديري النظم الصحية، ولخدمات البيانات، إلى جانب فئات التطبيقات الرقمية ونظم المعلومات. ويهدف هذا التصنيف إلى دعم التخطيط والتنفيذ، وتحليل الاستثمارات، والبحوث، واعتبارات التشغيل البيني، وصياغة السياسات، وحوكمة مبادرات الصحة الرقمية، بما يعزز الاستخدام المنسق والفعال للتقنيات الرقمية في النظم الصحية. d6249cef1d6c.title: Global hepatitis report 2026
d6249cef1d6c.content: World Health Organization (2026). Global hepatitis report 2026. World Health Organization. TitleGlobal hepatitis report 2026 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2026-4-24 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240122383 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis report provides a comprehensive assessment of the global burden of viral hepatitis and progress towards the goal of eliminating hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030. Drawing on data reported by Member States and modelled estimates, it analyses trends in incidence, prevalence and mortality associated with hepatitis B and C, covering the period from 2015 to 2024 based on the latest available data. It also situates these trends within the context of global commitments, strategies and targets. The publication reviews the coverage and impact of key interventions for prevention, diagnosis and treatment, including vaccination, infection prevention and control, harm reduction and access to antiviral therapies. It identifies persistent gaps in testing and treatment, marked regional disparities, and the need for accelerated scale-up of services, particularly in high-burden settings. The report concludes that progress towards the 2030 elimination targets remains off track despite the availability of effective interventions. Intended for policymakers, programme managers and public health stakeholders, it serves as an analytical and strategic resource to guide national and global responses to viral hepatitis. b746f2da6684.title: WHO guidelines for screening and treatment of precancerous lesions for cervical cancer prevention
b746f2da6684.content: World Health Organization (2013). WHO guidelines for screening and treatment of precancerous lesions for cervical cancer prevention. World Health Organization. TitleWHO guidelines for screening and treatment of precancerous lesions for cervical cancer prevention AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2013-11-19 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241548694 Languageen AbstractThese guidelines provide recommendations for screen-and-treat strategies to prevent cervical cancer by detecting and treating precancerous cervical lesions. The screen-and-treat approach bases treatment decisions on screening results, allowing treatment soon or ideally immediately after a positive test, rather than requiring histological confirmation. The guidelines compare strategies using human papillomavirus (HPV) testing, visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), and cytology, linked to treatment with cryotherapy or loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). They are intended primarily to support policy-makers, programme managers and other health professionals in selecting appropriate cervical cancer prevention strategies according to available resources and existing programmes. Nine recommendations are provided. HPV-based screening is generally preferred where feasible, while VIA is suggested where HPV testing is not feasible; cold knife conization is not recommended as part of a screen-and-treat strategy. Recommendations apply to all women, with specific guidance for women living with HIV. Decision-making and implementation flowcharts support adaptation of the recommended strategies to country and regional contexts. 0b12cfe55a29.doc: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 3: diagnosis: web annex B: evidence synthesis and analysis
0b12cfe55a29.title: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 3: diagnosis: web annex B: evidence synthesis and analysis
0b12cfe55a29.content: World Health Organization (2025). WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 3: diagnosis: web annex B: evidence synthesis and analysis. World Health Organization. TitleWHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 3: diagnosis: web annex B: evidence synthesis and analysis AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2025-4-10 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization DOIhttps://doi.org/10.2471/B09341 Languageen AbstractThis web annex to the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, Module 3: Diagnosis, compiles the evidence synthesis and analyses used to inform WHO recommendations on diagnostic technologies for tuberculosis and drug-resistant tuberculosis. The publication presents systematic reviews, meta-analyses, qualitative evidence syntheses and economic evaluations examining the diagnostic accuracy, safety, cost–effectiveness and implementation considerations of multiple diagnostic approaches, including low- and moderate-complexity nucleic acid amplification tests, targeted next-generation sequencing technologies and Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen-based skin tests. The annex describes the methods applied to identify, assess and synthesize evidence across diverse populations and settings, including adults, adolescents, children and people living with HIV. It addresses the detection of pulmonary and extrapulmonary tuberculosis, rifampicin resistance and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis using respiratory and non-respiratory specimens. The document also examines stakeholder and user perspectives, operational feasibility and factors influencing implementation. Developed in accordance with WHO guideline development standards, the annex provides the technical evidence base underpinning updates to WHO policy guidance on tuberculosis diagnosis and drug-resistance testing. cf8d8bf3aa71.doc: WHO guideline: recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening
cf8d8bf3aa71.title: WHO guideline: recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening
cf8d8bf3aa71.content: World Health Organization (2019). WHO guideline: recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening. World Health Organization. TitleWHO guideline: recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2019-4-16 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241550505 Languageen AbstractThis WHO guideline provides evidence-based recommendations on the use of digital interventions to strengthen health systems and support progress towards universal health coverage (UHC). Developed in response to the growing adoption of digital technologies and the 2018 World Health Assembly resolution on digital health, it addresses the need for rigorous evaluation of digital health interventions to ensure that investments are informed by evidence of their benefits, harms, acceptability, feasibility, resource implications and equity considerations. The guideline emphasizes that digital technologies should complement, rather than replace, the fundamental components of well-functioning health systems. The recommendations focus on a prioritized set of digital health interventions accessible at a minimum through mobile devices, including birth and death notification, stock notification and commodity management, client-to-provider and provider-to-provider telemedicine, targeted client communication, digital tracking of clients’ health status and services, health worker decision support, and digital learning for health workers. The guideline also outlines implementation considerations, identifies research gaps, and supports ministries of health, public health practitioners, development partners and other stakeholders in making evidence-based decisions on the adoption, scale-up and institutionalization of effective digital health interventions. TitleToolkit for analysis and use of routine health facility data: integrated health services analysis: district and facility level AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-6-16 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240060609 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guidance document, part of the WHO Toolkit for analysis and use of routine health facility data, provides practical guidance on the integrated analysis and use of routine health information system (RHIS) data at district and health facility levels. It is intended to support managers, analysts and other health system stakeholders in monitoring health service delivery and using routine data for operational decision-making. The document promotes an integrated, standards-based approach that uses a limited set of tracer indicators representing multiple programmes and service components, thereby supporting primary health care, universal health coverage and the health-related Sustainable Development Goals. The publication presents principles for RHIS data analysis, including integration across programmes, focused use of key indicators, standardization of analyses and visualizations, routine assessment of data quality, and purpose-oriented use of information for management and planning. It organizes indicators into three groups: health status and epidemiological profile, health service performance, and health service resources. For each group, the publication provides indicator definitions, metadata, recommended disaggregations, analytical approaches, and examples of dashboards and visualizations. It emphasizes the interpretation of routine data within local contexts and illustrates how standardized dashboards can support supervision, performance review, resource allocation and continuous improvement of health services at subnational levels.
