15d7cba6ea93.doc: National health workforce accounts: implementation guide
15d7cba6ea93.title: National health workforce accounts: implementation guide
15d7cba6ea93.content: World Health Organization (2018). National health workforce accounts: implementation guide. World Health Organization. TitleNational health workforce accounts: implementation guide AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2018-10-19 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241514446 Languageen AbstractThe National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) Implementation Guide provides practical guidance for countries on establishing and sustaining systems to collect, analyse, use and report standardized health workforce data. Developed as a companion document to the NHWA Handbook and in support of the Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030, the guide outlines a structured approach to strengthening health workforce information systems and improving the availability, quality and use of human resources for health data. It is intended for policy-makers, programme managers, technical experts and stakeholders involved in health workforce planning, monitoring and governance, and emphasizes collaboration across sectors such as health, education, labour, finance and statistics. The guide presents an implementation framework organized into three phases—conceptualization, operationalization, and scaling up and sustainability—comprising eight steps that address political commitment, governance arrangements, planning, legal considerations, data compilation and analysis, validation, dissemination, and process review. It describes the roles of national institutions and multistakeholder coordination mechanisms, provides guidance on data quality, reporting and communication processes, and promotes the integration of existing information systems. By supporting the systematic monitoring of health workforce indicators, the guide aims to strengthen evidence-informed decision-making and contribute to health workforce development, universal health coverage and broader national and global health objectives. 28101b61bb68.content: World Health Organization (2023). Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing: WHO recommendations in digital systems: web annex D: function and non-functional requirements. World Health Organization. TitleDigital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing: WHO recommendations in digital systems: web annex D: function and non-functional requirements AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-12-14 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis web annex provides the high-level functional and non-functional requirements supporting the WHO Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems. It translates WHO HIV recommendations and service delivery workflows into standardized system requirements to guide the design, development, procurement and implementation of interoperable digital health solutions. The annex defines functional requirements for key business processes across HIV prevention, testing, treatment, care, diagnostics, referral, follow-up and reporting, together with non-functional requirements addressing system performance, security, confidentiality, privacy, interoperability, usability, reliability and offline functionality. Structured as a software-neutral implementation resource, it enables consistent interpretation of operational requirements while allowing adaptation to national policies and digital health architectures. Intended for digital health architects, software developers, implementers, procurers and programme managers, this resource supports the development of standards-based HIV information systems that accurately implement WHO recommendations while ensuring robust, secure and sustainable digital health solutions. Poliovirus containment: guidance to minimize risk for facilities collecting, handling or storing materials potentially infectious for polioviruses: web annex A: country and area specific poliovirus data, April 2023 update. World Health Organization. TitlePoliovirus containment: guidance to minimize risk for facilities collecting, handling or storing materials potentially infectious for polioviruses: web annex A: country and area specific poliovirus data, April 2023 update AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-7-24 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis web annex provides updated country- and area-specific poliovirus circulation data to support the assessment of potentially infectious materials in facilities collecting, handling or storing samples that may contain polioviruses. It accompanies the second edition of Poliovirus containment: guidance to minimize risks for facilities collecting, handling or storing materials potentially infectious for polioviruses and is intended to assist facilities in identifying samples requiring appropriate risk mitigation or containment measures. The annex presents Table A2.1, which compiles poliovirus circulation dates by country and area, including wild poliovirus (WPV), vaccine-derived poliovirus (VDPV) and oral polio vaccine type 2/novel oral polio vaccine type 2/Sabin2 potentially infectious material periods. The data were derived from national poliovirus reports, systematic literature searches and consultations with WHO regional offices, and are regularly revised and updated. The information supports the identification and management of potentially infectious materials according to the containment requirements outlined in the accompanying guidance. 2235b46f765f.doc: Use of tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in low- and middle-income countries : policy statement
2235b46f765f.title: Use of tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in low- and middle-income countries : policy statement
2235b46f765f.content: World Health Organization (2011). Use of tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in low- and middle-income countries : policy statement. World Health Organization. TitleUse of tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in low- and middle-income countries : policy statement AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2011-12-31 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241502672 Languageen AbstractThis policy statement provides evidence-based recommendations on the use of commercial interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) for tuberculosis (TB) in low- and middle-income countries, particularly settings with a high TB and/or HIV burden. Based on systematic reviews and GRADE assessment, it evaluates IGRAs for diagnosis of active TB, detection of latent TB infection (LTBI) in children and people living with HIV, screening of health care workers and contacts, outbreak investigations, and prediction of progression to active disease. The evidence was generally of low or very low quality and did not demonstrate superior performance of IGRAs over the tuberculin skin test (TST). WHO recommends that IGRAs and the TST not be used to diagnose active TB or identify individuals at risk of developing active disease, and that IGRAs not replace the TST for LTBI diagnosis in children, people living with HIV, or contacts. Given comparable performance, greater cost and technical complexity, replacing the TST with IGRAs as a public health intervention in resource-constrained settings is not recommended. Classification of digital interventions, services and applications in health: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for health. World Health Organization. TitleClassification of digital interventions, services and applications in health: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for health AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-10-24 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240081949 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis second edition of the Classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health provides a standardized taxonomy for describing how digital technologies are used to address individual and health system needs. Developed by WHO, the classification establishes a shared language to support communication among policy-makers, health programme managers, researchers, implementers, technology developers and other stakeholders involved in digital health. It organizes digital health interventions around discrete technological capabilities designed to address health system challenges and links these interventions to the digital services and application types through which they are delivered. The publication updates and expands the first edition published in 2018 to reflect advances in digital health technologies, evolving implementation practices and lessons learned from global use. The framework is structured around three interconnected axes: health system challenges, digital health interventions and digital services and application types. It includes interventions for persons, health-care providers, health system managers and data services, alongside categories of digital applications and information systems. The classification is intended to support planning, implementation, investment analysis, research, interoperability considerations, policy development and the governance of digital health initiatives, thereby facilitating more consistent and effective use of digital technologies in health systems. 45a9a6ab4202.title: Contingency fund for emergencies: 2020 annual report
45a9a6ab4202.content: World Health Organization (2021). Contingency fund for emergencies: 2020 annual report. World Health Organization. TitleContingency fund for emergencies: 2020 annual report AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-7-2 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis annual report presents an overview of the activities, financing and operational impact of the World Health Organization’s Contingency Fund for Emergencies (CFE) in 2020. The publication describes how the CFE enabled WHO to respond rapidly to 14 emergencies in 13 countries and to support the global response to COVID-19 through the release of nearly US$ 44 million. It outlines the Fund’s role in supporting outbreak control, emergency health operations, supply chain management, surveillance, vaccination activities, procurement of essential medical supplies and continuity of health services during infectious disease outbreaks, humanitarian crises, natural disasters and technological emergencies. The report highlights WHO-supported responses to the COVID-19 pandemic, Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Beirut port explosion, Tropical Cyclone Harold in Vanuatu and the humanitarian crisis in north-eastern Syria. It also examines funding allocations, reimbursement mechanisms, donor contributions and accountability arrangements governing the CFE. Through operational examples and financial analysis, the publication demonstrates the importance of rapid, flexible and predictable financing for strengthening emergency preparedness and enabling timely public health action in complex and evolving emergencies. 1f4f6a2282b4.content: World Health Organization (2023). Pandemic influenza preparedness framework: annual progress report, 1 January – 31 December 2022. World Health Organization. TitlePandemic influenza preparedness framework: annual progress report, 1 January – 31 December 2022 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-8-4 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240076907 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThe Pandemic Influenza Preparedness (PIP) Framework: annual progress report, 1 January–31 December 2022 presents technical and financial progress in implementing the PIP Framework, which aims to strengthen the sharing of influenza viruses with human pandemic potential and improve developing countries’ access to pandemic vaccines and other response supplies. The report assesses progress under the High-Level Implementation Plan II (2018–2023), including activities financed through the industry-funded Partnership Contribution mechanism. The report documents achievements and challenges in influenza laboratory capacity and surveillance, virus sharing, disease burden estimation, regulatory preparedness, risk communication and community engagement, deployment planning, and national pandemic preparedness. In 2022, 91% of Partnership Contribution recipient countries reported influenza data to FluNet, 48 countries had implemented regulatory approaches for pandemic influenza products, and 37 countries had developed or updated pandemic preparedness plans. It also presents progress in securing pandemic response products through benefit-sharing agreements, alongside financial allocations, expenditures and implementation milestones. 7e2c5f54daa7.doc: Classification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langag…
7e2c5f54daa7.title: Classification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langag…
7e2c5f54daa7.content: Organisation mondiale de la Santé (2024). Classification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langage commun pour décrire les diverses utilisations de la technologie numérique dans le domaine de la santé. Organisation mondiale de la Santé. TitleClassification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langage commun pour décrire les diverses utilisations de la technologie numérique dans le domaine de la santé AuthorsOrganisation mondiale de la Santé Issued2024-9-12 Typebook PublisherOrganisation mondiale de la Santé ISBN9789240093720 (version électronique) Languagefr AbstractCette deuxième édition de la Classification des interventions, services et applications numériques en santé présente une taxonomie normalisée permettant de décrire la manière dont les technologies numériques sont utilisées pour répondre aux besoins des individus et des systèmes de santé. Élaborée par l’OMS, cette classification établit un langage commun destiné à faciliter la communication entre les décideurs, les responsables de programmes de santé, les chercheurs, les responsables de mise en œuvre, les développeurs de technologies et les autres acteurs du domaine de la santé numérique. Elle organise les interventions numériques en santé autour de capacités technologiques distinctes conçues pour répondre à des défis des systèmes de santé et relie ces interventions aux services et types d’applications numériques qui les mettent en œuvre. La publication met à jour et élargit la première édition publiée en 2018 afin de refléter les progrès des technologies de santé numérique, l’évolution des pratiques de mise en œuvre et les enseignements tirés de leur utilisation à l’échelle mondiale. Le cadre est structuré autour de trois axes interconnectés : les défis des systèmes de santé, les interventions numériques en santé et les services et types d’applications numériques. Il comprend des interventions destinées aux personnes, aux prestataires de soins, aux gestionnaires des systèmes de santé et aux services de données, ainsi que des catégories d’applications numériques et de systèmes d’information. Cette classification vise à soutenir la planification, la mise en œuvre, l’analyse des investissements, la recherche, l’interopérabilité, l’élaboration des politiques et la gouvernance des initiatives de santé numérique. TitleWHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 1: prevention: tuberculosis preventive treatment AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2020-3-23 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240002906 Languageen AbstractThis operational handbook provides practical guidance for the programmatic management and scale-up of tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) in line with WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis. The publication addresses the global burden of tuberculosis infection and the need to expand preventive interventions among populations at high risk of developing TB disease, particularly people living with HIV, household contacts of TB patients and other vulnerable groups. It supports implementation of commitments made at the United Nations High-Level Meeting on Tuberculosis and outlines strategies to strengthen national responses through integrated, people-centred approaches. The handbook describes the cascade of care for TPT, including identification of target populations, exclusion of active TB disease, testing for TB infection, treatment options, management of adverse events, adherence support, monitoring and evaluation, and ethical considerations. It also provides operational guidance for contact investigation, integration of preventive services with active TB case finding and HIV services, health system strengthening, and resource mobilization. Practical implementation tools, policy considerations and monitoring indicators are included to assist national TB programmes, policy-makers and health-care providers in adapting and scaling up TPT services in diverse epidemiological and health system settings. ea619ba8ee13.doc: Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006
ea619ba8ee13.title: Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006
ea619ba8ee13.content: World Health Organization. Regional Office for South-East Asia (2006). Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006. WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia. TitleEnumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006 AuthorsWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for South-East Asia Issued2006-12-31 Typedocument PublisherWHO Regional Office for South-East Asia Languageen AbstractDescription: Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes is essential for initiation of antiretroviral therapy for a person with HIV as well as for monitoring the response to treatment. The techniques for enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes are evolving. The flow cytometry continues to be the gold standard of CD4 T lymphocytes enumeration in spite of the fact that the technology is expensive both in terms of initial investment in sophisticated equipment and running cost. The newer techniques may be economical to procure and maintain. The latter are particularly intended for countries with limited resources. WHO conducted a workshop to orient the nationals about these technologies and integration of a quality system into routine testing, at Siriraj Hospital Bangkok. The report describes the status of CD4 testing in these countries. While Indonesia, India and Thailand have developed a good infrastructure for enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Sri Lanka have made a beginning in this direction. The workshop focussed on principles of various techniques and imparted a hands-on training for performing the same. The issues regarding selection of technology, procurement of equipment and their maintenance; ensuring continuous supply and economical use of reagents and biosafety in laboratory were discussed and have been presented in this Report. TitleDigital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-12-21 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240085138 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis second edition of the digital adaptation kit for HIV provides operational, software-neutral requirements to support the incorporation of WHO clinical, public health and data use recommendations into digital systems. Developed within the SMART Guidelines approach, it focuses on the content requirements for person-centred digital tracking and decision support systems used by health workers for HIV services in primary health care settings. The kit is intended to facilitate transparent, consistent and adaptable translation of narrative guidance into digital implementations while supporting interoperability and local customization. The publication organizes HIV-related requirements into eight components: health interventions and associated recommendations; generic personas; illustrative user scenarios; business processes and workflows; core data elements; decision support and scheduling logic; indicators and performance metrics; and high-level functional and non-functional requirements. It covers processes including HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis, care and treatment, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, infant diagnosis, diagnostics, client follow-up, referral, and aggregate reporting and data use, with complementary operational resources provided in web annexes. 5c552a56d52d.doc: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents
5c552a56d52d.title: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents
5c552a56d52d.content: World Health Organization (2022). WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents. World Health Organization. TitleWHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-3-18 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240046764 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractTuberculosis (TB) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children and adolescents, with substantial gaps in case detection, diagnosis and access to preventive treatment worldwide. This guideline consolidates new and existing WHO recommendations for the management of TB in these populations, replacing the 2014 guidance and reflecting the latest evidence on prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and models of care. It aims to support countries in strengthening the continuum of TB care and improving health outcomes through evidence-based policies and practices tailored to the specific needs of children, adolescents and their families. The publication provides recommendations on TB screening and contact investigation, TB preventive treatment, diagnostic approaches, treatment of drug-susceptible and drug-resistant TB, management of TB meningitis, and decentralized, family-centred models of care. It incorporates updated evidence on the use of Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, integrated treatment decision algorithms, shortened treatment regimens for non-severe TB, and therapeutic options for multidrug- or rifampicin-resistant disease in children. Developed according to WHO guideline development standards, the document is intended for national TB programmes, policy-makers, health professionals and implementing partners, and contributes to global efforts to reduce TB-related morbidity and mortality in line with the End TB Strategy and Sustainable Development Goals. 8b506b5d5ef6.title: Consolidated HIV guidelines: service delivery
8b506b5d5ef6.content: World Health Organization (2026). Consolidated HIV guidelines: service delivery. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated HIV guidelines: service delivery AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2026-7-22 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240124233 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractHIV remains a major public health challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, despite the availability of effective treatment and prevention tools. Many evidence-based interventions are not implemented consistently or delivered in a timely manner, contributing to ongoing HIV transmission, advanced disease and preventable mortality. These consolidated WHO guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations to strengthen HIV service delivery through people-centred, integrated and equitable approaches that improve access to care, continuity of treatment and accelerate progress towards ending AIDS as a public health threat. The publication consolidates all WHO recommendations on HIV service delivery issued between 2013 and 2025. It is intended to support the development of national and subnational policies, clinical guidelines and implementation guidance. It addresses key components of HIV service delivery, including linkage to care and antiretroviral therapy initiation, clinical follow-up and medication refills, adherence support and re-engagement in care, services for adolescents and young people, task sharing, decentralized service delivery, and integration with maternal and child health, tuberculosis, sexual and reproductive health, diabetes, hypertension and mental health services. Recommendations are classified as new, updated or revalidated according to WHO guideline development procedures. 3eab7db370a8.title: Understanding national health workforce accounts
3eab7db370a8.content: World Health Organization (2017). Understanding national health workforce accounts. World Health Organization. TitleUnderstanding national health workforce accounts AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2017-12-31 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractUnderstanding National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) is an introductory guidance document developed by the World Health Organization to explain the purpose, policy relevance and structure of the National Health Workforce Accounts framework. The publication outlines how NHWA supports the standardization of health workforce information systems, improves the quality and comparability of data, and strengthens the evidence base for health workforce policy, planning and monitoring. Positioned within the context of universal health coverage, the Sustainable Development Goals, the Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030, and related international commitments, the document highlights the importance of reliable workforce information for addressing current and future health system challenges. The publication describes the benefits of NHWA at national, regional and global levels and presents key policy questions that can be informed through systematic workforce data collection and analysis. It introduces the health labour market framework used by NHWA, emphasizing workforce production, labour market flows, distribution, productivity and regulation. The document also summarizes the development process of the NHWA indicators and explains the modular structure of the framework, which comprises ten modules covering workforce stock, education, labour market dynamics, employment conditions, financing, governance, planning and information systems. Together, these elements provide a foundation for evidence-informed decision-making and strengthened health workforce monitoring. 0b38ffda2f8d.title: Cost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republ…
0b38ffda2f8d.content: Khadijeh Ezoji; Mohsen Yaghoubi; Marzieh Nojomi; et al. (2019). Cost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran. World Health Organization. Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean. TitleCost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran AuthorsKhadijeh Ezoji; Mohsen Yaghoubi; Marzieh Nojomi; Sussan Mahmoody; Seyed Mohsen Zahraie; Maziar Moradi-Lakeh; Sedigheh R. Tabatabaei; Abdollah Karimi Issued2019-10-29 Typedocument PublisherWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean DOIhttps://doi.org/10.26719/emhj.19.039 Languageen AbstractBackground: Pneumococcal disease caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae results in considerable mortality and morbidity. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV), such as PCV-13, can prevent invasive pneumococcal disease and avoid disability and death. The cost of introducing PCV-13 in childhood immunization schedules should be assessed against the cost of pneumococcal diseases for each community. Aims: This study aimed to evaluate the cost–effectiveness of introducing PCV-13 in the national immunization programme for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran. Methods: The TRIVAC decision support model was used to estimate total costs of introducing PCV-13 and the disability-adjusted life years (DALYs)averted. The main pneumococcal diseases were considered—pneumonia, meningitis, acute otitis media, and non-pneumonia, non-meningitis infections—in terms of hospital admissions, outpatient visits and deaths. Local data were used to estimate costs. Results: Pneumococcal disease is estimated to affect 18 713 211 children under 5 years (519 412 pneumonia, 18 148 116 acute otitis media, 6884 meningitis, and 38 799 non-pneumonia, non-meningitis)in 10 years (2014–2023)without use of the vaccine. Introduction of PCV-13 would prevent 4 900 084 cases of pneumococcal disease (190 849 pneumonia, 4 692 450 acute otitis media, 2529 meningitis, and 14 256 non-pneumonia, non-meningitis). Pneumococcal infection would cause 287 950 hospital admissions and 29 399 deaths; vaccination could avert 105 802 hospital admissions and 9997 deaths. The incremental cost–effectiveness was estimated to be US$ 1890 and US$ 1538 per averted DALY for the government and society respectively. Conclusion: According to WHO-recommended thresholds for interpreting cost–effectiveness, introduction of PCV-13 for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran would be cost-effective Sources . | iris.who.int/handle/10665/385346 (canonical) | doi:https://doi.org/10.26719/emhj.19.039 (doi) | repository record (repository) | . 91a8739ccab6.content: World Health Organization (2026). Digital transformation handbook for reporting substandard and falsified medical products. World Health Organization. TitleDigital transformation handbook for reporting substandard and falsified medical products AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2026-6-9 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240120747 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis handbook provides practical guidance to support countries in planning, designing and implementing digital solutions for reporting substandard and falsified medical products. These products pose a significant threat to public health, contributing to therapeutic failure, adverse effects, loss of trust in health systems and broader socioeconomic impacts. Effective detection and reporting are essential to enable regulatory authorities to investigate suspected cases, remove harmful products from circulation and contribute to global surveillance efforts through mechanisms such as WHO’s Global Surveillance and Monitoring System. The document outlines a structured approach to digital transformation, covering assessment of the current environment, stakeholder engagement, governance and policy alignment, definition of system requirements, implementation planning, and monitoring and evaluation. It emphasizes the transition from fragmented or paper-based reporting systems to interoperable digital platforms that improve data quality, standardization and timeliness. Drawing on global experience and existing WHO frameworks, the handbook promotes the use of user-centred design, open standards and integration with pharmacovigilance systems. It is intended for ministries of health, national regulatory authorities and partners seeking to strengthen reporting systems and enhance the capacity to detect and respond to substandard and falsified medical products. db7fa64d423c.title: Consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection: recommendations…
db7fa64d423c.content: World Health Organization (2016). Consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection: recommendations for a public health approach. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection: recommendations for a public health approach AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2016-6-6 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241549684 Languageen AbstractThis evidence-based guideline consolidates World Health Organization recommendations on the use of antiretroviral (ARV) drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection, providing a comprehensive public health framework for HIV diagnosis, prevention, treatment, service delivery, and monitoring and evaluation across all age groups and populations. Developed in response to advances in scientific evidence and evolving programmatic needs, the second edition updates the 2013 consolidated guidelines and incorporates new recommendations, including universal eligibility for antiretroviral therapy (ART) regardless of CD4 cell count, expanded use of pre-exposure prophylaxis, and optimized approaches to HIV testing, treatment monitoring and management of coinfections and comorbidities. The guideline also outlines the methods used for guideline development and the principles underpinning a public health approach. The publication provides evidence-based recommendations on HIV testing services, antiretroviral therapy, prevention interventions, differentiated service delivery models, linkage to care, adherence, decentralization, task sharing, laboratory services and programme monitoring. It emphasizes integrated, people-centred and community-based approaches to improve access to high-quality HIV services, strengthen health systems and support implementation in diverse epidemiological settings. Intended primarily for national HIV programme managers, clinicians, policy-makers and implementing partners, the guideline aims to accelerate progress towards universal access to HIV services and the global goal of ending the HIV epidemic as a major public health threat by 2030. 69ce72285a07.title: Global strategy on digital health 2020-2025
69ce72285a07.content: World Health Organization (2021). Global strategy on digital health 2020-2025. World Health Organization. TitleGlobal strategy on digital health 2020-2025 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-8-18 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240020924 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThe Global strategy on digital health 2020–2025 provides a framework to support Member States in strengthening health systems through the appropriate adoption and use of digital technologies. Developed in response to World Health Assembly mandates and aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals and WHO’s Triple Billion targets, the strategy outlines a shared vision for improving health and well-being through accessible, affordable, secure and sustainable digital health solutions. It emphasizes the importance of strong governance, interoperability, ethical use of data, privacy protection, workforce capacity-building and investment in digital infrastructure to support national health priorities and universal health coverage. The document establishes four strategic objectives: promoting global collaboration and knowledge exchange; advancing the implementation of national digital health strategies; strengthening governance for digital health at global, regional and national levels; and advocating people-centred health systems enabled by digital technologies. It also presents guiding principles, an implementation framework and monitoring mechanisms to support countries in developing interoperable digital health ecosystems. Particular attention is given to addressing barriers faced by low- and middle-income countries and ensuring that digital transformation contributes to equitable, effective and resilient health systems. 2bbd08b5b21a.content: World Health Organization (2023). Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing: WHO recommendations in digital systems: web annex B: decision-support logic. World Health Organization. TitleDigital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing: WHO recommendations in digital systems: web annex B: decision-support logic AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-12-14 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis web annex provides the standardized decision-support logic supporting the WHO Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems. It translates WHO HIV recommendations into structured, software-neutral decision tables that can be incorporated into digital tracking and decision-support systems to support consistent clinical and public health decision-making. The annex includes decision logic for HIV testing, prevention, treatment, advanced HIV disease, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, diagnostics, follow-up and related service delivery workflows, using standardized input expressions, decision rules, outputs, scheduling logic and triggering events. It also provides implementation guidance on rule syntax, comparison operators, hit policies and coding conventions to promote transparency, interoperability and consistent interpretation across digital platforms. Intended for software developers, digital health architects, implementers and programme managers, this resource supports the development and adaptation of standards-based decision-support functionality that accurately reflects WHO recommendations while allowing contextualization for national policies and health system requirements. b6ca31aaab4c.doc: National health workforce accounts: a handbook
b6ca31aaab4c.title: National health workforce accounts: a handbook
b6ca31aaab4c.content: World Health Organization (2017). National health workforce accounts: a handbook. World Health Organization. TitleNational health workforce accounts: a handbook AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2017-10-26 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241513111 Languageen AbstractThis handbook introduces the National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA), a standardized framework developed by the World Health Organization to strengthen health workforce information systems and support evidence-based workforce planning and policy-making. The publication is intended to assist countries in monitoring and analysing health workforce capacity, distribution, education, labour market dynamics, financing, governance and information systems in the context of universal health coverage and the health-related Sustainable Development Goals. It outlines the rationale for improved health workforce data and highlights the role of harmonized metrics in addressing challenges related to workforce availability, accessibility, performance and retention. The handbook presents a modular framework comprising 78 core indicators organized across 10 modules covering active workforce stock, education and training, regulation and accreditation, education financing, labour market flows, employment conditions, workforce spending and remuneration, skill mix, governance, and health workforce information systems. For each indicator, it provides definitions, methodological guidance, reporting requirements, data sources and disaggregation options. The publication also describes implementation principles, reporting standards and potential applications of the NHWA, supporting countries in strengthening health workforce monitoring, facilitating international comparability and informing policies aimed at improving health system performance and population access to quality health services. eaafc48037ea.doc: Stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020-2025
eaafc48037ea.title: Stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020-2025
eaafc48037ea.content: Organisation mondiale de la Santé (2021). Stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020-2025. Organisation mondiale de la Santé. TitleStratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020-2025 AuthorsOrganisation mondiale de la Santé Issued2021-8-18 Typebook PublisherOrganisation mondiale de la Santé ISBN9789240027558 (version électronique) Languagefr AbstractLa Stratégie mondiale pour la santé numérique 2020–2025 fournit un cadre destiné à aider les États Membres à renforcer leurs systèmes de santé grâce à l’adoption et à l’utilisation appropriées des technologies numériques. Élaborée en réponse aux mandats de l’Assemblée mondiale de la Santé et alignée sur les Objectifs de développement durable ainsi que sur les objectifs du « Triple milliard » de l’OMS, cette stratégie présente une vision commune visant à améliorer la santé et le bien-être au moyen de solutions de santé numérique accessibles, abordables, sûres et durables. Elle souligne l’importance d’une gouvernance solide, de l’interopérabilité, de l’utilisation éthique des données, de la protection de la vie privée, du renforcement des capacités des personnels de santé et des investissements dans les infrastructures numériques afin de soutenir les priorités nationales de santé et la couverture sanitaire universelle. Le document définit quatre objectifs stratégiques : promouvoir la collaboration mondiale et le partage des connaissances ; faire progresser la mise en œuvre des stratégies nationales de santé numérique ; renforcer la gouvernance de la santé numérique aux niveaux mondial, régional et national ; et promouvoir des systèmes de santé centrés sur les personnes grâce aux technologies numériques. Il présente également des principes directeurs, un cadre de mise en œuvre et des mécanismes de suivi destinés à soutenir les pays dans le développement d’écosystèmes numériques interopérables. Une attention particulière est accordée aux obstacles rencontrés par les pays à revenu faible ou intermédiaire et à la nécessité de veiller à ce que la transformation numérique contribue à des systèmes de santé plus équitables, efficaces et résilients. 87ecd460d7a7.title: Clasificación de intervenciones, servicios y aplicaciones digitales en salud: un lenguaje compartido para describir l…
87ecd460d7a7.content: Organización Mundial de la Salud (2024). Clasificación de intervenciones, servicios y aplicaciones digitales en salud: un lenguaje compartido para describir los usos de la tecnología digital para la salud. Organización Mundial de la Salud. TitleClasificación de intervenciones, servicios y aplicaciones digitales en salud: un lenguaje compartido para describir los usos de la tecnología digital para la salud AuthorsOrganización Mundial de la Salud Issued2024-9-24 Typebook PublisherOrganización Mundial de la Salud ISBN9789240093744 (versión electrónica) Languagees AbstractEsta segunda edición de la Clasificación de intervenciones, servicios y aplicaciones digitales en salud proporciona una taxonomía normalizada para describir cómo se utilizan las tecnologías digitales para responder a las necesidades de las personas y de los sistemas de salud. Desarrollada por la OMS, la clasificación establece un lenguaje común destinado a facilitar la comunicación entre responsables de la formulación de políticas, gestores de programas de salud, investigadores, implementadores, desarrolladores tecnológicos y otras partes interesadas en la salud digital. Organiza las intervenciones de salud digital en torno a capacidades tecnológicas específicas diseñadas para abordar desafíos de los sistemas de salud y las vincula con los servicios digitales y los tipos de aplicaciones mediante los cuales se prestan. La publicación actualiza y amplía la primera edición, publicada en 2018, para reflejar los avances en las tecnologías de salud digital, la evolución de las prácticas de implementación y las lecciones aprendidas a partir de su utilización a nivel mundial. El marco se estructura en torno a tres ejes interrelacionados: los desafíos de los sistemas de salud, las intervenciones de salud digital y los tipos de servicios y aplicaciones digitales. Incluye intervenciones dirigidas a las personas, los proveedores de atención sanitaria, los gestores de sistemas de salud y los servicios de datos, junto con categorías de aplicaciones digitales y sistemas de información. La clasificación está concebida para apoyar la planificación, la implementación, el análisis de inversiones, la investigación, las consideraciones de interoperabilidad, la elaboración de políticas y la gobernanza de las iniciativas de salud digital, facilitando así un uso más coherente y eficaz de las tecnologías digitales en los sistemas de salud. 945f9efcb64c.title: Guidelines on long-acting injectable cabotegravir for HIV prevention
945f9efcb64c.content: World Health Organization (2022). Guidelines on long-acting injectable cabotegravir for HIV prevention. World Health Organization. TitleGuidelines on long-acting injectable cabotegravir for HIV prevention AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-7-27 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240054097 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guideline provides evidence-informed recommendations on the use of long-acting injectable cabotegravir (CAB-LA) as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention in people at substantial risk of HIV infection. Developed according to WHO guideline development procedures, it is based on systematic reviews, GRADE assessments and additional evidence on effectiveness, safety, acceptability, feasibility, equity and cost–effectiveness. The document reviews the global HIV prevention context, the rationale for expanding HIV prevention choices, and the evidence supporting CAB-LA as an additional PrEP option. It also outlines the principles guiding implementation within a public health and human rights framework and identifies the intended audiences for the recommendations. The guideline recommends that long-acting injectable cabotegravir may be offered as an additional HIV prevention choice as part of combination prevention approaches for people at substantial risk of HIV infection. It discusses key implementation considerations, including HIV testing, service delivery models, comprehensive prevention services, community engagement, provider training and adherence support. The publication also identifies priority research gaps related to safety, drug resistance, delivery strategies and population-level impact, and describes the guideline development process, dissemination strategy and supporting evidence underpinning the recommendation. 1f8d5744033a.doc: Classification of digital health interventions v1.0: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for…
1f8d5744033a.title: Classification of digital health interventions v1.0: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for…
1f8d5744033a.content: World Health Organization (2018). Classification of digital health interventions v1.0: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for health. World Health Organization. TitleClassification of digital health interventions v1.0: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for health AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2018-3-14 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis publication presents version 1.0 of the World Health Organization’s Classification of Digital Health Interventions (DHIs), a taxonomy developed to provide a shared and standardized language for describing how digital and mobile technologies are used to address health system needs. Intended primarily for public health audiences, the framework supports communication among policymakers, programme planners, implementers, researchers, donors and technology specialists by defining digital health interventions as discrete digital functionalities linked to specific health objectives. The classification was developed to facilitate evidence synthesis, landscape analyses, planning processes and the articulation of digital solutions to identified health system challenges. The framework organizes digital health interventions into four primary groups according to the main user: clients, health-care providers, health system managers and data services. It links digital interventions to broader health system challenges and to system categories such as electronic medical records, logistics management information systems and telemedicine platforms. Developed through technical consultations, literature review and public feedback, the classification builds on existing mHealth and eHealth frameworks while providing a simplified and practical reference for health programmes. The document is intended to support the design, implementation, evaluation and interoperability of digital health initiatives and will be periodically updated to reflect emerging technologies and evolving practices in digital health. b5a1f8519f5d.content: World Health Organization (2023). National health workforce accounts: a handbook. World Health Organization. TitleNational health workforce accounts: a handbook AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-11-23 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240081291 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThe National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) Handbook, second edition, provides the conceptual framework, standards, methods and indicators that support the systematic collection, analysis and use of health workforce data for evidence-informed policy-making and planning. Developed by the World Health Organization, the handbook supports implementation of the National Health Workforce Accounts as a country-led system to strengthen human resources for health information systems, improve data quality and availability, and monitor progress towards universal health coverage, the Sustainable Development Goals and other global health objectives. It describes the rationale, principles and applications of NHWA at national, regional and global levels and outlines a modular approach to health workforce monitoring. The handbook presents guidance on implementation and reporting methods and defines a set of standardized indicators organized into four modules covering workforce stock and flows, education, finance and expenditures, and working conditions, governance and leadership. It explains indicator metadata, calculation methods, disaggregation requirements and reporting standards, and illustrates how NHWA data can be used to support workforce planning, policy development, retention strategies, equity analyses and monitoring of health workforce trends. The revised edition incorporates updated indicators, occupational classifications, tools and guidance to address evolving health workforce priorities and emerging global health challenges. 344929e589ca.doc: Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems
344929e589ca.title: Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems
344929e589ca.content: World Health Organization (2024). Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems. World Health Organization. TitleDigital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2024-11-4 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240093362 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis handbook provides practical guidance for countries seeking to digitally transform primary health care through the development and implementation of person-centred point of service systems (PCPOSS). It addresses the transition from paper-based and fragmented digital systems towards integrated, interoperable digital solutions that support service delivery, continuity of care, data use and health system strengthening. Grounded in WHO recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening and aligned with the SMART Guidelines framework, the publication outlines approaches for translating clinical and public health guidance into digital systems while maintaining fidelity to normative standards. The publication presents a stepwise methodology covering assessment of digital readiness, identification of user requirements, workflow and business process mapping, system design and adaptation, software selection, testing, deployment and scale-up. It emphasizes person-centred care, interoperability, longitudinal health records, decision support and the use of standards-based digital architectures. Through practical tools, worksheets and implementation guidance, the publication supports policy-makers, programme managers, digital health practitioners and software developers in designing and optimizing digital systems that improve service quality, strengthen accountability and enable more effective, integrated and responsive primary health care services. a75a16ea840e.title: Лечение и уход в связи с ВИЧ/СПИДом в Беларуси: отчет оценочной миссии: январь 2014 г.
a75a16ea840e.content: Lundgren, Jens D; Raben, Dorthe; Ерамова, Ирина; et al. (2014). Лечение и уход в связи с ВИЧ/СПИДом в Беларуси: отчет оценочной миссии: январь 2014 г.. Всемирная организация здравоохранения. Европейское региональное бюро. TitleЛечение и уход в связи с ВИЧ/СПИДом в Беларуси: отчет оценочной миссии: январь 2014 г. AuthorsLundgren, Jens D; Raben, Dorthe; Ерамова, Ирина; Ильенкова, Вера Issued2014-12-31 Typereport PublisherВсемирная организация здравоохранения. Европейское региональное бюро Languageru AbstractОценка лечения и ухода в связи с ВИЧ/СПИДом выполнена с учетом стратегии или концепции ВОЗ/ЮНЭЙДС «Лечение 2.0», где указаны пять приоритетных областей: оптимизация лекарственных схем, обеспечение доступа к диагностике в местах оказания помощи, снижение стоимости, адаптация систем оказания услуг и мобилизация сообществ или гражданского общества. Для оценки использованы результаты анализа существующих документов и отчетов и страновой миссии, которая состоялась 11-14 ноября 2013 года в гор. Минске и Солигорске, Беларусь. Особое внимание было уделено практике тестирования на ВИЧ, поскольку именно здесь начинается лечение и уход в связи с ВИЧ, а также уязвимым группам и обеспечению доступа к лечению и уходу. Кроме того, была проанализирована устойчивость программ в свете используемых в настоящее время и будущих международных и национальных схем финансирования. 0649df4d65b0.title: Estrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025
0649df4d65b0.content: Organización Mundial de la Salud (2021). Estrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025. Organización Mundial de la Salud. TitleEstrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025 AuthorsOrganización Mundial de la Salud Issued2021-8-18 Typebook PublisherOrganización Mundial de la Salud ISBN9789240027572 (versión electrónica) Languagees AbstractLa Estrategia mundial sobre salud digital 2020–2025 proporciona un marco para apoyar a los Estados Miembros en el fortalecimiento de los sistemas de salud mediante la adopción y el uso adecuados de las tecnologías digitales. Elaborada en respuesta a los mandatos de la Asamblea Mundial de la Salud y alineada con los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible y las metas de los “Tres Mil Millones” de la OMS, la estrategia establece una visión compartida para mejorar la salud y el bienestar a través de soluciones de salud digital accesibles, asequibles, seguras y sostenibles. Destaca la importancia de una gobernanza sólida, la interoperabilidad, el uso ético de los datos, la protección de la privacidad, el fortalecimiento de las capacidades del personal sanitario y la inversión en infraestructura digital para apoyar las prioridades nacionales de salud y la cobertura sanitaria universal. El documento define cuatro objetivos estratégicos: promover la colaboración mundial y el intercambio de conocimientos; avanzar en la implementación de estrategias nacionales de salud digital; fortalecer la gobernanza de la salud digital a nivel mundial, regional y nacional; y fomentar sistemas de salud centrados en las personas mediante el uso de tecnologías digitales. Asimismo, presenta principios rectores, un marco de implementación y mecanismos de seguimiento destinados a apoyar a los países en el desarrollo de ecosistemas de salud digital interoperables. Se presta especial atención a los obstáculos que enfrentan los países de ingresos bajos y medianos y a garantizar que la transformación digital contribuya a sistemas de salud más equitativos, eficaces y resilientes. Ren∗, Yuanjie. MerLean: An Agentic Framework for Autoformalization in Quantum Computation. TitleMerLean: An Agentic Framework for Autoformalization in Quantum Computation AuthorsRen∗, Yuanjie Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2602.16554 AbstractWe introduce MerLean, a fully automated agentic framework for autoformalization in quantum computation. MerLean extracts mathematical statements from LATEX source files, formalizes them into verified Lean 4 code built on Mathlib, and trans- lates the result back into human-readable LATEX for semantic review. We evaluate MerLean on three theoretical quantum computing papers producing 2,050 Lean dec- larations from 114 statements in total. MerLean achieves end-to-end formalization on all three papers, reducing the verification burden to only the newly introduced definitions and axioms. Our results demonstrate that agentic autoformalization can scale to frontier research, offering both a practical tool for machine-verified peer review and a scalable engine for mining high-quality synthetic data to train future reasoning models. Our approach can also be generalized to any other rigorous research in mathematics and theoretical physics. Sources . | arxiv.org/abs/2602.16554 (canonical) | . TitleProcess-Driven Autoformalization in Lean 4 AuthorsLu1∗, Jianqiao; Wan2∗, Yingjia; Liu3, Zhengying; Huang4, Yinya; Xiong1, Jing IssuedD:20241015 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2406.01940 AbstractAutoformalization, the conversion of natural language mathematics into formal languages, offers significant potential for advancing mathematical reasoning. How- ever, existing efforts are limited to formal languages with substantial online corpora and struggle to keep pace with rapidly evolving languages like Lean 4. To bridge this gap, we propose a large-scale dataset Formalization for Lean 4 (FORML4) de- signed to comprehensively evaluate the autoformalization capabilities of large lan- guage models (LLMs), encompassing both statements and proofs in natural and for- mal languages. Additionally, we introduce the Process-Driven Autoformalization (PDA) framework that leverages the precise feedback from Lean 4 compilers to enhance autoformalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PDA improves autoformalization, enabling higher compiler accuracy and human-evaluation scores using less filtered training data. Moreover, when fine-tuned with data containing detailed process information, PDA exhibits enhanced data utilization, resulting in more substantial improvements in autoformalization for Lean 4. Humans, Automating Blueprint Generation for; AI. LeanArchitect: Automating Blueprint Generation for Humans and AI. TitleLeanArchitect: Automating Blueprint Generation for Humans and AI AuthorsHumans, Automating Blueprint Generation for; AI Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2601.22554 AbstractLarge-scale formalization projects in Lean rely on blueprints: structured dependency graphs linking informal mathematical exposition to formal declarations. While blueprints are central to human collaboration, existing tooling treats the informal (LATEX) and formal (Lean) components as largely decoupled artifacts, leading to maintenance overhead and limiting integration with AI automation. We present LeanArchitect, a Lean package for extracting, managing, and exporting blueprint data directly from Lean code. LeanArchitect introduces a declarative annotation mechanism that associates formal declarations with blueprint metadata, automatically infers dependency information, and generates LATEX blueprint content synchronized with the Lean development. This design eliminates duplication between formal and informal representations and eases fine-grained progress tracking for both human contributors and AI-based theorem provers. We demonstrate the practicality of LeanArchitect through the automated conversion of several large existing blueprint-driven projects, and through a human–AI collaboration case study formalizing a multivariate Taylor theorem. Our results show that LeanArchitect improves maintainability, exposes latent inconsistencies in existing blueprints, and provides an effective interface for integrating AI tools into real-world formalization workflows. arXiv:2601.22554v1 [cs.LO] 30 Jan 2026 Sources . | arxiv.org/abs/2601.22554 (canonical) | . Parag Mali, Puneeth Kukkadapu, Mahshad Mahdavi, and, Richard Zanibbi. ScanSSD: Scanning Single Shot Detector for Mathematical Formulas in PDF Document Images. TitleScanSSD: Scanning Single Shot Detector for Mathematical Formulas in PDF Document Images AuthorsParag Mali, Puneeth Kukkadapu, Mahshad Mahdavi, and, Richard Zanibbi IssuedD:20200319 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2003.08005 AbstractWe introduce the Scanning Single Shot Detector (ScanSSD) for locating math formulas offset from text and embedded in textlines. ScanSSD uses only visual features for detection: no formatting or typesetting information such as layout, font, or character labels are employed. Given a 600 dpi document page image, a Single Shot Detector (SSD) locates formulas at multiple scales using sliding windows, after which candidate detections are pooled to obtain page-level results. For our experiments we use the TFD-ICDAR2019v2 dataset, a modiﬁcation of the GTDB scanned math article collection. ScanSSD detects characters in formulas with high accuracy, obtaining a 0.926 f-score, and detects formulas with high recall overall. Detection errors are largely minor, such as splitting formulas at large whitespace gaps (e.g., for variable constraints) and merging formulas on adjacent textlines. Formula detection f-scores of 0.796 (IOU ≥0.5) and 0.733 (IOU ≥0.75) are obtained. Our data, evaluation tools, and code are publicly available. I. INTRODUCTION The PDF format is used ubiquitously for sharing and printing documents. Unfortunately, while the latest PDF speciﬁcation supports embedding structural information for graphical elements (e.g., ﬁgures, tables, and footnotes1), most born-digital PDF documents contain only rendering-level information such as characters, lines, and images. These low-level objects can be recovered by parsing the document [1], but graphic regions must be located using detection algorithms. For example, PDFFigures [2] extracts ﬁgures and tables from born-digital Computer Science research papers for Semantic Scholar.2 Unfortunately, older PDF documents may contain only scanned images of document pages, providing no information about characters or other graphical objects in the page images. We present a new image-based detector for mathematical formulas in in both born-digital and scanned PDF documents. Pluzhnikov, Ivan. LLM-supported document separation for printed reviews from zbMATH Open. TitleLLM-supported document separation for printed reviews from zbMATH Open AuthorsPluzhnikov, Ivan IssuedD:20260402 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2604.00554 AbstractThis paper presents a specialized methodology for digitizing and segmenting mathematical documents from zbMATH Open, a com- prehensive database of mathematical literature, to enhance ma- chine processing capabilities. Currently, approximately 831,000 documents exist only in scanned volumes, which makes them not machine-processable. Furthermore, these scans often span multi- ple pages or share pages with other documents and incorporate diverse typesetting techniques, posing challenges for automated processing. To address these issues, we evaluate various Optical Charac- ter Recognition (OCR) tools and document separation techniques, proposing an optimized pipeline that outperforms existing ap- proaches. Our study identifies Mathpix as the most effective OCR tool for LaTeX conversion, demonstrating superior performance based on BLEU and Edit Distance metrics. For document sepa- ration, we fine-tune generative Large Language Models (LLMs) and integrate them into a Majority Voting framework, achieving 97.5% accuracy when providing the text of the document. Addi- tionally, our method identifies the start and end indexes for 90.6% of the test dataset, with an accuracy of 98.4% on applicable cases, resulting in an overall accuracy of 89.1% on the entire dataset. This approach surpasses traditional baselines, including regular expres- sions, ChatGPT-4o, and computer vision-based techniques. As a practical outcome, we process 810,977 mathematical documents into machine-readable text and extract precise document bound- aries for 721,288 documents in LaTeX format. These contributions significantly improve accessibility for mathematical information re- trieval systems, machine learning models, and related applications. Horn1[0009−0004−1911−1138], Pius; Janis Keuper1, 2[0000−0002−1327−1243]. Benchmarking Document Parsers on Mathematical Formula Extraction from PDFs. TitleBenchmarking Document Parsers on Mathematical Formula Extraction from PDFs AuthorsHorn1[0009−0004−1911−1138], Pius; Janis Keuper1, 2[0000−0002−1327−1243] IssuedD:20260825 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2512.09874 AbstractCorrectly parsing mathematical formulas from PDFs is crit- ical for training large language models and building scientiﬁc knowledge bases from academic literature, yet existing benchmarks either exclude formulas entirely or lack semantically-aware evaluation metrics. We in- troduce a benchmarking framework centered on synthetically generated PDFs with precise LaTeX ground truth, enabling systematic control over layout, formulas, and content characteristics. For evaluation, we apply LLM-as-a-judge to assess semantic equivalence of parsed formulas, cap- turing mathematical meaning beyond surface-level notation diﬀerences. We validate this approach through a human study (250 formula pairs, 750 ratings from 30 evaluators), showing a Pearson correlation of r=0.78 with human judgment, compared to r=0.34 for character-level match- ing (CDM) and r≈0 for text similarity. Our robust two-stage matching pipeline combining LLM-based extraction with fuzzy validation reliably aligns parsed formulas with ground truth despite format inconsisten- cies across parsers. Evaluating 20+ contemporary PDF parsers across 100 synthetic documents with 2,000+ formulas reveals signiﬁcant per- formance disparities, providing actionable guidance for practitioners se- lecting parsers for downstream applications. What Keeps Agent Skills from Being Reusable? Evidence from 138K SKILL.md Files. TitleWhat Keeps Agent Skills from Being Reusable? Evidence from 138K SKILL.md Files AuthorsZhang, Chi IssuedD:20260811 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2608.08453 AbstractUnder the current standard, Agent Skills are SKILL.md files that combine instructions with supporting resources, en- abling Large Language Model (LLM) agents to reuse proce- dures beyond a single conversation. Yet many public skills appear to originate from a single task, repository, or conver- sation, even when they are shared as reusable components. We analyze this gap across 138,133 public SKILL.md files from 20,556 repositories using a two-tier defect taxonomy grounded in the official specification and best-practice guid- ance. We find that 91.8% of skills contain at least one de- tected defect, with stable estimates across lenient and strict thresholds (88.8–94.6%). The dominant failures are ordinary packaging problems rather than exotic attacks: weak routing metadata, bloated or non-actionable bodies, and poor re- source organization. A deterministic routing stress test over 20,000 skills shows the functional impact: skills with valid routing metadata are retrieved more reliably from startup descriptions than skills with routing defects. Defect rates vary by platform and provenance: specification-aware skills contain fewer defects, while AI-marked skills show more safety and portability problems. Lightweight enforcement and repair experiments support a quality-assured generation workflow combining spec-aware prompting, lightweight lint- ing, automated repair, and safety gating. Son, Seongho; Yoon, Sangwoong; Tang, Jiahua; et al.. SWE-Router: Routing in Multi-turn Agentic Software Engineering Tasks. TitleSWE-Router: Routing in Multi-turn Agentic Software Engineering Tasks AuthorsSon, Seongho; Yoon, Sangwoong; Tang, Jiahua; Wang, Shuhan; Wolf, Lorenz; Bogunovic, Ilija Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2607.00053 AbstractLarge language models (LLMs) embedded in multi-turn agentic harnesses are reshaping soft- ware engineering (SWE), but routing every task to a frontier model is wasteful when many issues admit cheap fixes. Existing LLM routers operate on the task description alone, which inherits an information-theoretic Bayes-error floor in agentic settings: a similar issue can hide either a localized typo or a multi-module refactor, and the prompt does not separate the two. We introduce SWE- Router, a value-based temporal approach that lets a cheap model run for a few exploratory turns and reads the resulting partial trajectory before de- ciding whether to continue cheaply or to escalate to an expensive model. We provide a Bayes- optimality theorem showing that conditioning on the partial trajectory never harms routing and is strictly better whenever exploration is informative. Across the LLM pairs of weak and strong models spanning the contemporary cost–capability frontier, we show that SWE-Router greatly improves the cost efficiency of SWE tasks, while maintaining the majority of the performances of the stronger model. We additionally release a multi-LLM trajectory dataset which allows reproduction of our trajectory-level routing. Sources . | arxiv.org/abs/2607.00053 (canonical) | . Rawal, Kaivalya. Evaluating Model Explanations without Ground Truth. TitleEvaluating Model Explanations without Ground Truth AuthorsRawal, Kaivalya IssuedD:20250611 Typearticle-journal DOI10.1145/3715275.3732219 NotearXiv:2505.10399 AbstractThere can be many competing and contradictory explanations for a single model prediction, making it difficult to select which one to use. Current explanation evaluation frameworks measure qual- ity by comparing against ideal “ground-truth” explanations, or by verifying model sensitivity to important inputs. We outline the limitations of these approaches, and propose three desirable princi- ples to ground the future development of explanation evaluation strategies for local feature importance explanations. We propose a ground-truth Agnostic eXplanation Evaluation framework (AXE) for evaluating and comparing model explanations that satis- fies these principles. Unlike prior approaches, AXE does not require access to ideal ground-truth explanations for comparison, or rely on model sensitivity – providing an independent measure of expla- nation quality. We verify AXE by comparing with baselines, and show how it can be used to detect explanation fairwashing. Our code is available at https://github.com/KaiRawal/Evaluating-Model- Explanations-without-Ground-Truth. CCS Concepts • Computing methodologies →Artificial intelligence; Ma- chine learning. Harris1, Joshua; †; Laurence1, Timothy; et al.. Evaluating Large Language Models for Public Health Classification and Extraction Tasks. TitleEvaluating Large Language Models for Public Health Classification and Extraction Tasks AuthorsHarris1, Joshua; †; Laurence1, Timothy; Loman1, Leo; Grayson1, Fan; Nonnenmacher1, Toby; Harry IssuedD:20250220 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2405.14766 AbstractAdvances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have led to significant interest in their potential to support human experts across a range of domains, including public health. In this work we present automated evaluations of LLMs for public health tasks involving the classification and extraction of free text. We combine six externally annotated datasets with seven new internally annotated datasets to evaluate LLMs for processing text related to: health burden, epidemiological risk factors, and public health interventions. We evaluate eleven open-weight LLMs (7-123 billion parameters) across all tasks using zero-shot in-context learning. We find that Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct is the highest performing model, achieving the best results on 8/16 tasks (using micro-F1 scores). We see significant variation across tasks with all open-weight LLMs scoring below 60% micro-F1 on some challenging tasks, such as Contact Classification, while all LLMs achieve greater than 80% micro-F1 on others, such as GI Illness Classification. For a subset of 11 tasks, we also evaluate three GPT-4 and GPT-4o series models and find comparable results to Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct. Overall, based on these initial results we find promising signs that LLMs may be useful tools for public health experts to extract information from a wide variety of free text sources, and support public health surveillance, research, and interventions. TitleInvestigating the impact of representation features on decision model comprehension (Extended Abstract) IssuedD:20240502 Typearticle-journal DOI10.18420/EMISA2024_05 Abstract)5 Djordje Djurica 1, Tyge F. Kummer 2, Jan Mendling 1,3, and Kathrin Figl 4 Abstract: Decision models play a crucial role in the development of information systems for tasks such as system analysis and design, as well as compliance management. The effective presentation of these models is essential to ensure their accuracy and completeness. Existing research on their cognitive effectiveness remains inconclusive. Our study advances understanding by examining the detailed representation features of decision models, including type (tree versus table), structure (expanded versus frugal), and design (monochromatic versus colored). We demonstrate that the use of color can improve model-task fit, and that structural features can enhance comprehension. Utilizing eye-tracking, we analyzed the underlying mechanisms of these effects. Our findings provide valuable insights for cognitive information systems research and practical applications, offering guidance for both users and developers of decision models. Tang1, Xunzhu; Kim2, Kisub; Song1, Yewei; et al.. CodeAgent : Autonomous Communicative Agents for Code Review. TitleCodeAgent : Autonomous Communicative Agents for Code Review AuthorsTang1, Xunzhu; Kim2, Kisub; Song1, Yewei; Lothritz3, Cedric; Li4, Bei; Ezzini5, Saad IssuedD:20240926 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2402.02172 AbstractCode review, which aims at ensuring the over- all quality and reliability of software, is a cor- nerstone of software development. Unfortu- nately, while crucial, Code review is a labor- intensive process that the research community is looking to automate. Existing automated methods rely on single input-output generative models and thus generally struggle to emulate the collaborative nature of code review. This work introduces CodeAgent, a novel multi- agent Large Language Model (LLM) system for code review automation. CodeAgent in- corporates a supervisory agent, QA-Checker, to ensure that all the agents’ contributions ad- dress the initial review question. We evaluated CodeAgent on critical code review tasks: (1) detect inconsistencies between code changes and commit messages, (2) identify vulnerabil- ity introductions, (3) validate code style ad- herence, and (4) suggest code revision. Tekanlou1, Hadi Bayrami Asl; Razmara1, Jafar; Sanaei1, Mahsa. Homa at SemEval-2025 Task 5: Aligning Librarian Records with OntoAligner for Subject Tagging. TitleHoma at SemEval-2025 Task 5: Aligning Librarian Records with OntoAligner for Subject Tagging AuthorsTekanlou1, Hadi Bayrami Asl; Razmara1, Jafar; Sanaei1, Mahsa IssuedD:20250501 Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2504.21474 AbstractThis paper presents our system, Homa, for SemEval-2025 Task 5: Subject Tagging, which focuses on automatically assigning subject la- bels to technical records from TIBKAT us- ing the Gemeinsame Normdatei (GND) tax- onomy. We leverage OntoAligner, a modu- lar ontology alignment toolkit, to address this task by integrating retrieval-augmented genera- tion (RAG) techniques. Our approach formu- lates the subject tagging problem as an align- ment task, where records are matched to GND categories based on semantic similarity. We evaluate OntoAligner’s adaptability for sub- ject indexing and analyze its effectiveness in handling multilingual records. Experimental results demonstrate the strengths and limita- tions of this method, highlighting the potential of alignment techniques for improving subject tagging in digital libraries. Institute for Parallel; Systems, Distributed. AI-assisted JSON Schema Creation and Mapping. TitleAI-assisted JSON Schema Creation and Mapping AuthorsInstitute for Parallel; Systems, Distributed Typearticle-journal NotearXiv:2508.05192 AbstractModel-Driven Engineering (MDE) places models at the core of system and data engineering processes. In the context of research data, these models are typically expressed as schemas that define the structure and semantics of datasets. However, many domains still lack standardized models, and creating them remains a significant barrier, especially for non- experts. We present a hybrid approach that combines large language models (LLMs) with deterministic techniques to enable JSON Schema creation, modification, and schema mapping based on natural language inputs by the user. These capabilities are integrated into the open-source tool MetaConfigurator, which already provides visual model editing, validation, code gener- ation, and form generation from models. For data integration, we generate schema mappings from heterogeneous JSON, CSV, XML, and YAML data using LLMs, while ensuring scalability and reliability through deterministic execution of generated mapping rules. The applicability of our work is demonstrated in an application example in the field of chemistry. By combining natural language interaction with deterministic safeguards, this work significantly lowers the barrier to structured data modeling and data integration for non-experts.
