Un paquete de contenido puede relajar un paso base declarándolo en skills/<package>/workflow-policy.json con un motivo —una flexibilización sin justificar no se carga, por lo que el archivo es el registro de lo que se eximió y por qué. Cinco pasos se niegan a ser relajados en absoluto: Task_ReviewFindings, Gateway_EditorDecision y Task_Commit (el editor viendo los hallazgos, la decisión, la escritura), además de Task_AuthorizeRelease y Task_PublishRelease (el requisito SHALL de publish-authorized). Si esos fueran negociables, la base no sería estricta, sería una sugerencia. bun run cat check:workflow-policy lista la política y valida cada flexibilización; se ejecuta en CI, por lo que una que haya dejado de aplicarse es un fallo de compilación en lugar de un descubrimiento el día en que se necesita. El límite de confirmación (commit boundary) es donde esto se impone de manera efectiva y no solo mediante consulta. scripts/check-corpus-gate.ts, ejecutado en el repositorio del folio desde un gancho de pre-commit o en CI, rechaza un bloque de contenido modificado para el cual ninguna instancia registra que el editor lo haya autorizado. workflow_gate responde a un agente que pregunta; el gancho no depende de que nadie pregunte. bun run <platform>/scripts/check-corpus-gate.ts --staged --platform <platform> bun run <platform>/scripts/check-corpus-gate.ts --staged --warn # adoptar gradualmente . Cómo leerlos . ✎ Edit QA… TR . | Un carril es un rol. Cada carril se asigna a un actor en .claude/skills/actors/ — consulta Quién es quién. | [nombre-habilidad] bajo una actividad es la habilidad de folio-assistant que la implementa. La misma referencia se transporta de forma legible por máquina como un elemento de extensión <bootstrap.processes:skill ref="…"/> en la actividad BPMN. | El carril “Plan de trabajo — beans” es el almacén compartido de tareas pendientes. Los pasos en ese carril leen y escriben en beans/, y están marcados con <cat-harness.processes:bean store="beans/"/> en el código fuente. | Un cuadro de borde grueso es una actividad de llamada —se expande en otro diagrama de esta página. | .

c8128756f108.title: Edición y la compuerta de validación de HCI
c8128756f108.content: ✎ Edit KG… . Este es el diagrama que más importa en el día a día: un cambio propuesto en un bloque de contenido. Abrir la fuente BPMN . La única regla para cuya declaración existe este diagrama . ✎ Edit QA… TR . Nada llega al corpus antes de que el editor haya visto los hallazgos. El agente de autoría produce un cambio propuesto, no una confirmación (commit). Esa propuesta se bifurca a través de la canalización de validación de HCI, los resultados se recopilan en un único informe y el editor decide: aceptar, revisar o descartar. La actividad Commit into the corpus se sitúa después de esa decisión, en su propio carril, y es el único paso que escribe contenido. Validación mecánica frente a no mecánica . ✎ Edit QA… TR . La compuerta paralela divide la canalización en dos, y esa división es la clave fundamental: . | Validación mecánica —cualquier cosa que una máquina pueda resolver por sí misma, con un veredicto reproducible: reglas de esquema y restricciones de bloque, prefijos de etiquetas, sintaxis, ortografía, resolución de referencias cruzadas y citas, estado de compilación y demostración en Lean, compilación en LaTeX, validación FHIR/SUSHI, ejes de QA. Sin juicios subjetivos, sin negociación; se aprueba o no se aprueba. | Validación no mecánica —todo lo que requiere juicio de valor: ¿es precisa la afirmación?, ¿mantiene la prosa la voz del folio?, ¿expresa el cambio realmente lo que el editor pretendía? Un agente de revisión se encarga de los casos rutinarios; cualquier aspecto que dependa de un criterio clínico o científico se traslada a un revisor humano o experto en la materia (SME). Ambas ramas constituyen la misma etapa de la canalización —el hecho de que el revisor sea una persona o un agente cambia quién responde, no a dónde va la respuesta. | . Ambas ramas deben informar antes de la unión. Una ejecución mecánica en verde no excusa una revisión ausente, y una revisión limpia no excusa una compilación en rojo. Actividades y las habilidades que las implementan . ✎ Edit QA… TR . | Actividad | Carril | Habilidad | . | Describir el cambio previsto | Editor / autor | — (humano) | . | Reclamar o abrir el bean | Plan de trabajo | todo-manager | . | Redactar la edición del bloque | Agente de autoría | content-author | . | Comprobaciones de esquema y restricciones | Validación mecánica | content-validate | . | Sintaxis, ortografía y enlaces | Validación mecánica | content-validate | . | Compuertas de compilación y QA | Validación mecánica | content-test | . | Revisión del cambio por el agente | Validación no mecánica | content-review | . | Revisión humana / por SME | Validación no mecánica | content-review | . | Recopilar los hallazgos en un informe | Canalización de validación de HCI | — (canalización) | . | Registrar los hallazgos en el bean | Plan de trabajo | todo-manager | . | Revisar los hallazgos | Editor / autor | — (humano — esta es la compuerta) | . | Revisar el cambio propuesto | Agente de autoría | content-author | . | Confirmar (commit) en el corpus | Corpus | — (sujeto al requisito commit-hygiene) | . | Resolver o reabrir el bean | Plan de trabajo | todo-manager | . Las comprobaciones específicas del dominio dependen de content-validate / content-test según el tipo de contenido: lean-formalization y proof-verification para artículos científicos, fhir-validation y quality-control para IGs, latex-authoring para renderizado.

651e85a66993.title: Del corpus al folio publicado
651e85a66993.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR KG… . El corpus no es la publicación. A partir de él se compila un borrador, que es revisado en su totalidad por el equipo de revisión, y solo entonces se publica. Abrir la fuente BPMN . Tres aspectos a destacar: . | Un borrador en rojo se corrige en el proceso de edición, no en el artefacto. La rama no de Draft QA green? regresa a través de la actividad de llamada de edición —lo que significa volver a pasar por la compuerta de validación de HCI. Nadie parchea un PDF ya compilado o una IG generada. | La revisión es paralela y ambas partes deben finalizar. El equipo de revisión (revisor de contenido, revisor de QC, oficial técnico) revisa el borrador como publicación; los SME clínicos o científicos dan el visto bueno sobre el contenido de dominio. La unión espera a ambos. | Las solicitudes de cambio se convierten en beans. Un resultado de changes requested no se evapora en un hilo de comentarios de revisión: cada solicitud se abre como un bean propio, de modo que quien retome el trabajo a continuación (humano o agente) vea con exactitud lo que la revisión solicitó. | . | Actividad | Carril | Habilidad | . | Abrir o reclamar el bean de lanzamiento | Plan de trabajo | todo-manager | . | Compilar la publicación en borrador | Corpus + canalización de compilación | content-publish | . | Ejecutar compuertas de QA de la publicación | Corpus + canalización de compilación | content-test · quality-control | . | Edición y validación de HCI | Editores + agentes de autoría | actividad de llamada → diagrama 3 | . | Distribuir el borrador | Responsable de publicación | content-review | . | Revisar la publicación en borrador | Equipo de revisión | content-review | . | Visto bueno clínico / científico | Expertos en la materia (SME) | content-review | . | Abrir beans para las solicitudes de cambio | Plan de trabajo | todo-manager · content-feedback | . | Autorizar el lanzamiento | Responsable del programa | content-publish | . | Versionar, etiquetar y publicar | Responsable de publicación | content-publish · ig-publication | . | Cerrar los beans de lanzamiento | Plan de trabajo | todo-manager | . Este diagrama implementa las compuertas de fase de req:content-lifecycle: validate-before-review, review-before-test, test-before-publish, publish-authorized — consulta skills/requirements/content-lifecycle.json.

52797281c5da.title: Visión general del ciclo de vida del contenido
52797281c5da.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR KG… . Un ciclo de un folio, desde planificar hasta retirar. Ambos diagramas anteriores aparecen aquí como actividades de llamada. Abrir la fuente BPMN . Este es el mismo ciclo de vida que la secuencia lineal planificar → autorizar → validar → revisar → probar → publicar → retroalimentación → retirar, con los actores y los bucles hechos explícitos. Ten en cuenta que Editing and HCI validation se ejecuta una vez por cada cambio propuesto, no una vez por ciclo —la secuencia lineal simplifica eso de forma plana.

59b267b946f0.title: El plan de trabajo — tareas como beans
59b267b946f0.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . Cada diagrama cuenta con un carril de Plan de trabajo, y no es mera decoración. El trabajo de edición se gestiona como beans (hmans/beans) en un directorio beans/ integrado en el repositorio (committed), lo que lo convierte en el único lugar donde un humano y un agente ven la misma respuesta a qué está hecho y qué sigue a continuación. | En qué parte del flujo de trabajo | Qué le ocurre al plan de trabajo | . | Se acuerda el plan | El plan se siembra como beans | . | Comienza una edición | El bean se reclama (--status in-progress) antes de cualquier redacción | . | Informes de validación | Los hallazgos se anexan al bean | . | Se confirma (commit) el cambio | El bean se resuelve —o se deja abierto con lo que aún queda pendiente | . | La revisión solicita cambios | Cada solicitud se abre como su propio bean | . | Se distribuye una versión | El trabajo enviado se cierra; lo que se postergó permanece abierto para el siguiente ciclo | . Por qué está modelado como un carril y no como una nota: . | Es un estado compartido, no el estado de una sesión. beans/ se confirma en el repositorio, por lo que el plan sobrevive a una sesión reanudada y es visible para agentes hermanos que trabajan en otras ramas. La lista efímera de tareas pendientes en memoria de un agente no lo es. | La reclamación es la forma en que dos trabajadores evitan el mismo elemento. Reclama antes de trabajar y nunca resuelvas el bean de otra persona. | beans create no es idempotente. Comprueba si existe un bean mediante el título exacto antes de crear uno —la protección y el incidente que la motiva se describen en todo-manager. | Los beans no son archivos accesorios (sidecars). Las colas generadas por máquinas (QA *.qa.json, archivos de testimonio, colas de vigilancia) siguen siendo JSON en masa; nunca se convierten en beans. | .

c184b899f684.title: Quién es quién
c184b899f684.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . Los roles en los carriles y la definición de actor a la que se asigna cada uno. Los roles se heredan (viewer → reviewer → author → admin). Lo que un actor puede hacer no es una propiedad de su rol: es una regla ODRL en policies/, y antes de cada tarea el ejecutor BPMN verifica que el actor esté autenticado, sea elegible para el rol del carril, esté autorizado por la política y tenga permitido manipular el contenido (task-authorization, incidencia #1207). Personas . ✎ Edit QA… TR . | En los diagramas | Actor | Autoridad | . | Editor / autor | author | Crea y modifica contenido. Decide aceptar / revisar / descartar en la compuerta de HCI. Hereda reviewer. | . | Revisor | reviewer | Visualiza contenido y añade comentarios de revisión. No puede realizar cambios directos. | . | Revisor humano / SME (edición) | clinical-sme | Información de referencia del dominio (domain ground truth). Resuelve las llamadas a juicio que escala un agente de revisión. | . | Equipo de revisión (borrador) | content-reviewer | Aprobación formal y visto bueno de compuerta de fase —la autoridad de aprobación de un borrador. | . |   | qc-reviewer | Control de calidad (QA) de preparación para la publicación en todas las capas; ejecuta los informes de QA. | . |   | technical-officer | Coordinación del área de programa y revisión de primera pasada. | . | Responsable de publicación | publication-manager | Compila, versiona, etiqueta y despliega. No autoriza el lanzamiento. | . | Responsable del programa | programme-manager | Alcance, equipo, cronograma, gobernanza —y autorización del lanzamiento. | . | Administrador | admin | Acceso administrativo completo: roles, configuraciones, todo el contenido. | . Roles de autoría de dominio que aparecen dentro de content-author en lugar de como su propio carril: business-analyst (DAK L2), fhir-modeller (FHIR L3), terminologist (sistemas de códigos y conjuntos de valores), translator (localización). Agentes y actores del sistema . ✎ Edit QA… TR . | En los diagramas | Actor | Qué hace —y qué no puede hacer | . | Agente de autoría | authoring-agent | Redacta y revisa un cambio propuesto. Posee content-authoring; no realiza confirmaciones (commit) —su resultado va al editor a través de la compuerta de validación. | . | Agente de revisión | review-agent | Validación no mecánica: precisión, voz, exposición. Solo dispone de review-comments —informa de hallazgos, no aprueba. | . | Validación mecánica | lean-mcp | Comprobación de demostraciones y diagnósticos en Lean 4 mediante MCP. | . |   | ig-publisher-service | Compilación mediante FHIR IG Publisher e informes de QA. | . La distinción que imponen los diagramas: un agente puede proponer y puede informar, pero la aprobación y la confirmación en el corpus corresponden a una persona. El hallazgo de un agente de revisión y el hallazgo de un SME llegan al mismo punto de la canalización —pero ninguno de ellos decide; lo hace el editor, y el lanzamiento es autorizado por el responsable del programa. Para consultar la lista completa de roles, sus capacidades y cómo se asigna un usuario a un rol, consulta Habilidades y roles.

cece35187ea3.title: Modificación de estos diagramas
cece35187ea3.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . Los archivos .bpmn son la fuente de verdad. # 1. editar processes/<diagrama>.bpmn — en un modelador o a mano # 2. regenerar los SVGs bun run cat render:bpmn # 3. o, en CI, solo comprobar que no estén desfasados bun run cat render:bpmn:check . render:bpmn renderiza cada archivo .bpmn con bpmn-js en Chromium headless y escribe docs/assets/img/workflows/<diagrama>.svg. Si el entorno sandbox incorpora un Chromium que no coincide con la versión fijada de Playwright, apunta hacia él con CHROMIUM_PATH=/path/to/chrome. Cuando añadas una actividad, incluye su extensión <bootstrap.processes:skill ref="…"/> (y <cat-harness.processes:bean store="beans/"/> si afecta al plan de trabajo) y la fila correspondiente en las tablas anteriores —que el diagrama y la lista de habilidades se desincronicen es el fallo que esta página existe para prevenir. Qué diagramas son BPMN y cuáles no . ✎ Edit QA… TR . Cada proceso en la documentación es BPMN. Los diagramas que permanecen como Mermaid no son procesos, y BPMN sería la notación equivocada para ellos —un grupo con carriles implica actores que realizan actividades a lo largo del tiempo, algo que ninguno de estos tiene: . | Diagrama | Notación | Por qué | . | README.md, inicio — “Qué hace” | Mermaid | Mapa de componentes / flujo de datos de la plataforma, no una secuencia de actividades | . | Arquitectura — servidor y adaptadores | Mermaid | Estructura de despliegue y módulos | . | Habilidades y roles — cómo se componen los cinco conceptos | Mermaid | Composición conceptual, sin eje temporal | . | Habilidades y roles — viewer → reviewer → author → admin | Mermaid | Una estructura reticular de herencia, no un flujo | . | Inicio — mapa de documentación | Mermaid | Grafo de navegación | . | Añadir un tipo de contenido — “Lo que proporcionas” | Mermaid | Lo que entregas, no lo que haces | . | Redacción de un artículo — la sesión de Lean | Mermaid sequenceDiagram | Una transcripción de interacción entre tú, el asistente y el servidor MCP. El equivalente en BPMN —una colaboración con flujos de mensajes— añadiría complejidad ceremonial sin aportar significado | . Si añades un diagrama que sí tiene actores, actividades y un flujo de control, pertenece a processes/ como BPMN, no dentro de un bloque de Mermaid.

a9091c0aeae1.title: 仓库中的每个工作流
a9091c0aeae1.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . 这里有多少个 BPMN 2.0 文件？本页面已不再给出数字，而这是解决之道，绝非避而不谈。 . 曾经作为此处开篇的那句话包含一个计数，并且接连错了五次——“六个”，接着是“十九个”，然后是“三十个”，再接着是“三十二个，全部位于 processes/ 下”，随后又是“三十九个”——每一次错误都持续了相当长时间，且每次都是由碰巧运行了 ls 的人发现的。最后一次在最终核对时差了十六个：它声称有三十九个，而实际有五十五个。 . 正文里的计数只是断言；派生的索引才是证据。因此，具体的数量保存在派生流程索引中，该索引由 bun run cat auto:docs 根据声明生成，受 CI 门禁把关，绝不会与其统计的图表发生偏差。本页面的任务则是负责无法自动生成的那一半——每个流程的用途是什么、何时会进入该流程，以及你真正需要的是哪一个相邻流程。 . 这种划分正是 auto-docs 技能的规则，而本页面就是其具体范例：索引说明了存在什么以及每个图表自身声明了什么；下文的一切则阐述了索引在结构上无法表达的内容。 . Bootstrap 的图表是有意排除在该索引之外的，它们的不存在是一个客观事实而非遗漏。bootstrap/workflows/ 由 bootstrap/bootstrap.json 声明，而非由根目录声明，因为若在根目录声明，就会将 bootstrap 的流程重新带入根目录发布的图中——#432 特意移除了这一点，并且仍有测试对此予以保护。Bean pve3 记录了这一抉择：bootstrap 的两半要么全要，要么全不要。 因此，派生索引涵盖根目录所声明的内容，而三个 bootstrap 图表则列在下表中。 . 每个图表都是带有图表交换格式的真实 BPMN 2.0 文档——可在 bpmn.io、Camunda Modeler 或任何 BPMN 工具中打开它。整个文档中的 SVG 均由 bun run cat render:bpmn 从这些文件生成；切勿手动编辑 SVG。 . 在其余所有流程之前——一个人最先接触的流程，也是在尚无 folio 时唯一运行的流程。 . 在 2026-09-20 之前，此表曾列出 bootstrap/workflows/bootstrap.bpmn——一个根本不存在的文件，早在很久以前就已重命名为 initialize-harness.bpmn——而三个真实的图表却全未列出。一个悬空引用隐藏在一个没有任何工具扫描的目录后面，而这正是未索引检查本应捕获却未能捕获的，因为它同样看不到该目录（bean 7u3g）。 . 现在这些行均已修正。这些图表对工具链而言仍是不可见的，在做出决定之前有意保持如此：bootstrap/workflows/ 由 bootstrap/bootstrap.json 声明，但未由根目录声明，在根目录声明会将 bootstrap 的流程重新带入根目录发布的图中——#432 特意移除了这一点，并且仍有测试予以防护。Bean pve3 记录了这一抉择：bootstrap 的两半要么全要，要么全不要。 . | 图表 | 解答的问题 | . | bootstrap/workflows/bootstrap.bpmn | 智能体被指向一个仓库，此时一无所知。这是否已经是一个实例——加载它——还是并非实例，此时它应该变成什么？唯一的输入是一个实例引用；harness 类型、知识图谱与表达风格均从该实例的声明中读取。参见 bootstrap/README.md 和提案 | . | bootstrap/workflows/initialize-harness.bpmn | 智能体被指向一个仓库，此时一无所知。bootstrap 中唯一由参与者启动（STARTS）的流程——阅读了 bootstrap/README.md 的引导智能体处于其启动事件处，没有其他起点。包含三条泳道：引导智能体、请求者和知识图谱数据存储。参见 bootstrap/README.md 和提案 | . | bootstrap/workflows/discussion.bpmn | 有两个事实在引导智能体可访问的任何文件中都找不到答案——该仓库应成为哪个 harness，以及从哪些仓库读取和向哪些仓库写入。它们是提出 harness 需求的人所持有的判断，因此任何指令主体都无法生成它们。当需要此类事实时，从 initialize-harness 内部进入，这也是 bootstrap 拥有第二个流程的原因：它是被每项任务所预设的，而非由某项任务明确指示 | . | bootstrap/workflows/log-message.bpmn | 一个子流程，绝非入口点——通过调用活动到达，从不由外部启动，这就是为什么 bootstrap 的 README 仍然可以说只有一个流程由你开始。可从任何任务中可选调用（参与者记录自己在做什么无需权限），或者由明确绘制该调用的图表强制要求；无论哪种方式都是同一个子流程，区别在于调用者是否显式绘制了它。它驻留在 bootstrap 而非 harness 中，因为 bootstrap 不能导入 harness，如果在上游定义日志记录器，那么最需要说明自己在做什么的参与者反而无法使用它 | . | getting-started.bpmn | 有人提出了“创建一个 folio”。他们指的是五件事中的哪一件，在写入任何内容之前必须满足什么条件？ | . QC clean? 和 FHIR valid? 同样是机械化的且同样值得拥有决策表——它们正在等待 WHO/FHIR 适配器，因为基于没有任何工具发射的事实建立的表格看似权威，实则不然。 . 基础流程是严格的 . ✎ Edit QA… TR . 三个与内容无关的图表——编辑、草稿到发布、生命周期——带有 <cat-harness.processes:policy enforcement="strict"/>。workflow_gate 会拒绝它们尚未到达的步骤。三个针对特定内容类型的图表则是建议性的（advisory），因为对 Lean 证明和 FHIR profile 而言，何为充分审阅是不同的问题，应该由了解该领域的软件包来解答。 . 内容包可以通过在 skills/<package>/workflow-policy.json 中进行声明并附带理由来放宽基础步骤——未作解释的放宽将无法加载，因此该文件记录了豁免了什么以及原因。有五个步骤根本不允许被放宽：Task_ReviewFindings、Gateway_EditorDecision 和 Task_Commit（编辑查看发现项、决策、写入），加上 Task_AuthorizeRelease 和 Task_PublishRelease（publish-authorized 必须满足的 SHALL 规则）。如果这些也可以商量，那么基础流程就不是严格的，而成了仅供参考的建议。 . bun run cat check:workflow-policy 列出策略并验证每一项放宽；它在 CI 中运行，因此不再适用的放宽会导致构建失败，而不是在需要它的当天才被发现。 . 提交边界是强制执行而非仅仅可供查询的地方。 在 folio 仓库中通过预提交钩子或 CI 运行的 scripts/check-corpus-gate.ts，会拒绝没有任何实例记录编辑已授权的已修改内容块。workflow_gate 回答发起询问的智能体；而钩子则不依赖于任何人发起询问。 . bun run <platform>/scripts/check-corpus-gate.ts --staged --platform <platform> bun run <platform>/scripts/check-corpus-gate.ts --staged --warn # adopt gradually . 如何阅读它们 . ✎ Edit QA… TR . | 泳道即角色。 每条泳道映射到 .claude/skills/actors/ 中的一个参与者——参见角色对照表。 | 活动下方的 [skill-name] 是实现该活动的 folio-assistant 技能。该引用同样以机器可读的形式作为 BPMN 活动上的 <bootstrap.processes:skill ref="…"/> 扩展元素承载。 | “Work plan — beans”（工作计划 — beans）泳道是共享的待办存储。该泳道中的步骤读取和写入 beans/，在源码中标记为 <cat-harness.processes:bean store="beans/"/>。 | 粗边框的框是调用活动——它展开为本页面上的另一个图表。 | .

eb6566614e79.title: 编辑与 HCI 验证门禁
eb6566614e79.content: ✎ Edit KG… . 这是日常工作中最关键的图表：针对单个内容块的单次提议变更。 . 打开 BPMN 源码 . 该图表旨在声明的一条核心规则 . ✎ Edit QA… TR . 在编辑看到发现项之前，任何内容都不能进入语料库。 创作智能体生成的是提议的变更，而非提交。该提议在 HCI 验证流水线中展开，结果汇总为一份报告，编辑做出决定——接受、修改还是放弃。Commit into the corpus（提交至语料库）活动位于该决定之后，处于其独立的泳道中，并且是唯一写入内容的步骤。 . 机械验证与非机械验证 . ✎ Edit QA… TR . 并行网关将流水线一分为二，这种划分正是其核心要旨： . | 机械验证——机器能够自行解决的任何事项，具有可重复的判定结果：块模式与约束规则、标签前缀、语法、拼写、交叉引用与引证解析、Lean 构建与证明状态、LaTeX 编译、FHIR/SUSHI 验证、QA 维度。无需主观裁决，无需协商；要么通过，要么不通过。 | 非机械验证——需要主观裁决的一切事项：论断是否准确、正文是否保持了 folio 的表达风格、变更是否真正表达了编辑的本意。审阅智能体处理常规情况；任何取决于临床或科学判断的事项都会升级至人类审阅者或 SME。这两个分支属于流水线的同一阶段——审阅者是人还是智能体，改变的是由谁来回答，而不是答案提交到哪里。 | . 两个分支都必须在汇聚之前进行报告。绿色的机械运行不能成为缺少审阅的借口，干净的审阅也不能成为构建失败的理由。 . 活动及其实现的技能 . ✎ Edit QA… TR . | 活动 | 泳道 | 技能 | . | Describe the intended change（描述预期的变更） | 编辑 / 作者 | —（人工） | . | Claim or open the bean（认领或创建 bean） | 工作计划 | todo-manager | . | Draft the block edit（起草块编辑） | 创作智能体 | content-author | . | Schema and constraint checks（模式与约束检查） | 机械验证 | content-validate | . | Syntax, spelling and links（语法、拼写与链接） | 机械验证 | content-validate | . | Build and QA gates（构建与 QA 门禁） | 机械验证 | content-test | . | Agent review of the change（变更的智能体审阅） | 非机械验证 | content-review | . | Human / SME review（人工 / SME 审阅） | 非机械验证 | content-review | . | Collate findings into a report（将发现项汇总为报告） | HCI 验证流水线 | —（流水线） | . | Log findings on the bean（在 bean 上记录发现项） | 工作计划 | todo-manager | . | Review the findings（审阅发现项） | 编辑 / 作者 | —（人工——这是门禁） | . | Revise the proposed change（修改提议的变更） | 创作智能体 | content-author | . | Commit into the corpus（提交至语料库） | 语料库 | —（遵循 commit-hygiene 要求） | . | Resolve or re-open the bean（解决或重新打开 bean） | 工作计划 | todo-manager | . 特定领域的检查按内容类型挂载在 content-validate / content-test 之下： 针对论文的 lean-formalization 与 proof-verification， 针对 IG 的 fhir-validation 与 quality-control， 针对渲染的 latex-authoring。 .

b07fea3b3400.title: 从语料库到发布的 folio
b07fea3b3400.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR KG… . 语料库并不是发布产物。从语料库构建出草稿，由审阅团队进行整体审阅，只有审阅通过后才会正式发布。 . 打开 BPMN 源码 . 需要注意的三点： . | 未通过的草稿在编辑流程中修复，而不是在制品中直接修补。 从 Draft QA green? 引出的 no 分支会返回到编辑调用活动——这意味着重新经过 HCI 验证门禁。没有人会直接给构建出的 PDF 或生成的 IG 打补丁。 | 审阅是并行的，且两部分都必须完成。 审阅团队（内容审阅者、QC 审阅者、技术官员）将草稿作为发布物进行审阅；临床或科学 SME 对领域内容进行签批。汇聚点等待两者的结果。 | 变更请求转化为 bean。 changes requested（请求变更）的结果不会消失在审阅会话线索中——每个请求都会作为独立的 bean 打开，以便接手该项工作的下一位人员（人类或智能体）能够确切看到审阅所要求的内容。 | . | 活动 | 泳道 | 技能 | . | Open or claim the release bean（创建或认领发布 bean） | 工作计划 | todo-manager | . | Build the draft publication（构建草稿发布物） | 语料库 + 构建流水线 | content-publish | . | Run publication QA gates（运行发布 QA 门禁） | 语料库 + 构建流水线 | content-test · quality-control | . | Editing and HCI validation（编辑与 HCI 验证） | 编辑 + 创作智能体 | 调用活动 → 图表 3 | . | Circulate the draft（传阅草稿） | 发布经理 | content-review | . | Review the draft publication（审阅草稿发布物） | 审阅团队 | content-review | . | Clinical / scientific sign-off（临床 / 科学签批） | SME | content-review | . | Open beans for the change requests（为变更请求创建 bean） | 工作计划 | todo-manager · content-feedback | . | Authorise the release（授权发布） | 项目经理 | content-publish | . | Version, tag and publish（确定版本、打标签并发布） | 发布经理 | content-publish · ig-publication | . | Close the release beans（关闭发布 bean） | 工作计划 | todo-manager | . 该图表实现了 req:content-lifecycle 阶段门禁——validate-before-review、review-before-test、test-before-publish、publish-authorized——参见 skills/requirements/content-lifecycle.json。 .

49f72f34adb5.title: 内容生命周期概览
49f72f34adb5.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR KG… . folio 的一个完整周期，从规划到退役。上述两个图表在此处均作为调用活动出现。 . 打开 BPMN 源码 . 这与线性的规划 → 撰写 → 验证 → 审阅 → 测试 → 发布 → 反馈 → 归档退役链条属于相同的生命周期，并明确指明了参与者与循环回路。请注意，Editing and HCI validation（编辑与 HCI 验证）是针对每次提议的变更运行一次，而不是每个周期运行一次——线性链条将此细节扁平化了。 .

90413343163d.title: 工作计划——任务即 bean
90413343163d.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . 每个图表都包含一条工作计划泳道，它绝非摆设。编辑工作作为 bean（hmans/beans）在已提交版本控制的 beans/ 目录中进行跟踪，这使得它成为人类与智能体对已完成什么、接下来做什么看到相同答案的唯一场所。 . | 工作流中的位置 | 工作计划发生的操作 | . | 方案达成一致 | 方案以 bean 的形式提供初始数据 | . | 编辑开始 | 在进行任何起草之前，先认领 bean（--status in-progress） | . | 验证报告出具 | 将发现项追加到 bean 中 | . | 变更被提交 | bean 被解决——或者保留未完成事项继续保持打开状态 | . | 审阅请求变更 | 每个请求作为独立的 bean 打开 | . | 版本发布交付 | 已交付的工作被关闭；延期的工作保持打开状态进入下一个周期 | . 为何将其建模为泳道而非注释： . | 它是共享状态，而非会话状态。 beans/ 已提交至版本控制，因此工作计划在恢复会话后依然存在，并且对在其他分支上工作的同胞智能体可见。智能体内存中短暂的待办清单则做不到这一点。 | 认领是两个工作者避免领取同一事项的方式。 工作前先认领，绝不解决属于他人的 bean。 | beans create 不是幂等的。 在创建 bean 之前，先按完全匹配的标题检查是否存在已有 bean——该防护措施及其诱发的事故记录在 todo-manager 中。 | Beans 不是 sidecar。 机器生成的队列（QA *.qa.json、见证文件、监视器队列）保持为批量 JSON；它们绝不会转变为 bean。 | .

74c1aaabba95.title: 角色对照表
74c1aaabba95.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . 泳道中的角色，以及各自映射到的参与者定义。角色具有继承性（viewer → reviewer → author → admin）。参与者可以做什么并非其角色的属性：它是 policies/ 中的 ODRL 规则，在每个任务执行之前，BPMN 执行器都会检查参与者是否已通过身份验证、是否具备泳道角色的资格、是否获得策略许可，以及是否允许接触该内容（task-authorization，issue #1207）。 . 人员 . ✎ Edit QA… TR . | 在图表中 | 参与者 | 权限 | . | Editor / author（编辑 / 作者） | author | 创建和修改内容。在 HCI 门禁处决定接受 / 修改 / 放弃。继承 reviewer。 | . | Reviewer（审阅者） | reviewer | 查看内容并留下审阅意见。不能直接进行更改。 | . | Human / SME reviewer（编辑阶段的人工 / SME 审阅者） | clinical-sme | 领域的最终真实依据。解答审阅智能体升级上报的主观裁决问题。 | . | Review team（草稿阶段的审阅团队） | content-reviewer | 正式批准与阶段门禁签批——草稿的批准授权机构。 | . |   | qc-reviewer | 跨层级的发布就绪度 QA；运行 QA 报告。 | . |   | technical-officer | 项目领域协调与初审。 | . | Publication manager（发布经理） | publication-manager | 构建、确定版本、打标签、部署。不负责授权发布。 | . | Programme manager（项目经理） | programme-manager | 范围、团队、时间线、治理——以及发布授权。 | . | Admin（管理员） | admin | 完全管理权限：角色、设置、全部内容。 | . 出现在 content-author 内部而非作为独立泳道的领域创作角色：business-analyst（L2 DAK）、fhir-modeller（L3 FHIR）、terminologist（代码系统与值集）、translator（本地化）。 . 智能体与系统参与者 . ✎ Edit QA… TR . | 在图表中 | 参与者 | 能做什么——以及不能做什么 | . | Authoring agent（创作智能体） | authoring-agent | 起草和修改提议的变更。拥有 content-authoring 权限；不执行提交——其产出通过验证门禁递交给编辑。 | . | Review agent（审阅智能体） | review-agent | 非机械验证：准确性、表达风格、阐述。仅具有 review-comments 权限——它汇报发现项，不作批准。 | . | Mechanical validation（机械验证） | lean-mcp | 通过 MCP 进行 Lean 4 证明检查与诊断。 | . |   | ig-publisher-service | FHIR IG Publisher 构建与 QA 报告生成。 | . 图表所强制执行的区别在于：智能体可以提议和汇报，但批准与提交是人类的职责。 审阅智能体的发现项与 SME 的发现项到达流水线中的同一位置——但两者都不作决策；编辑做出决策，发布由项目经理授权。 . 有关完整的角色列表、各自的能力以及用户如何映射到角色，请参阅技能与角色。 .

cd475e06a9ca.title: 修改这些图表
cd475e06a9ca.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR .bpmn 文件是唯一样本来源。 . # 1. 编辑 processes/<diagram>.bpmn — 在建模器中或手动编辑 # 2. 重新生成 SVG bun run cat render:bpmn # 3. 或者，在 CI 中仅检查它们是否过时 bun run cat render:bpmn:check . render:bpmn 在无头 Chromium 中使用 bpmn-js 渲染每个 .bpmn，并写入 docs/assets/img/workflows/<diagram>.svg。如果沙箱提供的 Chromium 与锁定的 Playwright 构建不匹配，请通过 CHROMIUM_PATH=/path/to/chrome 指定路径。 . 当你添加一项活动时，请添加其 <bootstrap.processes:skill ref="…"/> 扩展（如果涉及工作计划，还需添加 <cat-harness.processes:bean store="beans/"/>），并在上表中添加相应的行——图表与技能列表相互脱节，正是本页面旨在防止的失效模式。 . 哪些图表是 BPMN，哪些不是 . ✎ Edit QA… TR . 文档中的每个流程都是 BPMN。仍保留为 Mermaid 的图表不是流程，BPMN 对它们而言并不是合适的记号法——带有泳道的池意味着参与者随着时间推移执行活动，而这些图表都不具备这一特征： . | 图表 | 记号法 | 原因 | . | README.md, 首页 — “功能介绍” | Mermaid | 平台的组件 / 数据流图，而非活动序列 | . | 架构 — 服务器与适配器 | Mermaid | 部署与模块结构 | . | 技能与角色 — 五个概念如何组合 | Mermaid | 概念组合，无时间轴 | . | 技能与角色 — viewer → reviewer → author → admin | Mermaid | 继承格结构，而非控制流 | . | 首页 — 文档导航图 | Mermaid | 导航关系图 | . | 添加内容类型 — “你需要提供的内容” | Mermaid | 你交付的内容，而非你所执行的操作 | . | 撰写论文 — Lean 会话 | Mermaid sequenceDiagram | 你、助手与 MCP 服务器之间的交互记录。BPMN 的对应物——带有消息流的协作图——只会增加繁琐的形式而不会增加任何实质含义 | . 如果你添加的图表确实包含参与者、活动和控制流，它就应该作为 BPMN 存放在 processes/ 中，而不是放在 Mermaid 代码块中。 .

6c3fdb824b0b.title: Every workflow in the repo
6c3fdb824b0b.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Every process here is a real BPMN 2.0 document with diagram interchange — open it in bpmn.io, Camunda Modeler, or any BPMN tool. The SVGs are generated from those files by bun run cat render:bpmn; never hand-edit an SVG. The table below is not written on this page. It is read from the published knowledge graph — the named-subgraph JSON-LD that bun run cat subgraph:jsonld frames from kg-export — by walking each layer’s processes subgraph. Each row’s text is the first sentence of that diagram’s own bpmn:documentation, carried on its Process node as summary. To change what a row says, change the diagram. The derived process index lists this layer’s corpus of diagrams with their lanes and skills. Bootstrap’s diagrams are in the table, read from bootstrap’s own graph. bootstrap and bootstrap-tools sit below this layer and publish their own named subgraphs at their own sites; the repository index here links each with seeAlso, and the table follows those links. If that site cannot be read, the page says so beside the table rather than drawing a shorter one. Which of two neighbouring processes you are in: . | Before anything else. initialize-harness is the one bootstrap process an actor starts; every other bootstrap diagram is a sub-process reached from it. Once a harness exists, getting-started is where a request to “create a folio” begins. | Content-agnostic, nested. content-lifecycle is one cycle of a folio; it calls draft-to-publication, which calls editing-hci-validation for one proposed change to one block. The content-type processes — authoring-a-document, authoring-a-paper, l2-dak-authoring, l3-fhir-pipeline — describe how that change is drafted for a given kind of folio. | Content or platform. content-change-review takes a change to a folio’s content; code-change-review takes a change to the platform, and calls merge-base to bring the base branch in. | Review. review-task is the generic entry. It descends into review-narrative, review-code or narrative-code-review as separate processes rather than as extra skills on one reviewer, because a called process’s lane is scoped to that call path. | A disagreement. criterion-adjudication is for two reviewer entries on one QA criterion; every other judgement that no mechanism can settle goes to adjudication. | Remote content. materialize-remote decides whether a local copy may be held; refresh-materialized keeps one current; copy-out-materialized is how somebody edits content held as a read-only copy; sample-import and subscribe-kg call the first two rather than restating them. | Upstream releases. upstream-pin-watch notices a pinned dependency has fallen behind; upstream-version-adoption is the reusable sub-process that decides whether to take the release. | Translation. translation-workflow is the machine half; human-translation-workflow is the same cycle with a human translator and a subject-matter reviewer in it. | CI workflows. A .github/workflows/*.yml names the diagram it implements with a # bpmn: line, and each job names its node with # bpmn-node:; bun run cat check:workflow-coverage compares the two. | . The process table is drawn by JavaScript from the published named-subgraph JSON-LD, which can be read directly: each layer's processes/index.hydrated.jsonld holds every one of its processes. The same diagrams are listed, without scripts, in the derived process index, apart from bootstrap's, which are in its own processes/ directory. They also run . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . These files are not only pictures. The MCP server interprets them: workflow_start opens an instance for a subject, workflow_next reports what is enabled now — with the lane that performs it and the skill that implements it — and workflow_complete refuses a step the process has not reached. Commit into the corpus cannot be reported done before the editor’s decision is recorded, because there is no token on it until then. That is ordering, not enforcement: nothing stops an agent calling a capability tool directly. Enforcement is at the commit boundary (see below). Some decisions are computed, not judged . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Exclusive gateways do not all ask the same kind of question. Accept, revise or discard? is the editor’s call. Build green, no sorries? is arithmetic over lean_build and proof_status. A gateway carrying <cat-harness.processes:decision ref="decisions/x.dmn#Decision_Id"/> has its outcome computed from a DMN decision table under a decisions/ directory beside the diagram (here, processes/content/decisions/). The agent supplies facts — { failCritical: 0, failMajor: 2 } — and the table returns the branch; workflow_complete refuses a hand-supplied outcome there, and records which rule fired. | Gateway | Table | Reads | . | Build green, no sorries? | lean-build-gate.dmn | buildOk, deferredSorries | . | Draft QA green? | draft-qa-gate.dmn | failCritical, failMajor | . QC clean? and FHIR valid? are equally mechanical but have no table yet: no tool emits the facts one would read. The base processes are strict . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The three content-agnostic diagrams — editing, draft-to-publication, lifecycle — carry <cat-harness.processes:policy enforcement="strict"/>. workflow_gate refuses a step they have not reached. The three per-content-type diagrams are advisory, because what counts as adequate review of a Lean proof and of a FHIR profile are different questions, and the package that knows the domain should answer them. A content package may relax a base step by declaring it in skills/<package>/workflow-policy.json with a reason — an unexplained relaxation does not load. Five steps refuse to be relaxed at all: Task_ReviewFindings, Gateway_EditorDecision and Task_Commit (the editor seeing the findings, the decision, the write), plus Task_AuthorizeRelease and Task_PublishRelease (the publish-authorized SHALL). bun run cat check:workflow-policy lists the policy and validates every relaxation; it runs in CI. The commit boundary is where this is enforced. scripts/check-corpus-gate.ts, run in the folio repo from a pre-commit hook or CI, refuses a changed content block that no instance records the editor having authorised. workflow_gate answers an agent that asks; the hook does not depend on anyone asking. bun run <platform>/scripts/check-corpus-gate.ts --staged --platform <platform> bun run <platform>/scripts/check-corpus-gate.ts --staged --warn # adopt gradually . How to read them . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | A lane is a role. Every lane maps to an actor in cat-harness/scenarios/actors/ — see Who is who. | [skill-name] under an activity is the folio-assistant skill that implements it. The same reference is carried machine-readably as a <bootstrap.processes:skill ref="…"/> extension element on the BPMN activity. | The “Work plan — beans” lane is the shared to-do store. Steps in that lane read and write beans/, and are marked <cat-harness.processes:bean store="beans/"/> in the source. | A thick-bordered box is a call activity — it expands into another diagram on this page. | .

9f72994e6f13.title: Editing and the HCI validation gate
9f72994e6f13.content: ✎ Edit KG… . This is the diagram that matters most day to day: one proposed change to one content block. Open the BPMN source . The one rule this diagram exists to state . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Nothing reaches the corpus before the editor has seen the findings. The authoring agent produces a proposed change, not a commit. That proposal fans out through the HCI validation pipeline, the results are collated into one report, and the editor decides — accept, revise, or discard. The Commit into the corpus activity sits after that decision, in its own lane, and is the only step that writes content. Mechanical vs non-mechanical validation . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The parallel gateway splits the pipeline in two, and the split is the point: . | Mechanical validation — anything a machine can settle on its own, with a reproducible verdict: block schema and constraint rules, label prefixes, syntax, spelling, cross-references and citation resolution, Lean build and proof status, LaTeX compilation, FHIR/SUSHI validation, QA axes. No judgement, no negotiation; it passes or it does not. | Non-mechanical validation — everything that needs judgement: is the claim accurate, does the prose keep the folio’s voice, does the change actually say what the editor meant. A review agent handles the routine cases; anything turning on clinical or scientific judgement escalates to a human reviewer or SME. Both branches are the same stage of the pipeline — the reviewer being a person or an agent changes who answers, not where the answer goes. | . Both branches must report before the join. A green mechanical run does not excuse a missing review, and a clean review does not excuse a red build. Activities and the skills that implement them . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Activity | Lane | Skill | . | Describe the intended change | Editor / author | — (human) | . | Claim or open the bean | Work plan | todo-manager | . | Draft the block edit | Authoring agent | content-author | . | Schema and constraint checks | Mechanical validation | content-validate | . | Syntax, spelling and links | Mechanical validation | content-validate | . | Build and QA gates | Mechanical validation | content-test | . | Agent review of the change | Non-mechanical validation | content-review | . | Human / SME review | Non-mechanical validation | content-review | . | Collate findings into a report | HCI validation pipeline | — (pipeline) | . | Log findings on the bean | Work plan | todo-manager | . | Review the findings | Editor / author | — (human — this is the gate) | . | Revise the proposed change | Authoring agent | content-author | . | Commit into the corpus | Corpus | — (subject to the commit-hygiene requirement) | . | Resolve or re-open the bean | Work plan | todo-manager | . The domain-specific checks hang off content-validate / content-test by content type: lean-formalization and proof-verification for papers, fhir-validation and quality-control for IGs, latex-authoring for rendering.

21d78daff49d.title: From corpus to published folio
21d78daff49d.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… KG… . The corpus is not the publication. A draft is built from it, reviewed as a whole by the review team, and only then released. Open the BPMN source . Three things to note: . | A red draft is fixed in the editing process, not in the artifact. The no branch off Draft QA green? goes back through the editing call activity — which means back through the HCI validation gate. Nobody patches a built PDF or a generated IG. | Review is parallel, and both halves must land. The review team (content reviewer, QC reviewer, technical officer) reviews the draft as a publication; the clinical or scientific SMEs sign off on the domain content. The join waits for both. | Change requests become beans. Each changes requested item is opened as a bean, so whoever picks the work up next sees exactly what review asked for. | . | Activity | Lane | Skill | . | Open or claim the release bean | Work plan | todo-manager | . | Build the draft publication | Corpus + build pipeline | content-publish | . | Run publication QA gates | Corpus + build pipeline | content-test · quality-control | . | Editing and HCI validation | Editors + authoring agents | call activity → diagram 3 | . | Circulate the draft | Publication manager | content-review | . | Review the draft publication | Review team | content-review | . | Clinical / scientific sign-off | SMEs | content-review | . | Open beans for the change requests | Work plan | todo-manager · content-feedback | . | Authorise the release | Programme manager | content-publish | . | Version, tag and publish | Publication manager | content-publish · ig-publication | . | Close the release beans | Work plan | todo-manager | . This diagram implements the req:content-lifecycle phase gates — validate-before-review, review-before-test, test-before-publish, publish-authorized — see skills/requirements/content-lifecycle.json.

a914373b1200.title: Content lifecycle overview
a914373b1200.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… KG… . One cycle of a folio, plan to retire. Both diagrams above appear here as call activities. Open the BPMN source . This is the same lifecycle as the linear plan → author → validate → review → test → publish → feedback → retire strip, with the actors and the loops made explicit. Note that Editing and HCI validation runs once per proposed change, not once per cycle — the linear strip flattens that.

7c0ab0c8e2a5.title: The work plan — tasks as beans
7c0ab0c8e2a5.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Every diagram has a Work plan lane, and it is not decoration. Editing work is tracked as beans (hmans/beans) in a committed beans/ directory, which makes it the one place where a human and an agent see the same answer to what is done, and what is next. | Where in the workflow | What happens to the work plan | . | Plan is agreed | The plan is seeded as beans | . | An edit starts | The bean is claimed (--status in-progress) before any drafting | . | Validation reports | Findings are appended to the bean | . | The change is committed | The bean is resolved — or left open with what is still outstanding | . | Review requests changes | Each request is opened as its own bean | . | A release ships | Shipped work is closed; what slipped stays open into the next cycle | . Why it is modelled as a lane rather than a note: . | It is shared state, not session state. beans/ is committed, so the plan survives a resumed session and is visible to sibling agents working other branches. An agent’s ephemeral in-memory to-do list is not. | Claiming is how two workers avoid the same item. Claim before you work, and never resolve someone else’s bean. | beans create is not idempotent. Check for an existing bean by exact title before creating one; the guard is in todo-manager. | Beans are not sidecars. Machine-generated queues (QA *.qa.json, witness files, watcher queues) stay bulk JSON; they never become beans. | .

04f27dd758d3.title: Who is who
04f27dd758d3.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The roles in the lanes, and the actor definition each one maps to. Roles inherit (viewer → reviewer → author → admin). What an actor may do is not a property of its role: it is an ODRL rule in policies/, and before every task the BPMN executor checks that the actor is authenticated, eligible for the lane’s role, permitted by policy and allowed to touch the content (task-authorization). People . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | In the diagrams | Actor | Authority | . | Editor / author | author | Creates and modifies content. Decides accept / revise / discard at the HCI gate. Inherits reviewer. | . | Reviewer | reviewer | Views content and leaves review comments. Cannot make direct changes. | . | Human / SME reviewer (editing) | clinical-sme | Domain ground truth. Answers the judgement calls a review agent escalates. | . | Review team (draft) | content-reviewer | Formal approval and phase-gate sign-off — the approval authority on a draft. | . |   | qc-reviewer | Publication-readiness QA across layers; runs the QA reports. | . |   | technical-officer | Programme-area coordination and first-pass review. | . | Publication manager | publication-manager | Builds, versions, tags, deploys. Does not authorise the release. | . | Programme manager | programme-manager | Scope, team, timeline, governance — and release authorisation. | . | Admin | admin | Full administrative access: roles, settings, all content. | . Domain-authoring roles that appear inside content-author rather than as their own lane: business-analyst (L2 DAK), fhir-modeller (L3 FHIR), terminologist (code systems and value sets), translator (localisation). Agents and system actors . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | In the diagrams | Actor | What it does — and what it cannot do | . | Authoring agent | authoring-agent | Drafts and revises a proposed change. Has content-authoring; does not commit — its output goes to the editor through the validation gate. | . | Review agent | review-agent | Non-mechanical validation: accuracy, voice, exposition. Has review-comments only — it reports findings, it does not approve. | . | Mechanical validation | lean-mcp | Lean 4 proof checking and diagnostics over MCP. | . |   | ig-publisher-service | FHIR IG Publisher build and QA reporting. | . The distinction the diagrams enforce: an agent can propose and can report, but approval and commit are a person’s. A review agent’s finding and an SME’s finding arrive at the same place in the pipeline — but neither of them decides; the editor does, and the release is authorised by the programme manager. For the full role list, their capabilities, and how a user is mapped to a role, see Skills & roles.

829df6d3e2c3.title: Changing these diagrams
829df6d3e2c3.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The .bpmn files are the source of truth. # 1. edit processes/<area>/<diagram>.bpmn — in a modeler, or by hand # 2. regenerate the SVGs bun run cat render:bpmn # 3. or, in CI, just check they are not stale bun run cat render:bpmn:check . render:bpmn renders each .bpmn with bpmn-js in headless Chromium and writes docs/assets/img/workflows/<diagram>.svg. If the sandbox ships a Chromium that does not match the pinned Playwright build, point at it with CHROMIUM_PATH=/path/to/chrome. When you add an activity, add its <bootstrap.processes:skill ref="…"/> extension (and <cat-harness.processes:bean store="beans/"/> if it touches the work plan) and the matching row in the tables above, so the diagram and the skill list do not drift apart. Which diagrams are BPMN, and which are not . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Every process in the docs is BPMN. The diagrams that remain Mermaid are not processes, and BPMN would be the wrong notation for them — a pool with lanes implies actors performing activities over time, which none of these have: . | Diagram | Notation | Why | . | README.md, home — “What it does” | Mermaid | Component / data-flow map of the platform, not a sequence of activities | . | Architecture — server and adapters | Mermaid | Deployment and module structure | . | Skills & roles — how the five concepts compose | Mermaid | Conceptual composition, no time axis | . | Skills & roles — viewer → reviewer → author → admin | Mermaid | An inheritance lattice, not a flow | . | Home — documentation map | Mermaid | Navigation graph | . | Adding a content type — “What you provide” | Mermaid | What you hand over, not what you do | . | Writing a paper — the Lean session | Mermaid sequenceDiagram | An interaction transcript between you, the assistant and the MCP server. BPMN’s equivalent — a collaboration with message flows — would add ceremony without adding meaning | . If you add a diagram that does have actors, activities and a control flow, it belongs in processes/ as BPMN, not in a Mermaid fence.

c55dbee27844.title: Writing a document with folio-assistant
c55dbee27844.content: TR… . On this page . | What a document folio is | 1 · Scaffold the folio | 2 · The content model . | The kinds you may use | uses[] matters more here than in a paper | . | 3 · Author with the agent . | Carrying a recommendation | . | 4 · Validate | 5 · Render . | Not implemented | . | Moving between content types | Where things are | . This page is generated from docs/source/guides-writing-a-document/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Policy guidance, a standard, a report, a handbook — structured prose, authored with an LLM, published without a TeX installation.

bad94a8b2bce.title: What a document folio is
bad94a8b2bce.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… KG… . Everything a paper folio is, minus the formal layer. The same tree of chapters and sections over typed blocks, the same editorial uses[] graph, the same QA sidecars, the same HCI validation gate, the same publication pipeline. What it does not have is the seven block kinds whose assertion is a formal mathematical claim — and therefore neither of the two toolchains that serve them. No Lean. No LaTeX. A paper is a document plus Lean-bearing blocks. PaperContentAdapter extends DocumentContentAdapter in code, and adds the Lean lifecycle and the LaTeX renderer on top, so a feature “the paper adapter has” is usually already here. BPMN 2.0 source .

1f0594d948ef.title: 1 · Scaffold the folio
1f0594d948ef.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . In a new, empty repository: . git init git submodule add https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant.git folio-assistant (cd folio-assistant && bun install) bun run folio-assistant/scripts/init-folio.ts \ --type document \ --title "Cold Chain Guidance" \ --author "A. Author" . Or, if your agent already has a folio-assistant server connected, ask it: . initialize a new document folio here using litlfred/folio-assistant, titled “Cold Chain Guidance”, author A. Author . Either way you get content/, uploads/, library/, the manifests for one document with one chapter and one block, <name>.config.json, the builder shim, AGENTS.md with CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md stubs, .mcp.json, and the beans work plan. See the README quickstart for the full file list. The starter block is a placeholder that says so. Replace it.

d31b41db5d17.title: 2 · The content model
d31b41db5d17.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . content/cold-chain-guidance/ cold-chain-guidance.ts the document manifest — chapters, in reading order introduction/ introduction.ts the chapter manifest — sections, in reading order overview.ts a block manifest: kind, label, title, uses[] overview.md that block's prose overview.qa.json QA sidecar — machine-written, never hand-edited . Three ordered lists hold the whole structure, and a block reaches the output only if some section’s blocks[] names it. A block whose .ts and .md are committed but that no section lists renders nowhere. The kinds you may use . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . prose, example, remark, algorithm, simulator, equation, diagram, table, figure, recommendation. Not definition, theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, conjecture or proof. content_profile_check rejects them, and runs on every content_validate. uses[] matters more here than in a paper . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . uses[] lists the blocks a reader must already have read to follow this one. It is an editorial judgement; nothing derives it. A paper folio has a second, machine-derived dependency graph (from lean.ref); a document folio does not. So uses[] is the only dependency signal, and every ordering metric, every “what else changes if this changes?” question, and the reading-order review read it. List direct neighbours only.

a54440127586.title: 3 · Author with the agent
a54440127586.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Ask in plain language. The agent loads the skills it needs over MCP. add a chapter on cold-chain monitoring . document-structure — creates the directory, writes the chapter manifest, adds the entry to chapters[] in the right position. add a section on temperature excursions, with a recommendation that facilities audit the cold chain quarterly . document-authoring for the section and its blocks; normative-statements for the recommendation. what does the audit recommendation depend on? . Reads uses[] and the content graph. Carrying a recommendation . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . A normative statement is the block readers cite and implementers trace to. It wants a label, a stable identity and a place in the dependency graph. Its carrier is a recommendation block: . export default recommendation({ label: "rec:cold-chain-audit", title: "Audit the cold chain quarterly", strength: { list: "grade-recommendation-strength", code: "conditional" }, uses: ["rec:scope", "prose:cold-chain-terms"], }); . | One statement per block. A block holding three cannot be cited, reviewed, superseded or traced individually. | State the strength as a code in a declared code list: grade-recommendation-strength (strong, conditional) or rfc2119-requirement-level (must, should, may, …), or the folio’s own folio-code-list/v1 when its issuing body grades differently. | Keep the published number out of the label. Numbers change between editions; the label must not. Put the number in the title. | Do not use definition. Its lean field is required, so it will not validate here at all. | . The full convention is in the normative-statements skill.

547361982e78.title: 4 · Validate
547361982e78.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . content_validate schema + constraints + profile conformance content_profile_check profile conformance alone, over the whole folio qa_sweep the QA axes, per block . Profile conformance catches two things schema validation cannot, because a theorem is a valid theorem whatever folio it sits in: . | a block whose kind is outside the declared profile; and | a lean field or a .lean sibling on a kind the profile otherwise allows — remark, example, algorithm and simulator all declare an optional lean, so the type permits what the profile forbids. | . Both name the file and the remedy, including “declare contentType: "paper"” when that is what you actually meant.

1e248183c1d3.title: 5 · Render
1e248183c1d3.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . content/** → document_render_md → build/<slug>.md → document_render_html → build/<slug>.html → document_render_pdf → build/<slug>.pdf . Read the Markdown first. It is the only file with the whole document in reading order. Look for sections that came out empty, blocks in an order that does not read, and the > **Missing block:** marker. HTML needs only pandoc. PDF additionally needs one TeX-free engine — weasyprint (recommended), prince, or wkhtmltopdf: . apt install pandoc pip install weasyprint . If none is installed, document_render_pdf says which are missing and stops. It does not fall back to latexmk, even where TeX is present. Both renderers take a css path relative to the repo root. Keep the stylesheet in the folio, and put the print rules (@page, page breaks, running heads) in the same file as the screen rules, so the two outputs cannot drift. Not implemented . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The pandoc renderers (document_render_*) have no citations, no bibliography, no glossary and no automatic cross-reference numbering: \cite{…} passes through verbatim, so on that path write references as Markdown links or footnotes. The site build (build-document-site.ts) renders \cite{a,b} as [a, b], each key linked to its entry with --bibliography-url, and :defterm / :refterm as a term and its link; it has no cross-reference numbering either. Cross-references do work: every labelled block emits an HTML anchor, so [see the scope statement](#rec:scope) resolves in both HTML and PDF. Use the block’s label, never a heading-derived anchor, which changes whenever the title is edited.

90c7e11dfab6.title: Moving between content types
90c7e11dfab6.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . <name>.config.json’s contentType is the switch. document → paper is a one-line change. You are adding toolchains, not removing content. paper → document additionally means removing every math block and every lean field. Run content_profile_check after flipping the switch and it lists exactly what is in the way.
